# The artist KITAS: performing legally

 The artist KITAS is a work status for people performing in Indonesia for a fee: DJs, musicians, vocalists, dancers and performers. The sponsor is the venue or promoter whose events the status is issued against. Performing for money on a tourist visa risks fines, deportation and the collapse of the whole tour.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Who needs an artist status

 The artist KITAS is a work status for people performing in Indonesia for a fee: DJs, musicians, vocalists, dancers, performers and hosts.

 ✓The sponsor is an Indonesian organiser: a club, a hotel, an events agency, a promoter

 ✓Term and format depend on the contract and the performance schedule

 ✓Income is lawful within the sponsor's contract

 The operative words are for a fee. Playing a set for friends at a birthday and holding a club residency are different things to immigration, and the second requires status.

## Why a tourist visa does not work here

 Performing for money on a visit visa breaches the purpose of your stay outright. In Bali that is not an abstract risk: clubs and festivals are checked regularly.

 !Fines — for the artist and for the venue

 !Deportation with a re-entry ban: what people are deported for

 !A collapsed tour: being pulled from one event usually cancels the rest

 On barter and 'paid in accommodation': the form of the reward is irrelevant. What matters is that a paid performance took place inside the country.

## How it works on the organiser's side

 The filing comes not from the artist but from the venue: it submits the documents and carries the obligations.

 The contractOrganiser and artist fix the dates, venues and fee.

 Venue permitsThe organiser prepares its part of the pack as the host.

 Visa and entryThe artist enters on the visa arranged for that contract, not on a tourist one.

 Status on arrivalAfter landing the stay permit is issued, with biometrics.

We work with both sides and handle the organiser's pack in full — for venues that is usually the bottleneck.

## What to plan in advance

 ✓Dates. The status is tied to the contract: adding a venue mid-tour means checking whether it is covered

 ✓Equipment. Bringing gear in is a customs question, not an immigration one

 ✓Several countries on one tour. Each entry into Indonesia counts separately

 ✓Passport. Validity requirements are covered separately

## What it gives the venue

 Organisers sometimes see the paperwork as a cost. In practice it is insurance against far larger losses.

 ✓A check during the event does not turn into the show being stopped

 ✓No fines for the venue and no risk to its licences

 ✓The artist does not drop out of the schedule for later dates

 ✓Reputation: venues that document their artists find big bookings easier to land

 We handle both halves of the pack — artist and organiser — because separately they do not work: the status is issued against a specific contract with a specific venue.

## A residency versus one-off dates

 The shape of the contract affects the paperwork more than people expect. A single show and a seasonal club residency are different stories in documents and in lead time.

 ✓One-off dates — status against a specific event, prepared ahead for each date

 ✓A residency — a long contract with one venue, and a more predictable process

 ✓A multi-venue tour — the hardest case: one sponsor, many events

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do I need an artist KITAS for a single show?
If the show is paid, yes. The status turns not on the number of gigs but on receiving a fee for performing in Indonesia.

Вопрос: Who arranges it — the artist or the venue?
The venue. The sponsor is the Indonesian organiser: a club, hotel, promoter or events agency. An artist cannot obtain it alone.

Вопрос: What happens if I perform on a tourist visa?
Fines for the artist and the venue, and possible deportation with a re-entry ban. Clubs and festivals in Bali are checked regularly.

Вопрос: Does barter count as a fee?
Yes. Payment in accommodation, tickets or services does not change the substance: it is a paid performance inside the country.

Вопрос: Can a venue be added mid-tour?
It needs checking: the status is issued against a specific contract. Agree new dates and venues before, not after.

## Organisers: we will handle the whole foreign-artist pack

 We arrange the artist status and the venue's permits. Send the dates and line-up and we will assemble both sides.

# China, Korea and Singapore: where a visa is needed

 Three neighbouring destinations from Bali work in three different ways. China admits Russian citizens for 30 days on a passport alone, Korea for 60 but with a K-ETA authorisation. The surprise of the three is Singapore: a visa is required, and only 96-hour onward transit is free.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer for a Russian passport

 Three neighbouring destinations work in completely different ways, and intuition misleads here: the most closed of the three is not the one you would guess.

 ✓China — visa-free for up to 30 days. A valid passport is all you need

 ✓Korea — visa-free for up to 60 days, but the K-ETA electronic authorisation is mandatory

 ✓Singapore — a visa is required. Visa-free entry exists only in transit and only up to 96 hours

 Singapore is what catches people out: it is assumed to be open, because for many passports it is. For a Russian one it is not.

## China: 30 days on a passport alone

 The simplest of the three. Russian citizens may stay up to 30 days presenting only a valid passport at the border.

 ✓The arrangement runs as a pilot scheme — open-ended by nature it is not

 ✓Purposes are limited: tourism, business visits, family visits and transit

 ✓No advance forms, no fees, no consulates

 !Work, study and long stays are not covered — those need a separate visa

 !Pilot status means conditions can change: check before buying tickets

## Korea: visa-free, but not quite

 Formally South Korea is open to Russian passports for up to 60 days. In practice there is a compulsory step in between.

 K-ETAThe electronic travel authorisation is arranged online in advance. Without it you will not board.

 CostAbout KRW 10,000 — a nominal sum.

 Length of stayUp to 60 days, enough for a holiday or a long trip.

A K-ETA is an authorisation rather than a visa, but the consequences are much the same: without it the trip does not happen. Arrange it ahead, not at the airport.

## Singapore: the real trap

 For a Russian passport Singapore is a visa country. Visa-free entry exists but it is transit-only and hedged with conditions.

 ✓Up to 96 hours without a visa when travelling onward to a third country

 ✓Printed flight confirmations are required

 ✓Longer than 96 hours means a tourist visa, with no alternatives

 And here is the detail that catches people: transit means flying onward, not returning to where you came from. The classic Bali–Singapore–Bali pattern is not transit.
If you planned that route as a visa run, check the conditions before buying tickets. Being turned away at check-in costs more than the visa.

## If you do need a Singapore visa

 It is arranged online: applications go through authorised agents or visa centres located in Singapore itself.

 ✓Documents — passport scan, a photo on a white background, accommodation and flight bookings

 ✓Standard processing — 3 to 5 working days

 ✓Expedited — from a few hours to two days

 ✓Cost — roughly USD 60 to 150 depending on the provider and urgency

 What is assessed above all is your intention to return. Residency in Indonesia helps here as it does elsewhere: it explains where your life is.

## Where else you can file from Bali

 ✓Japan — the visa centre is in Denpasar, but a KITAS is required

 ✓Australia — entirely online, no visit anywhere

 ✓United States — an interview in Jakarta or Surabaya

 ✓Schengen — the Bulgarian route for Russian citizens

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do Russian citizens need a visa for China in 2026?
No, for trips up to 30 days for tourism, business, visiting relatives or transit. A valid passport at the border is enough. The arrangement runs as a pilot scheme.

Вопрос: What is K-ETA and is it compulsory?
It is the electronic travel authorisation for South Korea, arranged online in advance for about KRW 10,000. Without it you will not be allowed to board, despite the 60-day visa-free regime.

Вопрос: Is it true that Russians need a visa for Singapore?
Yes. Only transit remains visa-free, up to 96 hours, when travelling onward to a third country with printed tickets. Everything else requires a tourist visa.

Вопрос: Does a Bali–Singapore–Bali trip count as visa-free transit?
No. Transit means continuing to a third country, not returning to your point of departure. Such a trip needs a visa, and that is worth establishing before buying tickets.

Вопрос: How long does a Singapore visa take?
Typically 3 to 5 working days, with expedited processing from a few hours to two days. Filing is online through agents and visa centres in Singapore.

## We will help with the visa and check your route

 Tell us where and when you are flying — we will verify the requirements and gather the documents.

# Australia visa from Bali: entirely online

 Of the three popular destinations this is the simplest: the subclass 600 visitor visa is filed over the internet from anywhere, with no consulate visit. The charge is AUD 200, and half of applications from Indonesia are decided within ten days. Online filing is open to Russian passport holders too.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 Of the three popular destinations this is the easiest. No embassy, no flight to Jakarta: the application is filed over the internet.

 ✓Subclass 600 visa, Tourist and Business streams — the standard visitor route

 ✓Filed entirely online through the government's ImmiAccount portal

 ✓From anywhere with an internet connection — Bali, Jakarta, anywhere

 ✓Online filing is open to Russian passport holders for tourism and business travel

 Not needing to appear in person is no small thing. Schengen and US applications from Bali both mean a flight to Jakarta and at least one night; this one is settled from a laptop.

## Cost and waiting time

 Since 1 July 2026 the visitor visa charge is AUD 200 — the same for the Tourist and Business streams.
Processing times for applicants in Indonesia look better than the global picture:

 ✓Half of Tourist stream applications are decided within 10 days

 ✓Nine out of ten within 29 days

 ✓Global figures as of mid-2026 are more modest: 16–33 days for the Tourist stream and 6–26 for Business

 Plan with margin anyway. These are statistics, not commitments: complex cases go to further checks and fall outside those numbers.

## What to prepare

 The pack is assembled digitally and uploaded to your account.

 ✓Passport with sufficient validity

 ✓Proof of status in Indonesia — a KITAS or KITAP if you live here

 ✓Financial documents — statements showing the trip is affordable

 ✓Travel plan — itinerary, bookings, return ticket

 ✓Evidence of ties to where you live: work, business, housing, family

 The logic matches the US visa: the officer weighs whether you will return. Residency in Indonesia counts in your favour — it explains where your life is and why you are not planning to stay.

## Biometrics and what can follow

 Filing online does not always mean you will be left alone entirely.

 ✓Some applications trigger a biometrics request — then a visit to a collection centre is required

 ✓Additional documents may be requested: proof of income, an employer letter, a medical examination

 ✓The decision arrives by email and the visa is digital — nothing is pasted into your passport

 !Do not buy non-refundable tickets before the decision — that rule holds for all three destinations

 !Do not file a week before departure: even a fast stream guarantees nothing for your particular case

## How it compares

 Set against the other two routes available from Bali, the difference in effort is obvious.

 Destination | 
 How you file | 
 In person | 

 Australia | online, ImmiAccount | not required | 

 United States | online form, then an interview | Jakarta or Surabaya | 

 Schengen | consulate or visa centre | Jakarta | 

The others in detail: the US visa, Schengen via Bulgaria, the Japanese visa in Denpasar and trips to China, Korea and Singapore.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I apply for an Australian visa from Bali?
Yes. The subclass 600 visitor visa is filed online through the ImmiAccount portal from anywhere with an internet connection. No trip to a consulate or to Jakarta is needed.

Вопрос: Is online filing available to Russian citizens?
Yes. The online visitor visa application is open to Russian passport holders travelling for tourism or business.

Since 1 July 2026 the charge is AUD 200, the same for the Tourist and Business streams.

Вопрос: How long does processing take?
For applicants in Indonesia, half of Tourist stream applications are decided within 10 days and nine in ten within 29. Global times run longer, and complex cases go to further checks.

Вопрос: Are biometrics required?
Some applications trigger a request, in which case you attend a collection centre. You cannot know in advance, so build the possibility into your timeline.

# Autogate and All Indonesia: the border in 20 seconds

 The autogate opens on two conditions: a chipped passport and an approved electronic visa. Clearance takes 15–25 seconds and no stamp is placed in your passport. Before departure every traveller completes the free All Indonesia card, available from 72 hours before arrival. Children go through themselves from age six. The Love Bali levy of IDR 150,000 is paid separately.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Two conditions for the autogate

 The automated gates on arrival in Denpasar and Jakarta do not open for everyone. There are exactly two conditions, and both depend on what you do before you fly.

 ✓A chipped passport — biometric, with the symbol on the cover

 ✓An approved electronic visa — an e-VOA or other e-visa linked to that passport

 The system reads the chip and matches your face. Immigration reports clearance in 15–25 seconds — instead of a queue for an officer and a stamp in your passport.

## Before departure: the All Indonesia card

 All Indonesia is the single digital arrival card combining the immigration, customs and health forms. It is completed for every traveller, infants included.

 ✓Filed online, available from 72 hours before arrival

 ✓Free of charge

 ✓The QR code arrives by email — save it offline; airport wifi is not to be relied on

 Fill it in at home rather than on the plane: there is no connectivity in the air, and doing it on your phone in the arrivals queue is the worst version of this.

## At the gate: how it goes

 Passport on the scannerOut of its cover, flat against the glass — a cover blocks the chip read.

 Look at the cameraGlasses and hats off, face forward.

 The gates open15–25 seconds and you are in the country.

 No stampYour entry record stays in the system. That is normal and needs no confirmation.

Since August 2026 immigration has been receiving real-time passenger data from airlines, which speeds up border checks further.

## Children and the classic mistake

 Children have their own threshold, and it is where families most often come unstuck.

 ✓Children aged 6 and over use the autogate themselves, subject to the usual requirements

 ✓With a child under 6, one parent goes through a staffed counter

 ✓Every family member's arrival must be registered — infants included

 !The classic mistake: going through the autogate yourselves and leaving the child 'with someone'. Every person crosses the border individually

 !A passport without a chip will not open the gate — go straight to an officer rather than queue for the gates

## What is paid separately

 The autogate and the arrival card are immigration matters. Bali's tourist levy is unrelated and paid separately.

 ✓Love Bali — IDR 150,000 per person, through the province's official portal

 ✓Pay before arrival and keep the QR code

 ✓Details in our Love Bali levy article

 The visa that opens the autogate in the first place is an e-VOA arranged before departure. A visa bought at the airport counter costs you both the payment queue and the gate.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: What do I need to use the autogate?
Two things: a biometric passport with a chip, and an approved electronic visa linked to it. Plus a completed All Indonesia card.

Вопрос: How long does it take?
Immigration reports 15–25 seconds: the system reads the chip and matches your face. No stamp is placed in the passport — the entry record stays in the system.

Вопрос: When do I fill in All Indonesia?
The card opens 72 hours before arrival and is completed free online for every traveller, infants included. The QR code comes by email — save it offline.

Вопрос: From what age can children use the autogate?
From age 6, subject to the usual requirements. With a child under six, one parent goes through a staffed counter.

Вопрос: Does this include the Love Bali levy?
No. Bali's IDR 150,000 tourist levy is paid separately through the provincial portal and is unrelated to immigration procedures.

 An e-VOA all-in for IDR 900,000, in your inbox before departure — and no queue at the border.

# Bali immigration offices 2026: which one is yours

 Bali has five immigration offices: Denpasar, Ngurah Rai, Singaraja, Tabanan and Klungkung. The last two opened on 6 April 2026. You do not get to choose — your application goes to the office whose area covers your address. Filing is online, but one visit for the photo remains mandatory.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The five offices and their areas

 Your office is determined by your residential address, not by which one is easiest to park at. Here is how the island is divided.

 Office | 
 Areas covered | 

 Denpasar | Denpasar, North Badung, Gianyar, Bangli — including Ubud, Sanur, Kintamani | 

 Ngurah Rai | Badung and the airport area — Kuta, Legian, Seminyak, Canggu, Jimbaran, Uluwatu | 

 Singaraja | North, east and west — Buleleng, Karangasem, Jembrana: Lovina, Amed, Gilimanuk | 

 Tabanan | Tabanan regency — including Tabanan town and the Kedungu coast | 

 Klungkung | Klungkung and the islands — Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan, Nusa Ceningan | 

## What changed in April 2026

 On 6 April 2026 two new offices formally opened in Bali — Tabanan and Klungkung. Until then the island was served by three: Denpasar, Ngurah Rai and Singaraja, which meant Tabanan residents travelled to Denpasar and people on Nusa Penida took a ferry to the mainland.
The point is load: the number of foreigners on the island keeps growing, and Ngurah Rai alone carried the whole south. If you live in Tabanan or on the islands, the change is a practical one — your visit just got a lot closer.
Re-check which office is yours. If you extended last year and remember your office, it may have changed: some addresses moved into the new zones.

## Why you cannot pick your own office

 An extension application goes to the office whose working area covers the foreigner's place of residence. That is a rule, not a suggestion — an application filed at the wrong office simply will not go through, and you lose the time.

 !You cannot use a more convenient office instead of yours — the link is your address

 !Moved to another area mid-permit? Check the zone before you file, not after

 !The address on the application must be the real one: it is checked against accommodation records

## How the visit works

 Filing is online, but the procedure includes a photo taken at the office, so one visit stays mandatory.

 Apply onlineDocuments go through the government portal: passport, a sponsor's guarantee letter if you have a sponsor, and a statement of your purpose in Indonesia.

 PayAs long as payment clears before your current permit expires, no overstay accrues — even if the visit itself comes later.

 AppointmentThe office sends an electronic notice that your documents were received and books you in.

 Photo at the officeTakes a few minutes. Dress conservatively: shorts, singlets and beachwear are a common reason to be turned away.

 IssueThe finished permit arrives electronically — there is no paper to collect.

If something is wrong in your documents, the office sends a notice: you get 2 days from the notice date to fix it. Miss that and the application is rejected, and you start again.

## Timing and cost

 Official government fees for extending a visit stay permit:

 ✓30 days — IDR 500,000 per application (e-VOA extension)

 ✓60 days — IDR 2,000,000 (C1 visa and D-series multiple-entry extensions)

 ✓180 days — IDR 6,000,000 (C12 and D12 pre-investment visas)

 Processing takes up to 3 working days from the moment payment is received. You may file no earlier than 14 days before your current permit ends, and no later than the day it ends. The new period starts the day after the previous one finishes, so no days are lost.
File late and it becomes an overstay: IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person, children included.

## How to cut down the visits

 The logic is simple: the longer your permit, the less often you see immigration.

 ✓With an agency you come in once — just for the photo; filing, payment and status tracking are on us

 ✓A C1 visa instead of an e-VOA — 60 days rather than 30, so half the extensions

 ✓E33G for remote work — a year without the monthly extension routine

 ✓D1 and D2 multiple-entry visas — a year of entries with no visa before each trip

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How many immigration offices are there in Bali in 2026?
Five: Denpasar, Ngurah Rai, Singaraja, Tabanan and Klungkung. The last two opened on 6 April 2026. There were three before that, which is why older guides and checklists often give the wrong number.

Вопрос: Can I file at any office I like?
No. Your application is handled by the office whose working area covers your residential address. You cannot use a more convenient office — the link is the address, not your preference.

Вопрос: Which office covers Nusa Penida?
Klungkung, which opened on 6 April 2026 and covers Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan and Nusa Ceningan. Before that, island residents had to travel to mainland Bali.

Вопрос: Do I have to attend the office in person?
Yes, once — for the photo, which is part of the procedure. Everything else, including filing and payment, is done online, and the finished permit arrives electronically.

Вопрос: What happens if I file too late?
You may file up to and including the day your current permit expires. If payment clears by then, no overstay accrues. Miss it and the overstay starts at IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person.

## We will cut your immigration visits down to one

 We work out your office from your address, file the application, watch the deadlines and book your photo slot. You come in once.

# Bali Visas in 2026: Which One Fits Your Scenario

 Three questions decide your visa: how long you are coming for, what you will do, and whether you plan to stay. Up to 60 days — the eVOA; up to six months — a C1 or C2; frequent arrivals — a D1/D2; business scouting — the D12; remote work — the E33G KITAS; relocation — a KITAS for your situation. The full decision route in five minutes below.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Up to 60 days: eVOA

 The electronic visa on arrival is the default for a holiday: filed online before the flight, autogate lane at the border. It grants 30 days plus one 30-day extension. No sponsor needed — the only mainstream category without one. Details and application — on the eVOA page; extending it — in our step-by-step guide.

## 2–6 months: C1 and C2

 Single-entry visas for 60 days with two 60-day extensions — up to 180 days without leaving. The C1 covers tourism and a season of living; the C2 — negotiations, meetings, conferences (working on either is prohibited). Both are filed and extended through a sponsor — who that is, we explain in a separate article.

## Flying in often: D1 and D2

 Multiple-entry visas for 1–2 years: every entry grants 60 days, extendable in-country. The D1 follows tourist logic, the D2 — business. Ideal for those living between two countries who do not want to re-apply every trip.

## Scouting a business: D12

 The D12 Pre-Investment gives 180 days per entry for market research, extendable to 360. The extension does not require a registered PT PMA listing you in the deed — the D12 no longer works as a lifestyle visa; details in our D12 breakdown.

## Working remotely: E33G KITAS

 The E33G is a one-year residence status for those employed by a foreign company: legal remote work, multiple entry, family on companion visas. The key requirement is income from USD 60,000 a year. The status is extended for a further year, and you can switch to it from an e-VOA or C1 without leaving — through a Bridging Visa; the full picture is in our E33G guide.

## Relocating for good: KITAS and KITAP

 A KITAS is no longer a visa but a residence permit with a sponsor matching your situation: investor via a PT PMA, work from an employer, family through a spouse, retirement from 55, Second Home against a deposit. After several continuous KITAS years the KITAP — permanent residency — opens up. All statuses compared in our KITAS & KITAP guide.

## Cheat sheet: choose in 30 seconds

 ✓Holiday up to 2 months → eVOA

 ✓Wintering 3–6 months → C1

 ✓Negotiations and business trips → C2 or D2

 ✓Living between two countries → D1/D2

 ✓Researching the market before a business → D12

 ✓Remote work for a foreign company → E33G

 ✓Company already set up → Investor KITAS

 ✓Spouse is Indonesian or a KITAS holder → Family KITAS

 ✓55+ and settling in Bali → Retirement KITAS

 Pricing — on the all visas page; how each status extends — in the extension guide.

## FAQ

Вопрос: What is the simplest visa for a first trip?
The eVOA: applied for online before the flight, it grants 30 days plus one 30-day extension. For a holiday and a first look at Bali, that is enough.

Вопрос: I work remotely for a foreign company — what fits me?
The E33G KITAS: a year of residence and legal remote work with income from USD 60,000 a year. If you do not meet the criteria — a C1 with extensions or a D1/D2.

Вопрос: Can I switch to another visa without leaving?
Often yes: moving to a KITAS is processed in-country, and the Bridging Visa covers the gap between statuses. A visa never changes type by itself — only through a new status.

Вопрос: What should I choose if I plan to open a business?
For scouting — the D12 for 1–2 years. Once the company is set up — a 2-year Investor KITAS with no work permit needed.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

 Tell us your timeline, plans and family setup — we’ll suggest a status you won’t have to redo in six months.

# A bank account in Bali: it all comes down to status

 Opening an Indonesian bank account is a question not of which bank but of your status. KITAS and KITAP holders open accounts as an ordinary procedure; on a visit visa a standard resident account is generally unavailable. The core pack is a passport, a KITAS, proof of address and, depending on the bank, a tax number. Requirements vary between banks and branches.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Why it all comes down to status

 The main question when opening an account is not which bank but what status you arrive with. The bank needs to understand on what basis you are in the country and for how long.

 ✓With a residence status — a KITAS or KITAP — the account is an ordinary banking procedure

 ✓On a visit visa — an e-VOA, C1, C2 or multiple-entry — a standard resident account is generally not available

 Which is why 'a local bank account' appears in the benefits of almost every residence status: the E33G, Second Home, the retirement and family permits. The account is not a separate service but a consequence of status.

## What the pack usually contains

 The set varies between banks, but the core repeats:

 ✓Your passport

 ✓A valid KITAS or KITAP

 ✓An NPWP tax number, or a declaration that you have none — depending on the bank and account type

 ✓Proof of your address

 ✓Sometimes a letter from your sponsor or employer

 Honesty matters here. Requirements differ not only between banks but between branches of the same bank, and they change more often than they are published. Any list in an article — including this one — should be checked with the specific branch before you go, not relied on as final.

 Address registration — SKTT and STM — is done in the first 14 days after your KITAS is issued, and without it this step can stall.

## What the account gives you beyond transfers

 ✓Paying rent and utilities without cash or intermediaries

 ✓A local card accepted where foreign ones do not always work

 ✓The ability to evidence funds for visa and status procedures

 ✓For company owners — a separate corporate account for the PT PMA

 A corporate account is a different matter with a different pack: it is opened for the company after registration and the core documents, not for an individual.

## If you do not have status yet

 While you are on a visit visa, the sensible move is not to look for workarounds but to settle the status — the account follows.

 !'Open it in a local's name' schemes repeat the logic of nominee business ownership, with the same risks

 !An account that is not in your name is not yours — legally or practically

 If a residence status is in your plans, see which one fits: four questions in the visa finder give you a starting point.

## How to prepare for the visit

 A branch counter is not the place to discover the requirements. A few steps that save you a second trip:

 ✓Call or message the specific branch and confirm the list for your status type

 ✓Bring originals and copies — copies are asked for almost every time

 ✓Check that the address on your documents matches where you actually live

 ✓Confirm in advance whether an NPWP is needed for your particular account type

 On the statuses that unlock an account, see our E33G KITAS and Second Home guides.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I open an account on a tourist visa?
Generally no. Standard resident accounts are opened for KITAS or KITAP holders: the bank needs a basis for your presence in the country.

Вопрос: What documents are needed?
The core is a passport, a valid KITAS or KITAP, proof of address, and depending on the bank an NPWP tax number or a declaration that you have none. The exact list differs between banks and even branches.

Вопрос: Why does everyone quote different requirements?
Banks set internal rules themselves and change them more often than they publish them. Any list from an article is a guide, not a guarantee.

Вопрос: Do I need an NPWP?
It depends on the bank and account type: some require it, others accept a declaration that you have none. Worth confirming before you visit the branch.

Вопрос: What about a corporate account?
It is opened for the company after PT PMA registration and the core documents. A separate procedure, unrelated to a personal account.

## Status first — the account follows

 We will match a residence KITAS to your situation. With it come the bank, long-term rental and a local licence.

# The Bridging Visa: 60 days without flying out

 The Bridging Visa is a 60-day transitional status for people already in Indonesia. It does two jobs: it keeps you legal while a new KITAS is under review, and it lets you extend a stay on a visa on arrival by another 60 days without flying out. It costs IDR 4,000,000 with us. It removes the central fear of changing visa: the old status has ended, the new one is still being assessed, and no overstay fine accrues. It is issued only alongside an application for a new status and works only inside the country: leaving cancels it.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What it is and why it exists

 There used to be a grey zone between 'the old visa has expired' and 'the new one has been issued': either a visa run with a flight, or an overstay at IDR 1,000,000 a day. The Bridging Visa closes exactly that gap.

 ✓It gives 60 days of lawful waiting inside the country

 ✓No overstay accrues during that period

 ✓It is issued only alongside an application for a new status

 ✓The mechanism is provided for in the current visa and stay permit framework

 This is not a standalone visa for extending a holiday. No application for a new status means no bridging permit: it exists only as a bridge between two statuses.

## Who it suits

 ✓Moving from a visit visa to a KITAS — the classic case: from an e-VOA, C1, C2, D1/D2 or D12 to an investor, family, work or remote-worker status

 ✓Converting to an E33G from an e-VOA or C1 — moving to remote-worker status without leaving the country; IDR 16,000,000 turnkey with us

 ✓Changing KITAS category — for example from family to investor once a company is running

 !It does not work from visa-free entry. A change of status is prohibited there outright, so there is nothing to bridge

 !You cannot extend a holiday through bridging — that is not what it is for

## How it works

 File for the new statusAssemble the basis for the specific KITAS: company documents, an employer's offer, a marriage certificate, proof of income.

 The bridging permit is issuedIssued with the application — there is no separate request to make.

 Wait inside the countryUp to 60 days of lawful stay while the application is assessed.

 The KITAS is issuedOnce approved, the limited stay permit is issued with biometrics.

## What to keep in mind

 !It works only inside the country. Fly out and it is gone; you would return on a new visa

 !It is not open-ended. Sixty days is a waiting period, not a buffer for 'when I get round to the papers'

 !It does not grant the new status early. Until the KITAS is issued you cannot work on it

 On timing specifically: the change-of-status function is busier than usual in 2026. Allow extra room and start assembling the basis early — detail in our conversion article.

## Bridging, a visa run or an overstay

 When your old visa runs out and the new status is still being assessed, you have exactly three options. Two of them are bad.

 ✓Bridging — you stay lawfully for up to 60 days, no fines, the process continues

 ✓A visa run — a flight, a hotel, lost days, and on return the new application may need reassembling

 ✓An overstay — IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person, and a damaged record for future applications

 The choice is obvious, but it only works on one condition: the application for the new status must be filed before your current permit expires. A bridging permit is never issued retroactively — once the deadline has passed you are dealing with an overstay, not a bridge.

## Case one: extend a VOA by another 60 days

 This is the most common reason people come to us for a transitional permit, and almost nobody knows it is possible. Here is the standard path on a visa on arrival:

 ✓30 days — the base VOA term on entry

 ✓+30 days — the regular extension, which is the one and only

 ✓+60 days — the Bridging Visa on top of that, without leaving the country

 That is four months on the island instead of two, with not a single flight out for a stamp. For comparison, a chain of visa runs over the same period eats two tickets, two hotels and several lost days, and comes to a similar sum.

 Why this is easier than it sounds. All documents are filed remotely. You do not go to the immigration office and there is no verification step — the very thing people dread most since June 2025, when extending an ordinary visa started requiring an in-person visit and biometrics again. The stay permit is issued immediately.

## Case two: change your type of status

 The second job of a transitional permit is to close the gap while one status is ending and the next is still under review. Here are the two situations we see most often.

 From a visit visa to a KITASYou arrived on a VOA, decided to stay and work remotely. There is no direct switch from a VOA to a KITAS — the route runs through a transitional permit, which also keeps you legal while your E33G is processed. From a C1 visa, unlike a VOA, the conversion is direct.

 From one KITAS to anotherSay you held an investor KITAS (E28A), the company has been closed, but you keep working for a foreign client and now need an E33G. The old status closes, the new one is not issued yet, and the transitional permit covers that gap.

 The procedure costs IDR 4,000,000 with us. Changing KITAS type also requires closing the previous status: we covered how that works in our guide to EPO and ERP.

## How many days each step buys you

 A clear view of why the bridging permit exists: without it a VOA hits its ceiling on day sixty.

 Staying on a visa on arrival, with and without the bridging permit.
 Step | Adds | Total on the island | Flight out? | In person? | 

 Entry on a VOA | 30 | 30 | no | no | 

 Standard extension | +30 | 60 | no | yes, biometrics | 

 Bridging Visa | +60 | 120 | no | no, fully remote | 

 Without bridging | — | 60 | yes, a visa run | — | 

 Four months instead of two, and not a single flight for the sake of a stamp. The bridging permit costs IDR 4,000,000; a chain of visa runs over the same period eats two tickets, two hotels and several lost days.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much does a Bridging Visa cost?
IDR 4,000,000 with us, per procedure. That covers document preparation, filing and support through to the stay permit being issued.

Вопрос: Do I have to go to the immigration office in person?
No. Documents are filed remotely, this procedure requires no verification visit, and the stay permit is issued immediately. That is a notable difference from an ordinary visa extension, which since June 2025 requires an in-person visit and biometrics.

Вопрос: What is the Bridging Visa code?
There is none, and that is not an oversight. Its official name is Izin Tinggal Peralihan — a transitional stay permit. It is not a visa in the immigration classification but a mechanism for moving between permits, so it has no index like C1 or E33G. If you see a "bridging visa code" quoted somewhere, it is invented.

Вопрос: What is a Bridging Visa in plain terms?
A 60-day transitional status for people already in Indonesia awaiting a decision on a new stay permit. No overstay accrues throughout.

Вопрос: Can I get one on its own?
No. The bridging permit is issued only together with an application for a new status, usually a KITAS. It cannot be arranged by itself.

Вопрос: Does it expire if I leave?
Yes. It works only inside the country: leaving cancels it, and you would have to return on a new visa.

Вопрос: Can I work during that period?
No. The rights of the new status begin only once the KITAS is issued. Until then you cannot work.

Вопрос: Does it apply if I entered visa-free?
No. From visa-free entry a change of status is prohibited entirely, so a bridging permit does not apply.

## We will run the change of status with no gaps

 We assemble the basis, file the application together with the bridging permit, and see it through to the KITAS.

# Bali C1 visa 2026: half a year, no exit

 The C1 is a single-entry tourist visa. It gives 60 days from the date of entry and extends twice by 60 days each — up to 180 consecutive days without a single border run. Arranged online before departure, all-in from IDR 2,500,000. The main limitation: leaving the country cancels it.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How the C1 works

 The C1 is a single-entry tourist visa. It gives 60 days from the date of entry and extends twice inside the country by 60 days each — up to 180 consecutive days. It is the standard choice for a long winter stay: half a year on the island without a single border run.

 ✓60 days on entry, then two 60-day extensions — a ceiling of 180 days

 ✓Arranged online before departure, from any country, with no consulate visit

 ✓The autogate works with an electronic C1 on arrival

 ✓A sponsor is required — for our clients, we act as the sponsor

 !The visa is single-entry: leaving Indonesia cancels it, and you cannot return on it

 !Flying in and out? You need a D1 or D2 multiple-entry visa, not a C1

## Timing and extensions: 60 → 120 → 180

 Extensions are filed at the immigration office covering your address. The official fee for each 60-day extension is IDR 2,000,000, processed within 3 working days of payment.

 Days 1–60The first period starts on the date of entry. An extension may be filed no earlier than 14 days before it ends.

 First extensionAnother 60 days. The new period starts the day after the old one — no days are lost.

 Second extensionThe final 60 days. No further extension is possible: 180 days is the legal ceiling.

 After thatEither you leave, or you change status to a KITAS — and that has to start early, not in the last week.

File with at least 6 working days to spare. Miss the deadline and it is an overstay: IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person. With our support the dates are our problem: we remind you and file early.

## C1 or e-VOA: when the extra cost pays off

 The price difference is real, so the number to compare is the cost of the whole trip, not of the visa.

 ✓Staying up to 60 days — take the e-VOA at IDR 900,000; a C1 is money wasted

 ✓Staying 3–6 months — the C1 is cheaper and calmer than a chain of border runs and fresh e-VOAs

 ✓Thinking of staying — the C1 converts to a KITAS without leaving the country, and that is the decisive argument

 A detailed comparison of cost and timing is in C1 or e-VOA.

## Documents and cost

 The list is short, but the passport requirements are strict — that is where most applications fail.

 ✓A passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry

 ✓A clean scan of the photo page — no glare, no cropped corners

 ✓A photo on a white background

 ✓A return or onward ticket and your address in Indonesia

 The all-in price is from IDR 2,500,000, and processing takes a few working days. Extensions are paid separately at the official rate. Full terms are on the C1 visa page.

## What you cannot do on a C1

 The C1 is a visit visa. It carries no right to work or to earn inside the country, and that is not a technicality: according to immigration, working on a tourist visa is one of the leading causes of deportation from Bali.

 !Working for Indonesian companies or earning income inside the country

 !Providing services to local clients, commercial filming and advertising work

 !Long-form study and working as a journalist

 If you work remotely for foreign clients there is a dedicated status, the E33G. If you run a business in Indonesia, look at the investor KITAS.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay in Bali on a C1 visa?
Up to 180 consecutive days: 60 days on entry plus two extensions of 60 days each. That is the legal ceiling — there is no third extension.

Вопрос: Can I leave and come back on a C1?
No. The C1 is single-entry: leaving Indonesia cancels it and you cannot return on it. If you plan trips in and out, you need a D1 or D2 multiple-entry visa.

Вопрос: How much does a C1 extension cost?
The official fee is IDR 2,000,000 for each 60-day extension; turnkey with us it is IDR 2,500,000, or IDR 3,500,000 rushed. There are at most two. Processing takes up to 3 working days after payment; filing opens 14 days before the current period ends.

Вопрос: Can I convert a C1 into a KITAS without flying out?
Yes — changing status from a visit permit to a limited stay permit is provided for, and it is one of the C1's main advantages. The procedure is not quick, so start it early rather than in your final weeks.

Вопрос: Do I need a sponsor for a C1 visa?
Yes, the visa requires a sponsor. For our clients we act as the sponsor, so there is no one for you to find.

## We will arrange your C1 and handle every extension

 We file before you fly, act as your sponsor, track the deadlines and file extensions early — up to 180 days with none of the bureaucracy on you.

# C1 or e-VOA: which one for Bali

 The line falls at 60 days — the e-VOA ceiling. Staying less: take the e-VOA, IDR 900,000 all-in for 30 days with one extension. Staying longer: only the C1, from IDR 2,500,000, 60 days with two extensions up to 180. You cannot move from an e-VOA to a C1 inside the country, so decide before you fly.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 The line falls on one number — 60 days. That is the e-VOA ceiling, and no amount of extending gets around it.

 ✓Staying up to 60 days — take the e-VOA. A C1 costs three times as much for nothing

 ✓Staying longer than 60 days — take a C1, arranged before you fly

 ✓Not sure — take the C1: you cannot switch from an e-VOA to a C1 once you are in the country

 The classic mistake is taking an e-VOA to 'see how it goes' and planning to extend further. There is no second extension: on day 61 it is either a flight out or an overstay at IDR 1,000,000 a day.

 Check yourself. The visa finder also factors in your purpose and how many times you will enter over the year.

## The key differences

 | 
 e-VOA | 
 C1 | 

 On entry | 30 days | 60 days | 

 Extensions | one, of 30 days | two, of 60 days | 

 Ceiling | 60 days | 180 days | 

 All-in price | IDR 900,000 | from IDR 2,500,000 | 

 Extension fee | IDR 500,000 | IDR 2,000,000 each | 

 Leaving the country | cancels both — they are single-entry | 

 Conversion to KITAS | possible from either | 

## Running the numbers

 Comparing visa prices is pointless — compare the cost of a trip of the length you actually want.

 ✓30 days: e-VOA — IDR 900,000. No C1 needed

 ✓60 days: e-VOA — 900,000 plus the extension (fee 500,000). C1 — from 2,500,000 with no extension

 ✓120 days: e-VOA impossible. C1 — from 2,500,000 plus one extension of 2,000,000

 ✓180 days: e-VOA impossible. C1 — from 2,500,000 plus two extensions of 2,000,000

 Per day the e-VOA is cheaper — but only inside its own 60 days. The moment your trip runs past them, the C1 has no competitor: a chain of flights out for fresh e-VOAs costs more in airfare and draws questions at the border when repeated often.

## What the fee rise changes

 On 12 August 2026 immigration announced plans to raise the government fee for a visa on arrival: IDR 750,000 arranged online before departure and IDR 1,000,000 obtained at the airport, against the current 500,000. No effective date has been set.

 ✓The all-in e-VOA price will rise by roughly the increase in the fee

 ✓The gap between the e-VOA and the C1 narrows — short trips get pricier, long ones stay put

 ✓The spread between arranging ahead and buying at the airport becomes IDR 250,000, making advance filing clearly worth it

 Until the change takes effect the current rates apply. We track the announcement and will warn clients ahead of time.

## Who should take which

 ✓A two or three week holiday — the e-VOA, no question

 ✓A month and a bit — the e-VOA with its extension fits inside 60 days

 ✓Three to six months — a C1, arranged before departure

 ✓Testing the idea of moving — the C1: switching to a KITAS from it without leaving is more straightforward

 !Flying in and out several times during the trip — both are single-entry; you need a D1 or D2 multiple-entry visa

 !Planning to work — neither grants that right; look at the E33G or a work KITAS

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I switch from an e-VOA to a C1 while in Bali?
No. A C1 is arranged before departure, from outside Indonesia. If you have entered on an e-VOA and realise 60 days is not enough, you have two options: leave and re-enter on a C1, or change status to a KITAS if your case supports one.

Вопрос: Which is cheaper for 60 days, e-VOA or C1?
The e-VOA: IDR 900,000 all-in plus an extension with a 500,000 fee, against from 2,500,000 for a C1. But on day 61 the e-VOA is finished for good, while the C1 still has 120 days in reserve.

Вопрос: Are both visas single-entry?
Yes. Both the e-VOA and the C1 are cancelled when you leave Indonesia — you cannot return on the same visa. For trips in and out you need a D-series multiple-entry visa.

Вопрос: How many times can each be extended?
The e-VOA once, by 30 days, for a 60-day ceiling. The C1 twice, by 60 days each, for a 180-day ceiling. Neither limit can be exceeded at any price.

Вопрос: Will visas get more expensive in 2026?
Immigration has announced plans to raise the visa-on-arrival fee to IDR 750,000 online and IDR 1,000,000 at the airport. No date has been set, and current rates still apply.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

 Tell us your travel dates and we will price both options and arrange whichever works out cheaper for you.

# The C18 visa: a bridge to a work KITAS

 The C18 is the candidate foreign worker visa: for people an employer is already waiting for, while the company obtains its permits. It gives 60 days on entry, extendable in 60-day steps to a ceiling of 120. It is arranged on the employer's initiative and converts into a work KITAS without leaving. Working and earning begin only once the KITAS is issued.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Why a separate visa exists

 The situation is standard: you have an offer from an Indonesian company, but a work KITAS is not instant — the employer must obtain permits first. Flying in 'on a tourist visa for now' and sorting it out later is not an option: working on a visit visa is a breach carrying fines and deportation.
The C18 exists for exactly this window. You are in the country lawfully as a candidate while your employer prepares your full work status.

## Timing: 60 days extendable to 120

 In the official classification the C18 is the candidate foreign worker visa, single entry.

 ✓60 days on first entry

 ✓Extendable in 60-day steps — up to 120 days in total

 ✓Converts into a work KITAS without leaving the country

 Note the ceiling: 120 days, not 90 and not 180. That is less than a C1 tourist visa allows, which is precisely why the employer's side of the process must start early.

## How the path looks

 The offerThe starting point is an offer from an Indonesian company.

 Invitation and C18The visa is arranged on the employer's initiative, on the basis of an invitation.

 Arrival and onboardingYou are in the country lawfully as a candidate: meeting the team, completing the final stages of hiring.

 Employer permitsIn parallel the company obtains the RPTKA and its accompanying pack.

 Conversion to a work KITASOnce approved, you move to full work status without flying out.

## What is and is not allowed

 ✓Being in the country as a candidate for a role

 ✓Attending interviews, meeting the team and learning the processes

 ✓Preparing documents for your work status

 !Working and earning — only after the work KITAS is issued

 !Providing services to other companies

 The full picture of work status is in our work KITAS article: RPTKA, entry on a VITAS and the employer lock-in.

## Documents

 ✓A passport with plenty of validity left

 ✓A personal photo

 ✓An invitation or confirmation from the employer

 ✓Qualification documents matched to the future role

 Timing and parameters depend on how ready the company's paperwork is. We work with both sides — the candidate and the employer — so the two files come together in parallel.

## Common mistakes

 !Flying in on a tourist visa to 'sort it out here'. Working on a visit visa is a breach, and a correct declared purpose makes both this application and every future one easier

 !Confusing the C18 with the C2 business visa. The C2 is for meetings and negotiations; you cannot arrive on it to work

 !Not allowing time. The C18 ceiling is 120 days, and if the employer's permits are not ready that runs out faster than you expect

 !Starting with yourself rather than the company. Without an invitation and permits there is nothing to base the visa on

 The practical takeaway: once the offer is signed, run both tracks at once — yours and the employer's. Then 120 days is a buffer rather than a deadline.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay on a C18?
60 days on first entry, extendable in 60-day steps to a ceiling of 120 days in total. Beyond that you need the work KITAS itself.

Вопрос: Can I work on a C18?
No. The C18 legitimises a candidate's presence during processing, but the right to work and earn arrives only with the work KITAS.

Вопрос: Who arranges the C18?
The visa is arranged on the initiative of the Indonesian employer, on the basis of an invitation. A candidate cannot obtain it alone.

Вопрос: Do I have to leave to get the work KITAS?
No, the C18 converts into work status without leaving the country.

Вопрос: How does the C18 differ from the C2 business visa?
The C2 is about meetings and negotiations; the C18 is about starting a specific job on an offer. Arriving to work on a C2 is not allowed.

## We take both sides through it — candidate and company

 We arrange the C18 on the employer's invitation, help with the RPTKA and see it through to the work KITAS with no extra flights.

# The C2 business visa: up to 180 days of business

 The C2 is a single-entry visa for business travel: negotiations, conferences, market research, sourcing. It gives 60 days with two 60-day extensions — up to half a year in the country. All-in from IDR 4,200,000, sponsor required. The key limit: the C2 legitimises business activity but not employment or income inside Indonesia.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the C2 gives you

 The C2 is a single-entry visit visa for business purposes. Mechanically it works like the C1 tourist visa but is applied for under a different declared purpose.

 ✓60 days from the date of entry

 ✓Two 60-day extensions — up to 180 days in total

 ✓Single entry: leaving the country cancels it

 ✓Convertible into a KITAS without flying out

 Arranged entirely online, before departure, from anywhere. A sponsor is required — for our clients we act as the sponsor.

## What it covers

 ✓Negotiations and meetings with partners, investors and suppliers

 ✓Conferences, exhibitions and business events

 ✓Site visits, market research, preparing contracts

 ✓Sourcing goods for your business outside Indonesia

## The line: business purpose is not work

 The most important section. The C2 legitimises business activity but not employment and not income inside the country.

 !Holding a position in an Indonesian company is not allowed — that is a work KITAS

 !Providing services and being paid for them in Indonesia is not allowed

 !Running operations for a local company or signing on its behalf is not allowed

 Starting a job on an offer is covered by the C18 visa, and running your own company by the investor KITAS. The difference between 'came to negotiate' and 'started working' matters to immigration.

## Timing and cost

 ✓Minimal — IDR 4,200,000, processed in 10 working days

 ✓Regular — IDR 5,000,000, processed in 5–6 working days

 ✓Both include all taxes and fees, the e-visa, and document preparation and filing

 Extensions are paid separately: the official fee for a 60-day stay permit is IDR 2,000,000 each. File no earlier than 14 days before your current period ends and no later than the day it does.

## Documents

 ✓A photo of the full passport spread — valid at least 6 months from the date of entry

 ✓A personal photo

 ✓Details of your trip's purpose, as requested by the sponsor

 Passport requirements are covered separately: more applications fail on those than on anything else.

## When the C2 is not the best fit

 ✓Regular business trips — a D2 multiple-entry visa for one or two years with unlimited entries works out better

 ✓Scouting an investment — the D12 visa gives up to 180 days per visit

 ✓A short trip with no business element — an e-VOA is enough

## C2 or C1: the practical difference

 On timing and mechanics they are identical: 60 days and two 60-day extensions. What differs is the declared purpose and what you can do without putting your status at risk.

 ✓C1 — holidays, tourism, visiting family. Cheaper: from IDR 2,500,000

 ✓C2 — business meetings, conferences, negotiations, sourcing. From IDR 4,200,000

 For a mixed trip — a holiday plus a couple of meetings — the purpose is judged by what the trip is mainly about. Where the meetings are the point of the trip, the C2 is the correct visa: a mismatch between the declared purpose and actual activity is not read in the traveller's favour.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay in Indonesia on a C2?
60 days on entry plus two 60-day extensions — up to 180 days in total. The visa is single-entry: leaving the country cancels it.

Вопрос: How much does the C2 business visa cost?
The Minimal package is IDR 4,200,000 with a 10 working day turnaround; Regular is IDR 5,000,000 in 5–6 working days. Extensions are separate, at the official IDR 2,000,000 per 60 days.

Вопрос: Can I work on a C2?
No. The C2 covers meetings, negotiations and conferences, but not employment or income inside the country. Paid work requires a work KITAS.

Вопрос: Do I need a sponsor?
Yes, the visa is arranged with an Indonesian sponsor. For our clients we act as the sponsor, so there is nobody for you to find.

Вопрос: Can a C2 be converted into a KITAS?
Yes, conversion to a limited stay permit is possible without leaving the country. Start the process early.

## We will arrange the C2 — come and do the deal

 We act as your sponsor, file before departure and handle extensions. And we will say up front if a D2 suits your pattern better.

# Indonesia C6 visa: the social visit route

 The C6 is a single-entry visit visa for social activity: it covers social projects, travel and visiting family. It gives 60 days, extendable to 180 in total. The government fee is IDR 2,000,000. A sponsor is mandatory, along with three months of bank statements and a letter from the host organisation.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the C6 is

 The C6 is a single-entry visit visa for social activity. The official wording sounds narrow, but it covers more than it seems: on a C6 you may carry out social activity in Indonesia, and also travel and visit friends and family.

 ✓60 days on first entry, counted from the arrival date

 ✓Extendable several times — up to 180 days in total

 ✓Extensions are filed online by your sponsor through the government portal

 ✓Convertible into a limited stay permit (KITAS) — with the same sponsor

 Visa validity and permitted stay are different things. The visa itself is valid for 90 days from issue: fail to enter within that window and you apply again. Your days of stay only start counting on arrival.

## What it costs

 The government fee for a C6 comes in two parts and totals IDR 2,000,000:

 ✓C6 visa fee — IDR 1,000,000

 ✓Verification fee — IDR 1,000,000

 Extensions are paid separately at the stay-permit rate. Processing takes five working days from receipt of payment.

## Documents and the sponsor

 The key difference from tourist visas: the application is filed not by you but by your sponsor, from their account on the immigration portal. Without a sponsor there is no C6.

 ✓The sponsor's application and guarantee letter

 ✓A passport valid for at least 6 months (for travel documents other than a national passport, at least 12)

 ✓Three months of bank statements — in the name of the foreigner or the sponsor

 ✓A recent colour photo taken within the last year

 A requirement specific to the C6: a letter from a government body or private organisation setting out the activities and itinerary of the foreigner in Indonesia. That letter is why this visa cannot be arranged on a whim — it needs a real host.

## C6 or C1: which to take

 On timing they are near twins — 60 days extendable to 180. They differ in basis, paperwork and price.

 ✓C1 — the tourist visa, arranged for a holiday. All-in from IDR 2,500,000 with us as your sponsor. Explained in our C1 visa guide

 ✓C6 — for social activity and visits to a host. A IDR 2,000,000 fee, three months of statements and a letter from the organisation

 The practical read: if you have a host organisation or relatives willing to sponsor you, the C6 works. If you are travelling as an ordinary tourist, the C1 is simpler and more predictable — fewer documents and no dependence on a third party's letter.

## What you cannot do on a C6

 The restriction is written into the rules and follows the logic of every visit visa:

 !Selling goods or services in Indonesia

 !Receiving payment, wages or any other remuneration for work from people or companies in Indonesia

 So the C6 carries no right to income inside the country — the same as an e-VOA, a C1 or a multiple-entry visa. Working remotely for foreign clients? See the E33G. Taking a job with an Indonesian company? You need a work KITAS.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay in Indonesia on a C6?
60 days on first entry, then extensions — up to 180 days in total. Extensions are filed online by your sponsor through the immigration portal.

Вопрос: How much does a C6 visa cost?
The government fee is IDR 2,000,000: 1,000,000 for the visa and 1,000,000 for verification. Extensions are paid separately. Processing takes five working days after payment.

Вопрос: Do I need a sponsor for a C6?
Yes, always. The application is submitted by your sponsor from their account on the immigration portal — you cannot file it yourself. A letter from an organisation describing your activities is also required.

Вопрос: Is a bank statement really required?
Yes. The C6 officially requires three months of bank statements, in the name of the foreigner or the sponsor, as proof of funds to live on in Indonesia.

Вопрос: Can a C6 be converted into a KITAS?
Yes, the stay permit from a C6 can be converted into a limited stay permit, provided the sponsor stays the same.

## Let us work out whether the C6 fits

 Tell us who your host is and how long you are staying — we will compare the C6 with the C1 on paperwork and cost and arrange whichever clears more easily.

# Children in Bali: visas and paperwork

 A child has their own status: their own visa, their own stay permit and their own passport — they cannot be added to a parent's documents. Overstay counts for them exactly as for an adult. The autogate is available from age six. A child born in Indonesia to parents holding a visit permit receives the same permit at the nearest immigration office.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## A child is a separate person to immigration

 The first thing to understand: your child has their own status. They are not automatically attached to a parent, and they count as an adult in everything to do with deadlines and fines.

 !Overstay counts for a child too. IDR 1,000,000 a day, per person, infants included. For a family of four the total is multiplied by four

 !Their own visa and stay permit are needed from birth

 !Their own passport is mandatory — adding a child to a parent's is not enough

## Travelling with a child: which visa

 For a short trip the setup is the same as for adults, and it is arranged for each person separately.

 ✓e-VOA — 30 days with one extension, arranged separately for the child

 ✓C1 — if the trip runs beyond 60 days

 ✓Visa-free entry — if your nationality qualifies; the same limits apply: 30 days, no extension

 Plan around the 'shortest' family member: if your child's passport expires soonest, that is what decides which visa the whole family can take. Passport rules are covered in a separate article.

## The autogate: from what age

 The automated gates save the whole family time, but children have an age threshold.

 ✓Children aged 6 and over may use the autogate subject to the usual requirements — a biometric passport and an approved electronic visa

 ✓With a child under 6, one parent goes through a staffed counter

 ✓Every family member's arrival, infants included, must be registered by immigration

 The All Indonesia declaration is filed for each person — details in our autogate article.

## If your child is born in Indonesia

 There is a specific procedure in the rules: a child born in Indonesia whose father and/or mother held a visit stay permit at the time of birth receives the same permit at the nearest immigration office.

 ✓The child's passport

 ✓A birth statement from the hospital, or a birth certificate

 ✓The parents' passports

 ✓The parents' stay permits

 Do not delay. A newborn has no default status: until the paperwork is done the child is formally in the country without a permit. Your consulate issues the child's passport, and that is the first step, not the last.

## A family staying long term

 If the parents live in Indonesia on a residence status, the children are arranged alongside them.

 ✓The family KITAS — for spouses and children of KITAS or KITAP holders, for the term of the sponsor's document. Children are registered up to and including age 17

 ✓Family KITAS are issued alongside an E33G and alongside work status

 ✓Attending school on a family KITAS is allowed; working on it is not

 The process and documents are set out in our family KITAS article, including the marriage and birth certificate translations that most often cost people time.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Does a child need their own visa?
Yes. A child has their own status and their own stay permit; they cannot be added to a parent's documents. They also need their own passport.

Вопрос: Does overstay count for a child?
Yes, exactly as for an adult: IDR 1,000,000 for each day of overstay, per person, infants included.

Вопрос: From what age can a child use the autogate?
From age 6, subject to the usual requirements — a biometric passport and an approved electronic visa. With a child under 6, one parent goes through a staffed counter.

Вопрос: What do I do if my child is born in Indonesia?
A child born in the country to parents holding a visit stay permit receives the same permit at the nearest immigration office. You will need the child's passport, a birth statement or certificate, and the parents' passports and permits.

Вопрос: Up to what age can a child be included on a family KITAS?
Children are registered on a KITAS up to and including age 17. Older children are considered separately.

## We will handle the papers for the whole family at once

 We check the dates on every passport, match the visas to your overall plan and make sure nobody's status lapses.

# Closing a company in Indonesia: doing it cleanly

 An Indonesian company does not evaporate: while it is on the registers it must file and pay tax, and missed filings accumulate into fines for directors and shareholders. A proper liquidation means a shareholders' resolution, a liquidator, public notices, settling creditors, tax reconciliation with NPWP deregistration, and removal from the register. The tax stage is the longest.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Abandoning is not closing

 An Indonesian company does not vanish on its own. While it sits on the registers it must file reports and pay taxes, and missed filings accumulate into fines that land on specific people.

 !Debts and penalties build up on a company that trades nothing

 !The consequences fall on directors and shareholders, not on an abstract legal entity

 !Unsettled obligations resurface at your next registration and when renewing visa statuses

 Which is why 'just stop filing' is the most expensive scenario available.

## The stages of liquidation

 Shareholders' resolutionThe RUPS general meeting resolves to liquidate and appoints a liquidator.

 Public noticesPublication, and settlement with creditors and employees.

 Tax reconciliationClosing obligations and deregistering the NPWP. Usually the longest stage.

 Licences revokedThe NIB and permits are cancelled in the OSS system.

 Removal from the registerThe company is struck from the Ministry of Justice register.

## How much time to allow

 Timing is set not by the paperwork but by the tax side: reconciling obligations and deregistering the NPWP takes longer than everything else combined.

 ✓The cleaner the bookkeeping has been, the faster reconciliation goes

 ✓A company with missed periods must close those first and only then liquidate

 ✓Employees and creditors must be settled before deregistration

 The practical conclusion: decide to close not when the money has run out but when it is clear the project will not fly. Liquidation takes resources, and it is better to have them.

## When closing is not the answer

 Sometimes the problem is solved another way, and it is worth discussing before starting.

 ✓Changing activity — sometimes new KBLI codes and licences are enough

 ✓Changing ownership — shares can be transferred without liquidating

 ✓Pausing operations — a company may trade nothing but must still file

 If your KITAS depends on the company, liquidation affects it directly: the investor status rests on a stake in a live PT PMA.

## What to prepare before starting

 Liquidation moves faster when the papers are in order. What to gather in advance:

 ✓Founding documents and every amendment to them

 ✓The tax history: filed returns, payments, correspondence

 ✓A register of obligations: creditors, leases, employment contracts

 ✓Licences and permits obtained through OSS

 And separately — settle the owner's status in advance. If your KITAS rests on this company, you need to know what comes next: a move to another status, departure, or a new structure. Deciding that mid-liquidation is late and expensive.

## How long it takes

 The exact timeline depends on the state of the company's affairs, but the shape is consistent: the corporate steps move relatively quickly, and the tax side sets the whole schedule.

 ✓A company with clean filings and no debts closes noticeably faster

 ✓Missed periods are closed first, and only then does reconciliation begin

 ✓Settlements with employees and creditors must finish before deregistration

 If the answer is restructuring rather than closing, compare the forms in PT PMA or Local PT, and see How to open a PT PMA for the process.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I just abandon the company?
No. While it remains on the registers it must file and pay tax. Missed filings accumulate into fines, and directors and shareholders answer for them.

Вопрос: Which stage takes longest?
Tax reconciliation: closing obligations and deregistering the NPWP. It usually takes longer than all the corporate steps combined.

Вопрос: What happens to the licences?
The NIB and related permits are revoked in the OSS system, after which the company is struck from the Ministry of Justice register.

Вопрос: Does liquidation affect my KITAS?
Yes, if your status depends on the company. An investor KITAS rests on a stake in a live PT PMA, so the route needs planning in advance.

Вопрос: Could I change activity instead of closing?
Sometimes: new KBLI codes and licences, or a transfer of shares, solve the problem without liquidating. Worth discussing before you start.

## We will close the company cleanly

 We run every stage, from the shareholders' resolution to deregistration. And we will say early if your problem can be solved without liquidating.

# D1 and D2 multiple-entry visas 2026: a year of entries

 D1 and D2 are multiple-entry visit visas valid for one or two years with unlimited entries. Each arrival opens 60 days, extendable in-country to 180 days per visit. The D1 covers tourism (from IDR 5,000,000 a year), the D2 business purposes (from IDR 5,500,000). Leaving the country does not cancel them.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How D1 and D2 work

 These are D-series multiple-entry visit visas. The visa is issued for one or two years, and throughout that period the number of entries is unlimited. Each arrival opens a fresh 60 days, extendable inside the country up to 180 days per visit.

 ✓Visa validity — one or two years, with unlimited entries

 ✓Each visit — 60 days with two 60-day extensions, up to 180 days

 ✓A new 60 days starts on each arrival date — no need to reapply

 ✓Arranged online from any country; a sponsor is required

## D1 or D2: the difference

 The index is set by the purpose of your trips, and it cannot be changed later — the purpose is declared when you apply.

 ✓D1 — tourism and personal visits. From IDR 5,000,000 per year

 ✓D2 — business purposes: meetings, negotiations, conferences, exhibitions. From IDR 5,500,000 per year

 Both are visit visas. Neither D1 nor D2 grants the right to work in Indonesia or earn income inside the country. The D2 permits business meetings but not operational work: you cannot sign contracts on behalf of a local company or run its affairs on this visa.

## How the stay is counted

 This is where most confusion starts, so step by step: visa validity and permitted stay are two different things.

 The visa is valid 1–2 yearsThat is the window in which you may enter. On its own it does not entitle you to be in the country.

 Each entry gives 60 daysThe count restarts from the arrival date, however many times you come in.

 Extensions of 60 daysWithin a visit the stay can be extended twice, taking a single visit to 180 days.

 Leaving resets the counterFly out and back and you get 60 days again. The visa itself survives, unlike a C1.

The official fee for each 60-day extension is IDR 2,000,000. Our all-in extension is IDR 2,600,000 when filed 6 or more working days ahead; shorter notice costs more.

## Passport requirements

 Annual D-series visas are stricter than the e-VOA here, and a fair share of applications fail on this.

 ✓Passport validity of at least 18 months at the time of filing

 ✓At least 4 blank pages

 ✓A clean scan of the photo page and a photo on a light background

 !Passport expiring within a year — no annual multiple-entry visa; renew it first

 !Fewer than four free pages — same answer

## Who it pays off for, and who it does not

 A multiple-entry visa is justified by how often you fly, not by how long you stay.

 ✓Three or more trips a year — a D1 or D2 is cheaper and calmer than a visa before every flight

 ✓Living between two countries — Bali and somewhere else — this is your option

 ✓Travelling for business — regular meetings and conferences are covered by the D2

 !Living on the island without leaving — a C1 or E33G works out cheaper; a multiple-entry visa is money wasted

 !One two-week trip — take an e-VOA

 !Planning to work or run a business — you need a KITAS; visit visas will not help

 Full pricing, including the two-year options, is on the D1/D2 multiple-entry visa page.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay in Indonesia on a D1 visa?
Each entry gives 60 days, extendable twice by 60 — up to 180 days per visit. The number of entries during the visa's validity is unlimited, and the counter restarts after every departure.

Вопрос: What is the difference between D1 and D2?
The purpose of travel. The D1 is for tourism and personal visits, the D2 for business: meetings, negotiations, conferences. Neither grants the right to work in Indonesia.

Вопрос: How much does a one-year multiple-entry visa cost?
The D1 starts at IDR 5,000,000 and the D2 at IDR 5,500,000 for a one-year visa. Two-year versions cost more. Extending your stay in-country is paid separately, from IDR 2,600,000.

Вопрос: What are the passport requirements?
Annual D-series visas need a passport valid for at least 18 months with a minimum of 4 blank pages. That is stricter than the e-VOA, where six months is enough.

Вопрос: Does leaving the country cancel a multiple-entry visa?
No, and that is its key difference from the C1. The visa stays valid for its full term, and every new arrival opens a fresh 60 days of stay.

## We will pick D1 or D2 and work out whether it pays off

 Tell us how many trips you expect this year and we will compare a multiple-entry visa against a C1 and an e-VOA on cost. Filing and extensions are on us.
