# The D12 visa: a year to scout the market

 The D12 is a multiple-entry pre-investment visa valid one or two years with unlimited entries. Each visit gives up to 180 days, extendable by another 180 — up to a year per arrival. All-in from IDR 7,500,000. The requirements are stricter than usual: a passport valid 18 months, four blank pages, and English bank statements for three months showing USD 5,000 or more.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the D12 is

 The D12 is a multiple-entry visit visa for prospective investors: people sizing up the market, choosing a niche, partners and a location before committing capital and opening a company.

 ✓Visa validity — one or two years, with unlimited entries

 ✓Each visit — up to 180 days, extendable by another 180

 ✓The longest visits of any visit visa — up to a year in the country per arrival

 ✓Converts into an investor KITAS once the company is running

 Do not confuse visa validity with permitted stay. The visa opens a window of one or two years; how long you may remain per arrival is counted separately.

## What it costs

 ✓1 year · Minimal — IDR 7,500,000, processed in 10 working days

 ✓1 year · Regular — IDR 9,500,000, processed in 5–6 working days

 ✓2 years — IDR 10,500,000 and 13,000,000 respectively

 Extending the stay by another 180 days is IDR 5,000,000 all-in. The government stay-permit fee is already inside that figure.

## Documents: where applications fail

 The D12 has stricter requirements than short visas, and this is where people lose the most time.

 ✓A passport valid 18 months or more, with at least 4 blank pages, photographed in full without cropping or objects in frame

 ✓A personal photo

 ✓Bank statements in English for the last three months showing a balance from USD 5,000 or equivalent

 ✓An invitation or official letter from a company — we provide this

 The statements must be in English and must cover three months. A rough translation or a single-date balance certificate will not do — that is the most common reason for a return.

## What the D12 does not allow

 !Working or earning income in Indonesia — a visit visa does not grant that

 !Running operations on behalf of a local company

 !Providing services to local clients

 The D12 covers reconnaissance: negotiations, site visits, market study, structuring a future business. The moment work and income begin, a residence status is required.

## The route: D12 → PT PMA → KITAS

 Groundwork on the D12Up to a year per visit: study the market, find partners and a location, assemble the structure of the future company.

 PT PMA registrationKBLI activity codes, the deed, shareholdings, tax number, licences, bank account. Explained in how to open a PT PMA.

 Paying in your stakeYour personal share of capital must be paid in and evidenced.

 Investor KITASConverted without leaving, on the founding documents and proof of your stake.

The logic is simple: the D12 buys you time to decide without living on tourist visas or running for stamps.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long can I stay on a D12?
Up to 180 days per entry, extendable by another 180 — up to a year in the country per arrival. The number of entries during the visa's validity is unlimited.

Вопрос: How much does a D12 cost?
One year: IDR 7,500,000 on the Minimal package in 10 working days, or 9,500,000 on Regular in 5–6 days. Two years: 10,500,000 and 13,000,000. Extending by 180 days is from IDR 5,000,000.

Вопрос: What bank statements are required?
In English, covering the last three months, showing a balance from USD 5,000 or equivalent. A single-date balance certificate will not be accepted.

Вопрос: Can I work on a D12?
No. It is a visit visa: work and income in Indonesia are not permitted. It covers market research and business preparation, not the activity itself.

Вопрос: How do I move from a D12 to a KITAS?
Once the PT PMA is registered and your stake paid in, the visa converts into an investor KITAS without leaving the country.

 We act as sponsor, provide the invitation, arrange the visa and run the whole path to the company and the investor KITAS.

# Deported from Bali: the real reasons

 The overwhelming majority of deportations come down to two grounds: overstaying, and working on a visa that does not permit it. Official figures for 2025 show the Ngurah Rai office alone deported 331 people, with Russians, Australians and Americans the top three nationalities. The key line is 60 days of overstay: below it a fine settles matters, above it immigration measures begin.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Two causes out of three

 Deportation from Bali comes down, in the overwhelming majority of cases, to two grounds — and both are entirely within the traveller's control.

 !Overstaying. The permit expired and the person stayed on

 !Activity outside the visa's purpose. Working, providing services or earning on a visit visa that does not allow it

 The third category is ordinary law-breaking: any offence automatically becomes an immigration matter too, because compliance with Indonesian law is a condition of every visa.

## The numbers by office

 According to official figures for 2025, the Ngurah Rai office alone — the busiest on the island — deported 331 people. Singaraja deported 28 over the same period.

 ✓The reasons cited: overstaying and criminal activity

 ✓The top three nationalities deported: Russians, Australians and Americans

 ✓Ngurah Rai covers the south: Kuta, Legian, Seminyak, Canggu, Jimbaran and Uluwatu

 If you travel on a Russian, Australian or US passport you are in the most-represented group in these figures. That is not cause for alarm but for care with your status: almost everything people are deported for is avoidable.

## The 60-day threshold

 An overstay has a clear line past which the nature of the problem changes.

 ✓Up to 60 days — settled with a fine: IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person, paid on departure

 ✓Beyond 60 days — immigration measures apply, up to deportation and a re-entry ban

 You can work out your own total in the fine calculator, and the procedure is set out in our overstay article.

## What counts as work

 This is where people who genuinely did not think of themselves as offenders come unstuck. What matters is not how much you earned or where you sat with your laptop, but where the money came from.

 !Services for Indonesian clients — photo shoots, training, consultations, lessons

 !Renting out property and brokering rentals

 !Promoting and tagging local brands, barter included

 !Selling tours, transfers and excursions

 A lawful route for remote work exists and costs less than the consequences: the E33G KITAS for 12 months. The boundaries are mapped in our piece on working remotely, legally.

## Why enforcement tightened

 Oversight on the island grew markedly through 2026, and these are structural changes rather than one-off campaigns.

 ✓Since 6 April 2026 Bali has five immigration offices instead of three — Tabanan and Klungkung were added

 ✓Round-the-clock channels now let anyone report a suspected breach

 ✓Immigration publishes deportation cases in open press releases — from stay-permit violations to foreigners running commercial activity without the right status

 The practical conclusion is simple: betting on the island being big enough to hide in has stopped working.

## If your status is already in breach

 You have more options while the situation is still fresh. What to do depends on exactly what has gone wrong.

 Overstay under 60 daysSettled with a fine on departure. The earlier you start, the calmer it goes.

 Overstay past 60 daysNot something to handle alone — you need help and a plan set out in advance.

 Wrong status, permit still validA change of status may be possible: from a visit permit it is provided for, from visa-free entry it is not.

 A re-entry banThe length and terms depend on the grounds. Prospects can only be assessed from the actual documents.

Do not leave it until after the weekend. Every day of overstay costs money and narrows the options.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: What are people most often deported from Bali for?
Overstaying and activity outside the visa's purpose — that is, working and earning on a visit visa. The third category is ordinary law-breaking, which automatically becomes an immigration matter.

Вопрос: How many people are deported from Bali in a year?
According to official figures for 2025, the Ngurah Rai office deported 331 people and Singaraja 28. Ngurah Rai is the busiest: it covers Kuta, Canggu, Jimbaran and Uluwatu.

Вопрос: Are Russians really top of the deportation figures?
Yes — official figures put Russians, Australians and Americans as the top three nationalities deported from Bali. Nearly all the grounds are avoidable: extend your status on time and do not work on a visit visa.

Вопрос: What happens after 60 days of overstay?
Up to 60 days it is settled with a fine on departure — IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person. Beyond 60 days immigration measures apply, up to deportation and a re-entry ban.

Вопрос: Does a barter brand post count as work?
If the brand is Indonesian and you receive goods or services for the post, yes. The form of payment is irrelevant; what matters is that the activity took place inside the country.

 An overstay, the wrong visa type, or a refusal already on record — describe the situation and we will tell you honestly what can be done and how fast.

# Remote work in Bali 2026: doing it legally

 Working from a laptop for foreign clients while living in Bali is lawful — but only on the right status, and the E33G exists for exactly that. What is not lawful: any income from Indonesian sources and services for local clients, including non-obvious things like renting out a villa or posting brand content for barter. The line is drawn by where the income comes from, not where you work.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Where the line runs

 The rule is simple and rests on one thing — where the money comes from. Not where you sit with your laptop, and not how many hours you put in.

 ✓Working for a foreign employer or foreign clients — allowed

 ✓Income arriving from outside Indonesia — allowed

 ✓Ordinary resident life: renting, travelling, banking — allowed

 !Any income from Indonesian sources — not allowed

 !Services for Indonesian clients — not allowed, even one-off

 !Trading inside the country — not allowed

## The grey areas people miss

 These catch more people than obvious employment does. Formally they are work inside the country, even if it does not feel that way:

 !Advertising your villa for rent or looking for a housemate

 !Promoting and tagging brands on Instagram — including for barter, with no money involved

 !Photo shoots, training sessions, consultations and lessons for local clients

 !Selling tours, transfers and excursions

 !Managing someone else's property or brokering rentals

 Barter and 'doing a friend a favour' do not persuade immigration: what counts is that an activity took place inside the country, not how it was paid for. No bank transfer does not make the service free in an inspector's eyes.

## Why this is being watched more closely

 Oversight of foreigners in Bali has tightened noticeably. According to immigration, in 2025 the Ngurah Rai office alone deported 331 people and Singaraja 28, with overstaying and activity outside the visa's purpose among the leading reasons.

 ✓In 2026 the island moved to five immigration offices instead of three — coverage is denser

 ✓Round-the-clock channels now exist for anyone to report a suspected breach

 ✓Checks are not limited to paperwork: a foreigner's public activity is visible too

 The practical conclusion: betting on not being noticed has stopped working. Holding a status that explicitly permits what you actually do is cheaper and calmer.

## The right setup

 There is a dedicated status for remote work with foreign clients — the E33G.

 ✓12 months of residence, with free entry and exit

 ✓IDR 12,000,000 all-in, issued in 7–9 working days

 ✓Three documents: passport, selfie, address

 ✓A local bank account and family KITAS for your spouse and children

 The full breakdown is in our piece on the E33G KITAS. If your income comes from Indonesian sources the E33G will not cover it: you need a work KITAS for employment or an investor KITAS for your own business through a PT PMA.

## If you are already here on the wrong status

 It is a common situation: you arrived on a tourist visa, the work stretched on, and your status no longer matches reality. There are three routes, and which applies depends heavily on how you entered.

 ✓Entered on an e-VOA or C1 — changing status to a KITAS is provided for, and you need not leave. The procedure is not quick, so start early rather than a week before your permit ends

 ✓Entered visa-free — a change of status is prohibited outright. Only leaving and re-entering on the right visa

 ✓Already overstayed — the overstay is settled first, and only then does the status question get resolved

 What you should definitely not do is leave it to the final days. An extension must be filed no later than the day your current permit ends, and a change of status needs time to prepare. An overstay costs IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person and damages your record for future applications.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I work remotely while living in Bali on a tourist visa?
No. Visit visas — the e-VOA, C1 and D-series — carry no right to work at all. For remote work with foreign clients there is a separate status, the E33G.

Вопрос: Does promoting a brand on Instagram count as work?
If the brand is Indonesian and you receive money or goods for the post, yes — that is activity inside the country. Barter does not rescue the situation: what matters is the service, not how it was paid for.

Вопрос: Can I rent out my villa?
Renting out property is income from an Indonesian source and is not covered by the E33G. That activity has to be structured separately — we will go through it on a consultation.

Вопрос: What happens if I work without the right status?
It breaches the purpose of your stay. Sanctions range from a fine to deportation with a re-entry ban. According to immigration, activity outside a visa's purpose is one of the main causes of deportation from Bali.

Вопрос: Can I arrange an E33G while already on the island?
Yes, if your current status allows it: from a visit permit a change of status is provided for. From visa-free entry it is not — you would have to leave and re-enter.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

 We look at where your income actually comes from and tell you plainly which status settles it. The E33G is IDR 12,000,000 all-in.

# Passport rules 2026: six months or eighteen

 For an e-VOA, visa-free entry and the C1, C2 and C6 visas your passport must be valid for at least six months on the date of entry. Annual D-series multiple-entry visas are stricter: 18 months and at least four blank pages. A separate rule covers travel documents other than a national passport — at least 12 months.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How long your passport must be valid

 There is no single answer — the threshold depends on the visa. Count it from your date of entry, not the date you apply.

 Visa | 
 Passport | 

 e-VOA / VOA | 6 months or more | 

 C1, C2, C6 | 6 months or more | 

 D1, D2, D12 (annual) | 18 months or more, plus 4 blank pages | 

 Visa-free entry | 6 months or more | 

 KITAS | enough to cover the whole permit and then some | 

## The special cases

 Two requirements are rarely written about and regularly catch people out:

 !Travel documents other than a national passport — a temporary or emergency passport, a certificate of identity, a laissez-passer and the like — must be valid for at least 12 months, not six

 !Stateless applicants additionally attach a re-entry permit for the country of application and a return or onward ticket

 For annual D-series visas a passport with 'just over a year' left will not do: you need 18 months at the time of filing. Renew early if a multiple-entry visa is in your plans.

## Blank pages

 The minimum of four free pages applies to annual D-series visas. Free means without stamps or visas — the cover and the data page do not count.

 ✓Count the pages before filing, not after paying

 ✓Stamps from neighbouring countries eat pages faster than you expect

 ✓If you are short on pages, the only fix is a new passport

## The chip and the autogate

 A biometric passport is not needed for the visa but for speed at the border. With a chip and an approved electronic visa the autogate works: the system reads the chip and matches your face, clearing you in 15–25 seconds.

 ✓The chip symbol is on the passport cover

 ✓Children aged 6 and over may use it, subject to the usual requirements

 ✓With a child under 6, one parent goes through a staffed counter

 The whole arrival process is covered in our piece on the autogate and All Indonesia.

## Where applications fail

 In our experience almost every refusal and delay comes from small things that are visible in advance.

 !The name is spelled differently from the passport. One letter out and the application goes back for correction

 !The passport expires before the threshold. Count from the entry date, not the filing date

 !A poor scan. Glare, cropped corners, a shadow across the page — a common reason for a return

 !A photo that misses the spec. It must be recent, taken within the last year

 If a problem is found after filing, immigration allows 2 days from the notice to fix it. Miss that and the application is rejected, and you start again with a new payment.

## What else is asked for besides the passport

 ✓A return or onward ticket — checked by the airline at boarding and by immigration on arrival

 ✓Proof of accommodation: a booking or an address

 ✓For the C6 visa — three months of bank statements in the name of the foreigner or the sponsor

 ✓The All Indonesia declaration, filed online before landing

 ✓Bali's tourist levy of IDR 150,000 through the Love Bali portal

 We send the full list for your specific visa after a short consultation — it varies not only by visa type but by your circumstances.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long must my passport be valid for Bali?
For an e-VOA, visa-free entry and the C1, C2 and C6 visas — at least 6 months on the date of entry. For annual D-series multiple-entry visas the rule is stricter: 18 months and at least 4 blank pages.

Вопрос: How many blank pages do I need?
For annual D-series visas, at least four free pages — meaning no stamps or visas on them. Short visas have no such hard rule, but a couple of free pages are needed regardless.

Вопрос: Do I need a biometric passport?
Not to obtain a visa. But the chip is what lets you use the autogate: with it and an approved electronic visa the border takes 15–25 seconds instead of a queue.

Вопрос: What if my passport expires in 7 months?
That is enough for an e-VOA and short visas. For an annual D1 or D2 it is not — those need 18 months. Renew before you file rather than mid-process.

Вопрос: Why was I refused over the spelling of my name?
The application must match the passport character for character. A single letter out means a return for correction, and you get only two days to make it.

## We will check your passport before you file

 Send a photo of the data page and we will tell you whether it clears the visa you want, and flag the risks before you pay.

# Driving in Bali: the licence you actually need

 A tourist needs a valid national licence plus an international driving permit obtained at home before the trip — the national licence alone is not enough. A resident holding a KITAS or KITAP can obtain an Indonesian SIM. The recurring confusion is the SIM Internasional: that document is for driving abroad and requires an Indonesian licence and a KITAP.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Three documents people confuse

 Half the trouble in Bali comes from three different documents all being called 'a licence'.

 ✓Your home country licence — on its own it is not valid in Indonesia

 ✓An IDP, the international driving permit — issued in your own country and valid alongside your national licence

 ✓A SIM — an Indonesian licence, issued by the Indonesian police

 The specific trap is the SIM Internasional. That is Indonesia's own version of an IDP, issued by Korlantas for driving abroad. It does nothing for a visitor: obtaining one requires a valid Indonesian licence and a KITAP.

## What a tourist needs

 The setup is simple and the same whether you take a bike or a car:

 Your national licenceA valid licence from your own country is the foundation; nothing else works without it.

 An IDP from homeThe international driving permit is issued at home, before the trip. You cannot get one in Indonesia.

 The right categoryA motorbike needs a motorbike category. A car-only licence does not cover a bike — and that is also grounds for an insurer to decline.

 !Riding on your national licence alone, without an IDP, is a breach

 !'Everyone does it' persuades neither the police nor an insurer after a crash

 !Rental shops often do not check, but the liability sits with the rider, not with them

## What a resident can get

 If you hold a KITAS or KITAP you can obtain an Indonesian SIM — more convenient than carrying an IDP.

 ✓An immigration document is required: a KITAP for permanent residents, a KITAS for specialists and students

 ✓Your passport — original and copy

 ✓A minimum age, a health certificate and psychological testing

 ✓An examination: theory and practical

 The requirements are published by the regional traffic police; the exact document set and testing procedure are worth confirming at your own Satpas, as practice varies between regions.

 Address registration — SKTT and STM — is done in the first 14 days after your KITAS is issued, and without it this step can stall.

## Categories and motorbikes

 The most common mistake in Bali is getting on a bike with a car-only licence.

 !The category must match the vehicle: a motorbike needs the motorbike class, a car the car class

 !After a crash, a category mismatch becomes a problem immediately — with the police and with your insurer

 !A 125cc scooter is still a motorbike, not a 'bicycle with an engine'

 A helmet is mandatory, and not as a formality: fines for riding without one are issued routinely, and in a fall it decides the outcome.

## At a check and after a crash

 Documents are checked selectively, but they are checked. Knowing the drill in advance beats working it out at the roadside.

 ✓Carry your national licence and IDP together — separately they do not work

 ✓Photos on your phone do not replace the originals

 ✓Helmets are mandatory for rider and passenger alike

 After a crash, a category mismatch or a missing IDP becomes a problem on two fronts at once: with the police, and with an insurer entitled to decline. Which is why the exclusions in your policy are worth reading before you get on the bike, not after.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I drive in Bali on my home country licence?
No, not on its own. You need your national licence plus an international driving permit (IDP) obtained in your own country before the trip.

Вопрос: Where do I get an IDP?
Only in your own country, before you fly. Indonesia will not issue an international permit to a visitor — the local SIM Internasional is issued under different conditions.

Вопрос: What is the SIM Internasional and will it work for me?
It is Indonesia's version of an IDP, for driving abroad. Obtaining one requires a valid Indonesian licence and a KITAP, so it does not suit a tourist.

Вопрос: Can I get an Indonesian licence on a KITAS?
Yes — an immigration document is part of the requirements: a KITAP for permanent residents, a KITAS for specialists and students. A passport, health certificate, psychological testing and an exam are also required.

Вопрос: Do I need a separate category for a scooter?
Yes. A scooter is a motorbike, and a car-only licence does not cover it. A category mismatch causes problems both at a check and with your insurer.

## Sort the status and the rest gets easier

 A KITAS opens up a local licence, a bank account and life without the visa routine. Tell us about your situation.

# E33G KITAS 2026: a year in Bali, no border runs

 The E33G is a residence permit for remote work with foreign clients. It gives 12 months of residence with free entry and exit, family KITAS and a local bank account. All-in IDR 12,000,000, issued in 7–9 working days, with three files from you plus an employment contract and proof of income. The key restriction: your income must be foreign.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the E33G gives you

 The E33G is a residence permit for people working remotely for clients outside Indonesia. It is not a tourist visa with a longer term but a full resident status for 12 months: it ends the border runs and the monthly extension routine.

 ✓12 months of residence in Indonesia

 ✓Free entry and exit with no limits — leaving does not cancel it

 ✓Family KITAS for your spouse and children

 ✓An Indonesian bank account

 ✓Applying for Schengen, Japanese and other visas from inside Indonesia

## Where the line is drawn

 The E33G has one restriction, but a firm one: your income must come from abroad. Anything earned inside the country falls outside the status.

 !You may work only for a foreign company or foreign clients

 !Income from Indonesian sources is prohibited — local clients included

 !Trading and providing services inside the country is not allowed

 In practice this is where people come unstuck: renting out a villa, filming commercial content for local businesses, selling tours and consulting for Indonesian clients all count as working in the country. A detailed look at the grey areas is in Working remotely from Bali, legally.
Working on a tourist visa is one of the leading causes of deportation from Bali. The E33G exists precisely to move remote workers out of that risk zone.

## Documents: what you actually need

 The pack is far shorter than for most residence statuses, and that is part of the E33G's appeal. Three files come from you:

 ✓A photo of your passport spread — valid for at least 6 months

 ✓A selfie on a light or red background

 ✓Your address in Indonesia — plain text is enough

 Then there is what we prepare together: an employment contract with a company registered outside Indonesia, and proof of income of at least USD 60,000 per year. Immigration separately looks at a three-month bank statement, which must show at least USD 2,000 remaining as living funds. This is not a formality — the wording of the contract is where applications most often get sent back. The figure has to be visible in the contract, not merely implied by the fact of employment.

 Do not guess the requirements from an article. Immigration looks at the specific documents of a specific person, and the wording shifts over time. Message our consultant and we will explain what applies to your case: what the contract must state and which statement will work.

 The all-in price is IDR 12,000,000 and processing takes 7–9 working days. The issued visa has a shelf life: you must enter Indonesia within 90 days of it being issued, otherwise it lapses and has to be applied for again.

## Two ways to apply

 Offshore KITASIf you are outside Indonesia. Takes 7–9 working days and is the default route when applying from abroad.

 Onshore KITASIf you are already in Bali — a switch from your current visa without leaving the country. The route depends on the document you currently hold.

Check your current status first. From a C1 visa the conversion is direct. From an e-VOA there is no direct switch: it runs through an intermediate Bridging Visa, a separate procedure with its own cost. From visa-free entry it is not possible at all: you would have to leave and come back. That affects citizens of Kazakhstan and Belarus, who have been visa-free since July 2026.

 Do not leave it to the last week. A conversion has to be filed while at least 30 days remain on your current visa. With less time than that, the only route left is flying out and applying for an offshore KITAS.

## E33G versus the alternatives

 The useful comparison is where your money comes from and how much of the year you actually spend here.

 ✓Working for foreign clients and living on the island — the E33G is your status

 ✓In Indonesia for up to six months — a C1 visa is cheaper, up to 180 consecutive days

 ✓Flying in often but based elsewhere — a D1 or D2 multiple-entry visa

 ✓Working for an Indonesian company — you need a work KITAS; the E33G will not do

 ✓Running your own business here — the investor KITAS

## Doing the maths for a year

 The E33G costs IDR 12,000,000 for 12 months. Compare that with what a year on visit visas actually costs.

 ✓A C1 visa — from IDR 2,500,000, giving 60 days. Add two extensions at IDR 2,500,000 each and that is 180 days and no less than IDR 7,500,000 per half-year

 ✓For a full year you need two such cycles — from IDR 15,000,000, with a mandatory departure in between

 ✓The E33G — IDR 12,000,000, twelve months, and not a single flight out

 So on money the E33G works out cheaper than a chain of tourist visas, and on peace of mind there is no comparison: no extensions every two months, no border runs, no risk of missing a date. The status also brings a bank account and family KITAS, which a visit visa will never give you.

## What happens after a year

 The E33G is extendable — and this is the point the market is still confused about. Some agencies write that it cannot be extended; others quote different maximum terms. The official extension table for stay permits reads as follows: the first permit runs for a year, an extension is granted for no longer than the first term, and the total time on a KITAS can reach six years. After that it is either a different status or a KITAP.

 With us an extension costs IDR 12,000,000 — the same as issuing the permit in the first place. The timing matters more than the money here, because getting it wrong costs more than the service itself.

 ✓The filing window is the last 30 days of your permit: no earlier than 30 days before it expires and no later than the day it does. File sooner and it will simply not be accepted

 ✓You must be in Indonesia to file — an extension is an in-country procedure

 ✓In our experience it takes 3–4 weeks, and you should not plan a trip out of the country during that time. Formally the extension is filed online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id, but in Bali an office visit and biometrics are usually added

 ✓The grounds are the same as at application — a live contract and documented income do not go away

 The most expensive mistake with an E33G. If your KITAS expires while you are abroad, it stops working: you cannot return on it and will be applying for a new visa from outside the country, paying in full again. It also stays open in the immigration database — closing it still requires a separate ERP procedure, and without that a new visa will not be issued. That is exactly why we track our clients' dates in a CRM — nobody holds this deadline in their head.

 There is one more scenario — when the status is no longer needed because you are leaving for good or moving to a different KITAS. Flying out and forgetting about it does not work: the permit has to be closed officially. We covered how in our guide to EPO and ERP.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Will I have to pay tax in Indonesia?
That depends on how long you spend in the country, not on your visa type. You become an Indonesian tax resident if you live here or spend more than 183 days in any 12 months. A resident must register for tax (obtain an NPWP) and file a return, and in the general case worldwide income is declared, not just Indonesian income. A territorial-income relief does exist in the legislation, but it is targeted: it is designed for foreign specialists in certain occupations and for researchers, and it requires a separate application and approval from the tax office. It does not apply to a remote worker on an E33G by default, so claims along the lines of "there is no tax on the E33G" are a simplification you should not rely on. Work out your actual position with a tax adviser, taking your country's double taxation treaty into account.

Вопрос: Can the E33G be extended, and for how many years?
Yes, it is extendable. Under the official extension table for stay permits the total time on a KITAS reaches six years. An extension is filed no earlier than 30 days before the current permit expires and no later than the day it does. With us it costs IDR 12,000,000. The procedure runs in-country and takes 3–4 weeks, during which you cannot leave.

Вопрос: Do I qualify if I am self-employed or freelance?
The baseline E33G scenario is a contract with a foreign company. Freelance cases are assessed individually: much depends on how your income is structured and what you can document. Write to us and we will give you an honest read.

Вопрос: How much does the E33G cost and how long does it take?
IDR 12,000,000 all-in, with processing in 7–9 working days. That covers preparation, filing and support through to the status being issued.

Вопрос: Can I take projects from Indonesian clients?
No. The E33G covers foreign-source income only. Working for local clients, trading and providing services inside the country are not permitted on this status.

Вопрос: Can I switch to an E33G while already in Bali?
Yes, if your current status allows it. From a C1 visa the conversion is direct; from an e-VOA it runs through an intermediate Bridging Visa. From visa-free entry it is not possible: you would need to leave and re-enter. In every case at least 30 days must remain on your current visa.

Вопрос: Can I bring my family?
Yes. A spouse is covered by code E31B and children under 18 by code E31E. These are separate visas with their own cost: IDR 11,000,000 with us. They are filed once your own E33G has been issued and run until your status expires. You will need a marriage or birth certificate with a sworn translation into Indonesian if the document is not in English.

 We check whether your case fits the E33G and tell you honestly if it does not. All-in IDR 12,000,000.

# EPO and ERP: how to close a KITAS properly

 A KITAS does not close itself — not when you leave for good, and not when it expires. While the permit sits active in the immigration database, you cannot apply for a new Indonesian visa, not even a visa on arrival. There are two procedures: EPO if you are still in Indonesia, ERP if you have already left. With us either one costs IDR 1,500,000.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Reviewed by the Malina Visa team

## Why you cannot simply abandon a KITAS

 The logic of “it expires, so it goes away” does not hold. Your stay permit lives in the immigration database independently of where you physically are, and closing it is a human action, not a calendar event.

 !An unclosed KITAS stays active in the system — even if you flew out a year ago

 !While it is active you cannot get a new visa. That includes the eVOA many people count on as a fallback

 !If the KITAS expires while you are abroad and nothing has been filed, an overstay record may appear against you

 !Your sponsor stays formally attached to the permit, so the questions land on them too

 This surfaces later and at the worst moment: when you decide to come back and apply for a new visa. Unwinding the history after the fact costs more time and money than closing the permit on time.

## EPO: if you are still in Indonesia

 EPO (Exit Permit Only) is the procedure for people still inside the country. Immigration cancels the KITAS and gives you a window to fly out.

 ✓You have 7 days to depart once it is issued — miss the window and overstay begins

 ✓Your passport is physically submitted to the immigration office, so you cannot travel while it is being processed

 ✓The KITAS is cancelled immediately — you cannot come back on it, any return needs a new visa

 ✓It applies to an expired KITAS too — a common misconception is that an expired permit needs no closure. It does

 Do not book the flight first. Procedure first, ticket second. While your passport sits with immigration you physically cannot fly, and public holidays stretch the timeline easily. A ticket for the day after tomorrow is the most common source of panic in this process.

## ERP: if you have already flown out

 ERP (Exit Re-entry Permit) covers the case where you are already outside Indonesia with a KITAS left open. It is handled remotely: you stay abroad, your agent or sponsor files here.

 ✓You do not need to be present — everything is done in Indonesia under your authorisation

 ✓The KITAS is closed — the permit is cancelled exactly as it would be under EPO

 ✓You cannot return on it — despite the words “re-entry” in the name, this is a closure procedure, not a way back

 ✓You will need your ticket and exit stamp — proof that you actually left the country

 About the name. The acronym is misleading: historically “exit re-entry permit” meant permission to leave and come back. In KITAS closure practice, however, ERP refers to the offshore cancellation procedure. Returning on a closed KITAS is not possible — if you plan to come back, what you need is a new visa, not an ERP.

## Which one applies to you

 You are in IndonesiaEPO. Close the permit and fly out within 7 days.

 You have already leftERP. We close it remotely, no need for you to be here.

 You want to returnNeither helps with that — you need a new visa. The old permit still has to be closed.

 Both procedures cost IDR 1,500,000 with us. The only difference is where you physically are when it is filed.

## When closing the KITAS is mandatory

 There are more situations than “leaving for good”. Closure is required whenever an old permit has to make room for a new one.

 ✓Leaving Indonesia permanently — even with six months still left on the KITAS

 ✓Switching KITAS type — for example from E33G to an investor KITAS after setting up a company. The new permit will not be issued while the old one is live

 ✓Changing employers — a work KITAS does not transfer between companies. The old one closes, the new one starts from scratch

 ✓Closing the company that sponsored you — PT liquidation and closing the attached KITAS go together

## What to settle before closing

 A KITAS drags a tail of things attached to it, and they are easier to close while the permit is still valid.

 ✓Bank account — it is tied to your permit. Once cancelled, access can be restricted with your money still inside. More on accounts

 ✓Tax — if you were a tax resident, a final filing and your NPWP status remain to be handled. Do not leave this to sort out from abroad

 ✓Family KITAS — your spouse’s and children’s permits are tied to yours and close with it

 ✓Rentals, vehicles, subscriptions — anything registered with your KITAS details and address

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I just fly out and leave the KITAS open?
You will most likely pass through departures — an active permit does not block you. The problem comes later: the KITAS stays live in the database, and you cannot apply for a new Indonesian visa until it is closed. You will end up filing the same procedure anyway, only remotely and under more stress.

Вопрос: My KITAS expired on its own. Do I still need to close it?
Yes. This is the most common misconception. Expiry is not closure: the record stays in the system and has to be cleared by procedure. Both EPO and ERP can be filed on an expired permit.

Вопрос: How long does it take?
Expect several working days, plus the departure window in the case of EPO. The exact timing depends on the immigration office and its workload, so we quote it after reviewing your case rather than upfront. Do not plan a tight departure: public holidays stretch the schedule.

Вопрос: Can I come back to Indonesia after EPO or ERP?
Yes, but on a new visa. A closed KITAS cannot be revived and gives no right of entry. Closing a permit properly does not harm your record — quite the opposite, a cleanly closed KITAS makes future applications easier. It is the abandoned one that looks bad.

Вопрос: How much does it cost?
IDR 1,500,000 per procedure, for both EPO and ERP. If you also need to close the sponsoring company or arrange a new status, we will quote the whole thing together.

Вопрос: Can I get an EPO at the airport before my flight?
No. An EPO is processed at the immigration office covering your registered address, in advance, with your passport physically submitted. There is no same-day or airport option.

## We’ll close your KITAS properly

 Tell us where you are right now — in Indonesia or already abroad — and we’ll name the procedure, the timeline and the documents. IDR 1,500,000.

# Bali e-VOA 2026: your visa before you fly

 The e-VOA is an electronic visa on arrival arranged online before departure. It gives 30 days with one 30-day extension — 60 days maximum per entry. The government fee is currently IDR 500,000; our all-in price is IDR 900,000. Its main advantage over a visa bought at the airport: no payment queue, and the autogate works.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the e-VOA is and who it suits

 The e-VOA is a visa on arrival arranged in advance through the government portal. On paper it is the same B-series visa issued at the airport, but it reaches you by email before departure, and at the border you show nothing but your passport.

 ✓Tourism and holidays — the main scenario

 ✓Visiting family and friends

 ✓Business meetings, negotiations, conferences and exhibitions

 ✓Transit through Indonesia with a stop in the city

 !You cannot work on an e-VOA — not employed, not freelancing for local clients

 !Studying and journalism are not covered by this visa either

 !Selling services and running day-to-day operations belongs to business visas

## e-VOA versus a visa at the airport

 The status is formally identical. The difference is what happens after the plane lands.

 ✓No payment queue. The visa is already tied to your passport; you go straight to passport control

 ✓The autogate works. With a biometric passport, clearance takes 15–25 seconds

 ✓Extending is simpler. Visa, passport and entry record are linked electronically from the start

 ✓Refusals surface early. A document problem shows up at home, not at the border after a 12-hour flight

 The price gap is about to widen. On 12 August 2026 immigration announced plans to raise the fee: IDR 750,000 for a visa arranged online before departure and IDR 1,000,000 for one obtained at the airport. Both currently cost IDR 500,000. No effective date has been set, but the direction is clear: arranging in advance will save you a quarter of a million rupiah, not just some queueing.

## Timing: 30 plus 30, and not a day more

 The e-VOA gives you 30 calendar days from the date of entry. It can be extended exactly once, by exactly 30 days — 60 days maximum per entry. There is no second extension.
The extension fee is IDR 500,000. You may file no earlier than 14 days before your current permit ends and no later than the day it ends. Processing takes up to 3 working days after payment, and the new period starts the day after the old one, so no days are lost.

 !Need more than 60 consecutive days? The e-VOA will not do — take a C1 visa from the start

 !An overstay costs IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person

 !Leaving and returning for a fresh e-VOA is technically possible, but frequent visa runs draw attention at the border

## What you need to apply

 The list is short, which is part of why this visa is so popular:

 ✓A passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry

 ✓A scan of the passport photo page

 ✓A photo — an ordinary one, no studio requirements

 ✓A return or onward ticket

 ✓Your address in Indonesia

 We arrange the e-VOA all-in for IDR 900,000: we check the documents before filing, submit, pay and send the finished visa to your inbox. That pre-check is not a formality — the most common causes of refusal are a name spelled differently from the passport and a passport with under six months left.

## The autogate: crossing the border in 20 seconds

 The automated gates on arrival in Denpasar and Jakarta work with a biometric passport and an approved electronic visa. The system reads the chip and matches your face — immigration reports clearance in 15–25 seconds.

 ✓You need a chipped passport — look for the symbol on the cover

 ✓Children aged 6 and over may use it, subject to the usual requirements

 ✓With a child under 6, one parent goes through a staffed counter

 ✓The All Indonesia declaration is filed online before landing

 Separately from the visa, Bali's tourist levy of IDR 150,000 is paid through the Love Bali portal. Details in our piece on the Love Bali levy.

## What if 60 days is not enough

 Two routes, and you choose before you fly — changing your mind inside the country is harder and costs more.

 ✓The C1 visa — 60 days on entry, extendable in 60-day steps up to six months. From IDR 2,500,000. Compared with the e-VOA in C1 or e-VOA

 ✓D1 and D2 multiple-entry visas — a year of entries, up to 60 days each. From IDR 5,000,000

 ✓E33G — if you work remotely for foreign clients: a year without extensions

 One important difference between the e-VOA and visa-free entry: from an e-VOA you can change status to a limited stay permit. With visa-free entry that is not possible at all — worth knowing for citizens of Kazakhstan and Belarus, who since July 2026 need no visa for tourism.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How does the e-VOA differ from a visa at the airport?
The status is the same — a B-series visa for 30 days. The process differs: the e-VOA is arranged online before departure, so you skip the payment queue, can use the autogate, and learn about any document problem in advance rather than at the border.

Вопрос: How many times can an e-VOA be extended?
Once, by 30 days. The maximum per entry is 60 days. The extension fee is IDR 500,000, filed no earlier than 14 days before expiry and no later than the day it expires.

Вопрос: How much does an e-VOA cost?
The government fee is currently IDR 500,000. Our all-in price is IDR 900,000, which covers document checking, filing, payment and the finished visa in your inbox. Immigration has announced plans to raise the fee to IDR 750,000 for online applications; no date has been set.

Вопрос: Can I work on an e-VOA?
No. The visa covers tourism, visiting family and business meetings, but not work — neither employment nor freelancing. For remote work with foreign clients there is the E33G; for employment in Indonesia, a work KITAS.

Вопрос: Can I convert an e-VOA into a KITAS without leaving?
Yes, changing status from a visit permit to a limited stay permit is provided for. That sets the e-VOA apart from visa-free entry, where a change of status is prohibited outright. The procedure is not quick, so plan ahead.

## We will arrange your e-VOA for IDR 900,000 — in your inbox before departure

 We check your documents before filing, submit, and send the finished visa. If 60 days will not be enough, we will say so up front and suggest a C1.

# Extending an e-VOA in Bali: step by step

 The e-VOA extends exactly once, by exactly 30 days — a 60-day ceiling per entry. The fee is IDR 500,000, filed no earlier than 14 days before expiry and no later than the day itself, processed within 3 working days of payment. Filing is online, but one office visit for the photo is mandatory.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How much you can extend

 The visa on arrival gives 30 days and extends exactly once by another 30 — 60 days maximum. There is no second extension at any price.

 ✓Arrival and departure days each count as full days

 ✓The new period starts the day after the old one — no days are lost

 ✓You cannot obtain a fresh visa without leaving: after 60 days you fly out

 !The index-F VOA, which gives 7 days, cannot be extended at all

 !Planning beyond 60 days? Take a C1 from the start, before you fly

## When to file

 Two deadlines here, and confusing them is expensive.

 ✓No earlier than 14 days before your current permit ends — the system will not accept it sooner

 ✓No later than the day the permit expires

 ✓Processing takes up to 3 working days from receipt of payment

 The key point: no overstay accrues provided payment clears before the current permit expires — even if the office visit happens later. Which is why you pay with several working days to spare, not on the last day.

## How it works

 Apply onlineThrough the government portal: a passport scan, a sponsor's guarantee letter if you have one, and a statement of purpose.

 PayThe fee is IDR 500,000. From that moment an overstay is off the table.

 NotificationThe office confirms receipt electronically and books you in.

 Photo at the officeThe photo is part of the procedure — the one mandatory visit. It takes a few minutes.

 IssueThe extended permit arrives electronically; there is no paper to collect.

If a problem is found in your documents you get 2 days from the notice to fix it. Miss that and the application is rejected, and you start again with a new payment.

## Which office

 Your application goes to the office whose working area covers your address. Bali has five: Denpasar, Ngurah Rai, Singaraja, Tabanan and Klungkung — the last two opened in April 2026.
The zones and how the visit runs are covered in our immigration offices article. You cannot use a more convenient office — the link is your address.

## Yourself or through an agency

 The portal is open to everyone and you can technically file yourself. The difference is the cost of a mistake.

 ✓On your own: the portal, payment, correspondence, status tracking and the visit are all yours

 ✓With us: we file and pay early, watch the dates and book you at the right office. You come in once, for the photo

 On money: the IDR 500,000 fee is a government charge and is the same either way. Immigration has announced plans to raise the visa-on-arrival tariff — the detail is in our e-VOA guide.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How many times can an e-VOA be extended?
Once, by exactly 30 days. The maximum per entry is 60 days. There is no second extension and you cannot obtain a fresh visa without leaving.

Вопрос: How far ahead should I file the extension?
No earlier than 14 days before your current permit expires and no later than the day it does. Processing takes up to 3 working days after payment, so leave yourself room.

Вопрос: How much does the extension cost?
The government fee is IDR 500,000 per application — the official rate for a 30-day stay permit. Turnkey with us the extension costs IDR 950,000, that fee included, with nothing to top up at the office.

Вопрос: Do I have to attend the office in person?
Yes, once: the photo is part of the procedure. Everything else — filing, payment, issue — happens electronically.

Вопрос: What if I miss the filing deadline?
An overstay begins at IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person. Retroactive extensions are not possible: applications are accepted only up to the day the permit expires.

 We file early, pay before expiry and book you at the right office. The dates are our problem.

# Family KITAS 2026: for spouses and children

 The family KITAS is a residence permit for foreign spouses of Indonesian citizens and for the spouses and children of KITAS or KITAP holders. It comes in two stages: a VITAS entry visa first, then conversion to a KITAS with biometrics after arrival. It renews annually without leaving the country. It carries no right to work, but children may attend school.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Who the family KITAS is for

 This is a residence permit for people whose family is tied to Indonesia. The whole household lives here lawfully under one clear status, rather than on a chain of tourist visas.

 ✓Foreign spouses of Indonesian citizens and their minor children

 ✓Spouses and children of foreigners who already hold a KITAS or KITAP — for the term of the sponsor's document

 ✓Children are registered on a KITAS up to and including age 17

 The sponsor is either an Indonesian spouse or a family member holding a valid KITAS or KITAP. A family KITAS cannot be issued on its own — without a sponsor there is no basis for it.

## What the status changes day to day

 The difference from a visit visa is not only the term — the set of things you can actually do changes.

 ✓An Indonesian bank account

 ✓A driving licence

 ✓School for the children — studying on a family KITAS is allowed

 ✓Annual renewal without having to leave the country

 !A family KITAS carries no right to employment in Indonesia

 !Paid employment requires a separate work KITAS

 !Running your own business goes through the investor KITAS

## How the process works

 It runs in two stages, and you must enter on the correct visa — arriving and sorting it out later does not work here.

 VITAS entry visaIssued on the basis of the sponsor's documents and proof of marriage or parentage.

 Arrival on the VITASYou enter Indonesia on that visa, not on a tourist one.

 Conversion to KITASAfter arrival the VITAS becomes a KITAS: a photo and fingerprints at the immigration office covering your address.

 Annual renewalFrom then on the status is renewed each year, with no need to leave the country.

Which office is yours depends on your address: Bali has five, explained in our piece on immigration offices.

## Documents

 ✓A passport with plenty of validity left

 ✓A marriage certificate with an English translation

 ✓Children's birth certificates with English translations

 ✓Sponsor's documents: passport or KTP, their KITAS or KITAP, and proof of funds

 Translations are a common source of delay. Marriage and birth certificates are needed specifically with English translations; the exact list depends on who the sponsor is, and we send it after a short consultation.

## The route to permanent residence

 The family KITAS is not a dead end. After two years of official marriage to an Indonesian citizen you may apply for KITAP, permanent residence.

 ✓KITAP removes the annual renewals and gives a more settled status

 ✓Conditions, timelines and process are covered in our article on KITAP

 ✓For families of KITAS holders, the route to KITAP depends on the sponsor's own status

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Who can sponsor a family KITAS?
An Indonesian spouse, or a family member holding a valid KITAS or KITAP. This status cannot be issued without a sponsor.

Вопрос: Can I work on a family KITAS?
No, it carries no right to employment. Paid work needs a work KITAS and your own business an investor KITAS. Children, however, may attend school.

Вопрос: Up to what age can children be included?
Children are registered on a KITAS up to and including age 17. Older children are considered separately.

Вопрос: Do I have to leave the country to renew?
No. The family KITAS renews annually without leaving Indonesia. The only travel involved is at the first stage, since entry is made on a VITAS.

Вопрос: When can I apply for KITAP?
After two years of official marriage to an Indonesian citizen you become eligible to apply for KITAP, permanent residence.

## We will gather the documents and run both stages

 We check who can sponsor you, advise on translations, and take you from the VITAS through to the KITAS and the first renewal.

# Indonesia Golden Visa 2026: amounts, terms, categories

 The Golden Visa (the E28 index family) grants Indonesian residency for 5 or 10 years at once — no sponsor, no annual renewals. A private investor who does not set up a company places USD 350,000 for five years or USD 700,000 for ten; a company founder, USD 2,500,000 and USD 5,000,000. Filing is fully online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id, and the money must be placed within 90 days of the ITAS being issued.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the Golden Visa actually gives you

 This is neither a tourist status nor another one-year KITAS. The Golden Visa is a separate branch of Indonesian immigration law for investors, where capital — not a sponsor — is the ground for residency. Hence the package:

 ✓A stay permit for 5 or 10 years straight away, renewable for a further term

 ✓No sponsor at all: no employer, no local guarantor company

 ✓Multiple entries and exits for the whole validity, with the re-entry permit issued alongside the visa

 ✓No minimum physical presence — the status does not lapse if you are away for months

 ✓Spouse and minor children receive linked statuses for the same horizon

 ✓Fully online filing, with no immigration-office visit to collect the ITAS

 One important limit: the Golden Visa is not a work permit. You may run and sign for your own company, but you cannot take salaried employment with an Indonesian employer — that needs a work KITAS.

## How much you need to invest

 The threshold depends on who you are to Indonesia: a passive investor, a business founder, a corporation, or a participant in the new capital project. The figures below are confirmed by the Directorate General of Immigration's official clarification dated 2 February 2026.

 E28C · no company set up

 USD 350,000

 for 5 years · USD 700,000 for 10 years

 Indonesian government bonds

 Listed shares and mutual fund units

 Deposit with a state bank (Mandiri, BNI, BRI)

 The most common route for an individual

 E28B · company founder

 USD 2,500,000

 for 5 years · USD 5,000,000 for 10 years

 Investment into your own Indonesian company

 Several times the passive threshold

 For a smaller business, an investor KITAS makes more sense

 E28D · corporate investor

 USD 25,000,000

 for 5 years · USD 50,000,000 for 10 years

 The investor is a legal entity, not a person

 The company nominates executives for the status

 E28F · new capital (IKN)

 USD 5,000,000

 for 5 years · USD 10,000,000 for 10 years

 Introduced in January 2026

 Projects in Nusantara, East Kalimantan

 An 80% cut against the standard corporate threshold

 The investment must be maintained for the entire validity of the status. Withdraw the capital early and the ground for residency disappears with it.

## The property route

 A separate option for the ten-year Golden Visa is buying residential property worth at least USD 1,000,000. There is a catch that rules the route out for many Bali buyers:

 !It means an apartment or condominium unit, not a standalone villa on its own plot of land

 !A foreigner cannot hold land under Hak Milik — the structure runs through Hak Pakai, or through a PT PMA holding an HGB title

 !A long-term leasehold agreement does not count as an investment for Golden Visa purposes

 The practical takeaway: if your property budget is under a million dollars, or the object is a villa, it is cheaper and safer to enter via Second Home or an investor status, and to structure the purchase separately.

## How it is filed: five steps

 Pick the categoryIt drives both the amount and the document pack: a private investor proves funds, a founder adds the deed of establishment, NIB and NPWP.

 Prove the source of fundsThe origin of the capital must be traceable. This is the most common sticking point: statements, contracts and proof of asset sales are prepared in advance.

 File onlineThrough the government portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id. There is no interview, and the average turnaround is about four business days once documents are verified.

 Place the investmentThe declared investment must actually be made and reported no later than 90 days after the ITAS is issued.

 Arrive and hold the statusThe ITAS and the multiple re-entry permit come bundled with the visa — no separate trip to an immigration office.

## The 90-day rule and what is at risk

 The Golden Visa is granted against a commitment, not after the fact. If the investment is not placed and reported within 90 days of the ITAS being issued, immigration may unilaterally revoke both the stay permit and the re-entry permit. After that the ordinary rules apply: you cannot remain in the country without a valid status, and an overstay costs IDR 1,000,000 per day.

 !Do not file "for later" while the money is not ready to be placed

 !Keep the investment paperwork — it is requested both at reporting and at renewal

 !Pulling the capital out early means losing the ground for residency

## Golden Visa, Second Home or investor KITAS

 Three statuses solve a similar problem — living in Indonesia long-term without visa chores — but they are built for different budgets.

 ✓Golden Visa — 5–10 years, from USD 350,000, maximum convenience and minimum contact with bureaucracy. For capital already sitting in securities or a deposit

 ✓Second Home — also 5–10 years, but the entry bar is several times lower: proof of funds in an account instead of an investment into the economy. Full breakdown in "Second Home: Bali as your second home"

 ✓Investor KITAS — one or two years, renewable, tied to your PT PMA. The most affordable entry for anyone running a real business in Bali: the full guide

 ✓Been in the country for years on end? Look at KITAP: when it becomes available

## Global Citizen of Indonesia: not the same thing

 In February 2026 immigration separately clarified the difference between the Golden Visa and the new Global Citizen of Indonesia (GCI) status. They are different programmes for different people: the Golden Visa is for foreign investors, GCI is for the diaspora. GCI covers former Indonesian citizens and their descendants to the second degree, foreign spouses of citizens, and children of mixed marriages. Its validity is not capped at five or ten years, but self-reporting is required every five years, and the financial bar is milder — around USD 1,500 of monthly income. If your family is tied to Indonesia by blood or marriage, you may not need a Golden Visa budget at all — and a family KITAS is worth comparing too.

## FAQ

Вопрос: How much does the Indonesia Golden Visa cost?
The entry threshold for a private investor without setting up a company is USD 350,000 for five years and USD 700,000 for ten. It is not a payment to the state but an investment that stays yours: government bonds, listed shares, mutual funds or a deposit with a state bank. For a company founder the amounts are higher — USD 2,500,000 and USD 5,000,000 respectively.

Вопрос: Can I work on a Golden Visa?
You can run your own company. You cannot take salaried employment with an Indonesian employer on this status — that requires a separate work KITAS with a work permit.

Вопрос: Does my family get the status with me?
Yes, a spouse and minor children are issued linked statuses for the same term. Children over 18 are assessed separately — usually if they are in full-time education.

Вопрос: What happens if the investment is not placed within 90 days?
Immigration may revoke the stay permit and the re-entry permit that were issued. That is why filing only makes sense once the funds are genuinely ready to be placed.

Вопрос: Does the Golden Visa lead to Indonesian citizenship?
No. It is long-term residency, not a citizenship-by-investment programme. Indonesia does not allow dual citizenship for adults, and naturalisation follows the general rules rather than an investment track.

Вопрос: Do I have to live in Indonesia to keep the status?
There is no minimum-stay requirement, so the status is not cancelled by a long absence. The investment itself, however, must be maintained for the whole validity of the visa.

 We will work out whether the Golden Visa fits you or whether Second Home or an investor KITAS is the cheaper way in — and assemble the source-of-funds pack.

# Insurance in Bali: what is actually mandatory

 Insurance is not required to obtain an Indonesian visa: it does not appear in the official document lists for the e-VOA, C1 or C6. What is mandatory is something else — membership of the BPJS system for foreigners working or living in the country for at least six months. A tourist needs no policy on paper, but healthcare here is private and motorbikes are the leading cause of claims.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Is insurance required for a visa

 The short answer: it does not appear in the official document lists. We checked the immigration requirements across several visa types — insurance is not listed for the e-VOA, the C1, the C6, or in the rules for extending a stay permit.

 ✓e-VOA — passport valid 6+ months, a scan, a photo, a return ticket, an address

 ✓C6 — passport, sponsor's letter, three months of bank statements, a photo, a host letter

 ✓Stay permit extension — passport, sponsor's guarantee letter, statement of purpose

 So not having a policy will not stop you getting a visa or entering. That does not mean you should go without — it is simply not immigration that requires it, but common sense and your own budget.

## Who must join BPJS

 BPJS is Indonesia's state social insurance system. For some foreigners joining it is not optional.

 ✓BPJS Kesehatan (health) — foreigners working or living in Indonesia for at least six months are required to register as members; for employees the registration goes through the employer

 ✓BPJS Ketenagakerjaan (employment, covering accidents and old age) — mandatory for foreign workers employed in Indonesia for at least six months

 The practical read: if you are here on a work KITAS employed by an Indonesian company, your employer handles it. If you hold an E33G or an investor status, the arrangement differs — check it against your own situation.

## Why a tourist still needs cover

 Healthcare in Bali is private for foreigners and not cheap. The international clinics in Kuta, Denpasar and Nusa Dua charge expat rates, and settlement happens on the spot.

 !Motorbikes. The single most common reason people end up in a clinic. Many policies exclude riding a motorbike without the matching licence category — read the exclusions before you buy

 !Diving and surfing. Active sports are almost always a separate add-on

 !Evacuation. Medical repatriation is the most expensive line of all, and the one most often missing from a basic policy

 Check three things in your policy: whether it covers riding a motorbike, whether evacuation is included, and the sum insured. Everything else is secondary.

## What we do and do not do

 We are a visa agency, not an insurance broker: we do not sell policies and do not recommend particular insurers — that is neither our remit nor our expertise.

 ✓We tell you whether insurance is required for your visa type, from the official document list

 ✓We flag whether you fall under mandatory BPJS given your length of stay and status

 ✓We assemble the visa file so that nothing in it raises questions

 Choosing the insurer and the terms is yours to do — and reading the exclusions carefully matters more than anyone's recommendation.

 On policies and motorbikes specifically, see driving in Bali, and for what the border actually asks for, the passport rules.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do I need insurance for a Bali visa?
Insurance is not listed in the official document requirements for the e-VOA, C1 or C6, nor in the rules for extending a stay permit. No policy is needed to obtain a visa.

Вопрос: Is BPJS mandatory for foreigners?
Yes, for those working or living in Indonesia for at least six months. BPJS Kesehatan is arranged through the employer for employees; BPJS Ketenagakerjaan is mandatory for foreign workers.

Вопрос: Does ordinary travel insurance cover riding a motorbike?
Often not. Many policies exclude motorbike riding or require the matching licence category. Check the exclusions before you buy, not after you come off the bike.

Вопрос: How much does treatment in Bali cost without insurance?
International clinics charge foreigner rates and settle on the spot. The amount depends on the clinic and the case — which is exactly why a policy with a sensible sum insured is worth having.

Вопрос: Does BPJS help a tourist?
No. BPJS is designed for people living and working in the country for six months or more. For a short trip only ordinary travel insurance applies.

## We will assemble the visa file without the extras

 We tell you what is genuinely required for your visa type and will not make you collect what is not.

# Investor KITAS 2026: residency through your own company

 The investor KITAS is a 1–2 year residence permit for shareholders, directors and commissioners of a PT PMA. It carries the right to run your own company without a separate work permit. The basis is a registered PT PMA and your stake in it: usually from around IDR 1 billion, with company capital from IDR 10 billion. Unbroken status opens a route to KITAP.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the investor KITAS gives you

 This is a residence permit for business owners in Indonesia — shareholders, directors and commissioners of PT PMA companies. The key feature: it combines residency with the right to run your own company, and no separate work permit is needed for that.

 ✓Valid 1–2 years, renewable, multiple entry

 ✓The right to work in your own company without a separate work permit

 ✓Issued to PT PMA shareholders, directors and commissioners

 ✓A route towards KITAP if the status runs unbroken

 Do not confuse this with the work KITAS. The investor version lets you run your own company. Taking a job with an unrelated Indonesian employer is not permitted — that needs a work KITAS with RPTKA approval.

## Thresholds: stake and capital

 The basis for the status is a registered PT PMA and your share in its capital. Thresholds depend on your role in the company and its investment plan.

 ✓Personal stake — usually from around IDR 1 billion

 ✓Company capital — from IDR 10 billion

 ✓Exact figures depend on the structure: they are calculated for your company and your role

 This is not a payment to the state but capital in your own business. If the company does not exist yet, registering a PT PMA is a separate project with its own timeline: how it works is set out in How to open a PT PMA, and the comparison of structures in PT PMA or a local PT.

## The route from scratch

 If you have no business in Indonesia yet, the order matters — the status cannot come before the company.

 Groundwork on a D12The pre-investment visa gives 180 days, extendable up to a year — enough to study the market, find partners and prepare the structure without living on tourist visas.

 PT PMA registrationFounding documents, NIB, licences for your line of business, a company account.

 Paying in your stakeYour personal share of the capital must be paid in and evidenced.

 The investor KITASIssued on the strength of the founding documents and proof of your stake.

On the pre-investment visa and its extensions, see the D12 visa.

## Documents

 ✓A passport with plenty of validity left

 ✓A personal photo

 ✓PT PMA founding documents and proof of your stake

 ✓The company's corporate documents

 Pricing is individual — it depends on nationality, company structure and timing. We assemble the corporate side together with our legal team, licences and accounting included: a PT PMA must keep its books from the first month, even before trading begins.

## Investor KITAS or golden visa

 Both grant long-term residency on the basis of capital, but the thresholds differ by an order of magnitude.

 ✓The investor KITAS — 1–2 years, tied to your PT PMA, stake threshold from around IDR 1 billion. The most accessible entry for people running a real business in Bali

 ✓The golden visa — 5 or 10 years, from USD 350,000, with no sponsor at all. For capital that works in securities or on deposit

 ✓Second Home — 5 or 10 years on proof of funds, with no company to open

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Who can get an investor KITAS?
Shareholders, directors and commissioners of a PT PMA company. The basis is a registered company and your share in its capital.

Вопрос: What are the financial thresholds?
Typically a personal stake from around IDR 1 billion with company capital from IDR 10 billion. Exact figures depend on the company's structure and your role, and are calculated case by case.

Вопрос: Can I work on an investor KITAS?
You can run your own company — no separate work permit is required for that. You cannot take a job with an unrelated employer; that needs a work KITAS.

Вопрос: What if I do not have a company yet?
The standard route is a D12 pre-investment visa for the groundwork, then PT PMA registration, paying in your stake, and the KITAS. We support every step, licences and accounting included.

Вопрос: Does the investor KITAS lead to permanent residence?
Yes — with unbroken status it opens a route to KITAP, permanent residence. The conditions and timelines are covered in our separate article on KITAP.

## We will run the thresholds against your structure

 We look at your stake and the company's capital, tell you whether you clear the thresholds, and map the route — from a D12 through to the KITAS.

# Japan visa from Bali: filing in Denpasar

 The one popular destination that needs no flight to Jakarta: Japan's visa centre operates in Denpasar and processing takes about five working days. But applications are accepted only from residents holding a KITAS or KITAP — an e-VOA will not be taken.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 This is the one popular destination that requires no trip to Jakarta at all. Japan's visa centre operates in Denpasar.

 ✓Filed in Bali — the Japan Visa Application Centre in Denpasar

 ✓Residents only — applications are accepted from foreigners holding a KITAS or KITAP

 ✓About 5 working days from the date of filing

 ✓The consulate itself stopped taking applications on 1 April 2024: everything goes through the centre

 Here is the practical value of residency that rarely gets mentioned: with a KITAS a Japanese visa is arranged half an hour from home, and without one it cannot be arranged here at all.

## Who will be turned away

 The restriction is firm and stated plainly: the centre does not accept applications from foreigners in Indonesia on short-term visas.

 !An e-VOA or visa on arrival — the application will not be taken

 !A business visa — likewise no

 !The C1 tourist visa — a short-term status, giving no grounds

 Only a stay permit works: an ITAS or ITAP, known colloquially as a KITAS and KITAP. If you are in Bali on a visit visa, the Japanese visa has to be arranged in your country of citizenship.

## Where to go

 ✓Consulate of Japan: Jl. Raya Puputan No. 170, Renon, Denpasar

 ✓Document submission: 08:00 to 15:00 on working days

 ✓Passport collection: 08:00 to 16:00

 ✓Centre phone: 0361-300-0025

 ✓Email: info.japanid@vfshelpline.com

 Submission and collection hours differ — that is not a typo. You can collect a passport after 15:00, but you can no longer file.

 One more detail people discover on arrival: the centre keeps working days only and closes for Japanese public holidays, of which there are more than you would expect. Check that the day is a working one before driving to Denpasar, or the trip across the island is wasted. And budget for two visits: one to file, one to collect.

## What to prepare

 The pack is standard for a short-stay Japanese visa, but two documents are critical for a resident.

 ✓KITAS or KITAP — your grounds for filing in Indonesia

 ✓Passport with sufficient validity and blank pages

 ✓Application form and photograph to the centre's specification

 ✓Travel plan — a day-by-day itinerary, accommodation bookings, tickets

 ✓Financial documents — statements covering the cost of the trip

 ✓Proof of employment — a contract, an employer letter or your own company documents

 Japanese consulates are traditionally attentive to the itinerary: a day-by-day plan here is not a formality but a working document that gets read.

## How it compares with the other destinations

 Measured by effort, Japan from Bali is unexpectedly convenient.

 ✓Japan — filed in Denpasar, no travel needed, but a KITAS is required

 ✓Australia — entirely online, status less critical

 ✓United States — an interview in Jakarta or Surabaya

 ✓Schengen — Jakarta, and for Russian citizens only the Bulgarian route works

 ✓China, Korea, Singapore — where entry is free, where K-ETA applies and where a visa is not

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I apply for a Japanese visa without leaving Bali?
Yes. Applications are taken by Japan's visa centre in Denpasar. Since 1 April 2024 the consulate-general itself no longer accepts visa applications — everything runs through the centre.

Вопрос: Will they accept my documents if I am on an e-VOA?
No. The centre accepts applications only from foreigners holding an ITAS or ITAP stay permit. Short-term statuses — visa on arrival, business visa, tourist visa — give no grounds.

Вопрос: How long does it take?
Usually around five working days from filing. Complex cases and peak season can take longer, so file ahead.

Вопрос: Where is the visa centre?
The Consulate of Japan is at Jl. Raya Puputan No. 170, Renon, Denpasar. Documents are submitted from 08:00 to 15:00 and collected until 16:00 on working days.

Вопрос: How much does the travel plan matter?
Noticeably more than for many other destinations. A day-by-day itinerary with bookings is part of the file and is genuinely reviewed rather than filed away.

 Give us your travel dates and status in Indonesia — we will assemble the pack and check the itinerary.
