# KITAP 2026: Indonesian permanent residence

 KITAP is permanent residence: a five-year card that renews automatically, replacing annual KITAS renewals. There is no direct route to it — only years of unbroken temporary status. It comes fastest to spouses of Indonesian citizens, usually after two years of marriage; work, investor and retirement bases take several years.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How KITAP differs from KITAS

 KITAP is the top rung of Indonesia's immigration ladder. The difference from a KITAS is not in what you may do but in how settled the status is and how much of your time it consumes.

 ✓A five-year card that renews automatically — against annual KITAS renewals

 ✓The yearly document gathering and immigration office visits are over

 ✓The underlying basis is the same — work, investment, family — in permanent form

 There is no direct route to KITAP. You reach it only through years of unbroken KITAS. Arriving on a tourist visa and arranging permanent residence is impossible at any price.

## Who qualifies, and after how long

 The pace depends on the basis on which you live in the country.

 ✓Spouses of Indonesian citizens — the fastest route, usually after 2 years of official marriage

 ✓Work KITAS holders — after several years of unbroken status

 ✓Investor KITAS holders — also after several years, provided the stake in the company is maintained

 ✓Retirement KITAS holders — on the same continuity logic

 The operative word is unbroken. A gap resets the years you have accumulated, which makes 'sitting out a year on tourist visas' between two KITAS an expensive mistake that pushes KITAP years back.

## MERP: leaving the country on permanent status

 Permanent residence does not mean freedom of movement by default. To travel you need a multiple exit re-entry permit — the MERP.

 !Leaving without a valid MERP means putting your status at risk

 !The status is revoked after a long absence without permission

 !Watching the MERP date matters as much as watching KITAS dates used to

 The paradox of KITAP is that the visa routine ends but one date remains — and that is precisely the one people forget, having relaxed after years of annual renewals.

## Documents

 ✓A passport with plenty of validity left

 ✓Your current KITAS and the full history of your statuses

 ✓Basis documents: marriage certificate, company papers, employment or pension records

 ✓Sponsor documents, depending on your route

 The status history is the most important part of the file. It is what evidences continuity, so old KITAS cards and renewal records are worth keeping from your first year in the country rather than reconstructing later.

 The file also includes an SKCK police certificate: issued to residents only, filed in Jakarta, and valid for just six months.

## Strategy: think about KITAP early

 The route to permanent status is set not at the end of the journey but when you choose your first KITAS. That choice decides how many years the walk takes.

 ✓Family basis — the shortest path: a family KITAS and two years of marriage

 ✓Your own business — an investor KITAS through a PT PMA: longer, but it produces income as well as status

 ✓Employment — a work KITAS, tied to an employer whose change disrupts continuity

 If the long-term goal is to stay, it is worth discussing the route before you file for your first status. You can change course later, but every turn costs time — and here time is the currency.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: What is KITAP in plain terms?
Indonesian permanent residence. The card is issued for five years and renews automatically — the annual renewals, document gathering and immigration visits come to an end.

Вопрос: Can I get KITAP directly, without a KITAS?
No. There is no direct route: KITAP comes only after years of unbroken KITAS. Arriving on a tourist visa and arranging permanent status is not possible.

Вопрос: After how many years of marriage is KITAP granted?
For spouses of Indonesian citizens, usually after two years of official marriage — the fastest route. Work, investor and retirement bases require several years of unbroken status.

Вопрос: Can I travel abroad on a KITAP?
Yes, but you need a multiple exit re-entry permit, the MERP. Leaving without one, or a long absence without permission, leads to the status being revoked.

Вопрос: What happens if my KITAS lapses for a year?
The break resets your accumulated continuity and the count towards KITAP starts again. That is why bridging gaps on tourist visas is an expensive decision.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

 We assess your status history, work out how far you still have to go, and flag what not to break along the way.

# The Love Bali levy: paid in five minutes

 Love Bali is the provincial tourist levy: IDR 150,000 from every foreign visitor, on every entry to the island. Pay it on the province's official portal or at airport desks. Border checks are selective, but five minutes online closes the question. Do not confuse it with the free All Indonesia card or with paying for the visa itself.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the levy is

 Love Bali is the Bali provincial tourist levy: IDR 150,000 from every foreign visitor, around USD 10. The money goes to protecting the island's nature and culture.

 ✓Paid on every entry to Bali, not once for life

 ✓Charged per person, children included

 ✓Independent of visa type: e-VOA, C1 and KITAS holders all pay

## How to pay

 Online in advanceThe province's official portal, lovebali.baliprov.go.id. Card payment, with a QR confirmation by email. About five minutes.

 Save the QR offlineScreenshot it. Airport wifi is unreliable and you need the code to hand quickly.

 Or on arrivalThere are payment desks at the airport. It works, but it is a queue after a long flight.

Pay on the province's official portal. Third-party sites with a markup circle this levy — the payment is identical and the commission is yours.

## Mandatory or not

 Formally the levy applies to every foreign visitor. In practice checks at the border are selective and irregular — there is no hard 'no payment, no entry' rule.
Our practical view: paying takes five minutes online and closes the question. Treat it as a contribution to the island hosting you rather than another barrier. Checks are periodically stepped up, and being caught out is more annoying than spending five minutes in advance.

## Do not confuse it with other payments

 Three different things that get merged into one:

 ✓Love Bali — IDR 150,000, a provincial levy, payable on every entry

 ✓The All Indonesia card — a free and mandatory declaration, filed 72 hours before arrival: how it works

 ✓The visa — an e-VOA at IDR 900,000 all-in or another type, paid separately

 !Love Bali does not replace a visa or extend your stay

 !Paying it does not affect autogate clearance

 !Overstay fines are a separate tariff: IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person

## What to have ready on arrival

 ✓Your Love Bali QR code — saved offline

 ✓Your All Indonesia declaration QR code

 ✓Passport and approved electronic visa

 ✓A return or onward ticket and your address

 The full pre-departure checklist is on its own page. A pack assembled in advance saves more time on arrival than you would expect.

## Where the money goes

 The levy is earmarked: the province directs it to protecting Bali's nature and culture — beach cleaning and maintenance, upkeep of temples and heritage sites, and waste management programmes.
For a visitor it is the cheapest line of the trip: IDR 150,000 is roughly two coffees in Canggu. Set against visas, accommodation and transport, this is not the item to economise on.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much is the Love Bali levy?
IDR 150,000 per person, roughly USD 10. It is paid on every entry to Bali and charged for every visitor, children included.

Вопрос: Where do I pay?
On the province's official portal, lovebali.baliprov.go.id — by card, with a QR confirmation by email. Or at airport desks on arrival, where there may be a queue.

Вопрос: Do I pay on every entry?
Yes, the payment is tied to entry. Fly out and back and the levy is paid again.

Вопрос: What happens if I do not pay?
Checks are selective and there is no outright entry ban. But enforcement is periodically stepped up, and paying takes five minutes — easier to close the question in advance.

Вопрос: Is it the same as All Indonesia?
No. All Indonesia is the free, mandatory arrival declaration. Love Bali is a paid provincial levy. Two different things.

## Arrive prepared

 We arrange the visa and walk you through the levy and the declaration — nothing left open at the border.

# How to open a PT PMA 2026: steps and timing

 The PT PMA is the only company form a foreigner can own directly in Indonesia, and the only lawful way to earn income here. The requirements: share capital from IDR 10 billion, at least two shareholders, a director and a commissioner, and a legal address. Registration takes two weeks to two months. The decisive choice up front is your KBLI activity codes.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Why a PT PMA at all

 The PT PMA is a foreign-investment company and the only structure a foreigner can own directly in Indonesia. A company counts as foreign with any overseas shareholding at all: one per cent or one hundred.

 ✓Lawful trading and contracts in the company's name

 ✓A corporate account with an Indonesian bank

 ✓Investor KITAS for the owners

 ✓Hiring staff and operating in the local market on equal terms with Indonesian companies

 The essential point: a foreigner may carry on income-generating activity in Indonesia only through a company. Neither a tourist visa nor an E33G nor a family KITAS confers that right.

## Registration requirements

 ✓Share capital — from IDR 10 billion; how it is evidenced depends on the structure

 ✓At least two shareholders — individuals or companies

 ✓A director and a commissioner — mandatory roles in the structure

 ✓A legal address is required; a virtual office is acceptable in many cases

 ✓Registration time — two weeks to two months

 The permitted foreign shareholding depends on the line of business: many sectors allow a full 100 per cent, while some carry restrictions under the investment list.

## The stages

 Name and clearanceSeveral candidate names are checked for availability — more applications stall here than people expect.

 KBLI codesThe classification of business activities. It governs both the maximum foreign shareholding and the set of licences required.

 Deed and structureShareholdings, appointment of the director and commissioner, and division of authority.

 Registration and NPWPIncorporation of the legal entity and issue of its tax number.

 LicencesPermits for your specific activity — the set depends on the KBLI codes chosen.

 Bank accountThe corporate account is opened once registration and the core document pack are complete.

## Three decisions you cannot postpone

 A mistake at the start costs you not money but re-registration — which means the timeline and the fees all over again.

 !KBLI codes. The wrong classification means the wrong licences and the wrong ceiling on foreign ownership. It is fixable only by re-registering, which is why codes are matched to the plan from day one

 !Ownership structure. Who the shareholders are, who holds what, who is director and who is commissioner — this determines whether you clear the thresholds for an investor KITAS

 !Share capital. The amount and how it will be evidenced are settled before registration, not after

## What comes next: KITAS and obligations

 Registering the company is not the finish line but the start. Two tracks then run in parallel.

 ✓Status for you. On the strength of the founding documents and proof of your stake, an investor KITAS is issued — one to two years with the right to run your own company

 ✓The company's obligations. Accounting and reporting are mandatory from the first month, even before trading begins

 If you have no business yet and need time to prepare, the standard first step is the D12 pre-investment visa: 180 days, extendable up to a year, to study the market and assemble the structure without living on tourist visas. A comparison of company forms is in PT PMA or a local PT.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much money is needed to open a PT PMA?
Share capital from IDR 10 billion. How it must be evidenced depends on the company's structure and its line of business, so the specifics are worked through on a consultation.

Вопрос: Can a foreigner own 100 per cent of the company?
In many sectors, yes. The permitted share is set by the KBLI codes: some industries carry investment-list restrictions, which is why the classification is chosen before registration.

Вопрос: How long does registration take?
Two weeks to two months with documents ready. The spread depends on the business activity and the licences required for the chosen KBLI codes.

Вопрос: Do I need a physical office?
A legal address is required, but a virtual office is acceptable in many cases. The requirement depends on the type of activity.

Вопрос: Does a PT PMA give me the right to live in Indonesia?
The company itself does not, but it is the basis for an investor KITAS for shareholders, directors and commissioners: residency for one to two years with the right to run your own business.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

 We match the codes to your niche, build the structure around the investor KITAS thresholds, and run the registration and licensing.

# Overstay in Bali 2026: Fine, Consequences & What to Do

 Overstaying in Indonesia costs IDR 1,000,000 per day — from day one, per person, children included. Up to 60 days it is an administrative case: pay the fine and leave. Beyond 60 days — detention, deportation at your own expense and a re-entry ban of 6 months to 2 years.

 Updated: 22 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What counts as overstay

 Overstay starts the day after your permitted stay ends — Indonesia has no grace days, even one day counts. The rule applies to every status: VOA and eVOA, the C1 tourist visa, business visas, multiple-entry D1/D2, and KITAS. The fine is charged per person — a child has their own visa and their own counter.

 Work out your own total. The overstay fine calculator — enter the days and the number of people.

## The fine: how much and how it adds up

 The rate is IDR 1,000,000 (about USD 65) per day of overstay; it is an official state charge under Immigration Law No. 6/2011 (Art. 78) — not a “bribe” and not negotiable. It is paid at an immigration office or at the airport on departure, for overstays up to 60 days. Do the math:

 !10 days over — IDR 10,000,000 (~USD 650)

 !30 days — IDR 30,000,000 (~USD 1,950)

 !A family of four, 10 days — IDR 40,000,000: the fine applies to each person, children included

## Up to 60 days: how it goes

 An overstay under 60 days is an administrative violation. You go to immigration (or pay on departure), settle the amount for all days, get a receipt and leave the country. The overstay stays on your immigration record and is visible in future visa applications, but with the fine paid, future entry is generally possible.

## Beyond 60 days: deportation territory

 !Detention until the case is resolved — immigration facility

 !Deportation at your own expense, with no “just pay the fine” option

 !A re-entry ban (penangkalan) of 6 months to 2 years, longer in some cases

 !If unable to pay, or with aggravating factors, criminal liability is possible

## Already overstayed? Action plan

 ✓Don’t hide and don’t wait: every day adds another million rupiah

 ✓Go to the nearest immigration office yourself and explain the situation honestly

 ✓Pay the official charge and keep the receipts — you will need them for future visas

 ✓Leave the country within a reasonable time after paying

 ✓Avoid “fixers” promising to “erase” an overstay — that is a scam and a criminal risk

## How to never overstay

 ✓The expiry date is in your e-visa PDF, not “in your head”. Set a reminder 10 days ahead

 ✓Extend early: extension filings go in at least 6 working days before expiry — eVOA extension — step-by-step, C1 extensions

 ✓Staying in Bali long-term — get off the visa carousel with a multiple-entry D1/D2 or the E33G KITAS

 ✓Before flying to Bali, check our arrival guide

## FAQ

Вопрос: Is there a grace period after the visa expires?
No. Overstay starts the day after expiry, and the very first day costs IDR 1,000,000.

Вопрос: Is the fine charged for a child?
Yes. The fine is calculated per person, including children of any age.

Вопрос: Can I extend a visa that has already expired?
No. Extensions are only filed before expiry. Once overstayed, you pay the fine and leave; you come back on a new visa.

Вопрос: Can the fine be negotiated down?
No. It is a fixed state charge, and middlemen promising otherwise are scammers.

Вопрос: Will I be allowed back after a paid overstay?
For overstays under 60 days with the fine paid, future entry is generally possible, though the record remains on file. After deportation, a re-entry ban applies.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

## Rather not count days? Leave the deadlines to us

 We’ll extend your visa on time or match you with a status that needs no constant renewals.

# PT PMA or Local PT: which to choose

 The PT PMA is the foreign-investment company: any overseas shareholding, capital from IDR 10 billion, and the only way a foreigner can lawfully own a business and earn in Indonesia. The Local PT belongs solely to Indonesian citizens, capital from IDR 50 million, and for a foreigner it is a joint-project format with a partner. On nominee arrangements we are blunt: legally it belongs to whoever it is registered to.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Two forms, two logics

 The PT PMA and the Local PT are not an expensive and a cheap version of the same thing. The difference is who may own the company, and everything else follows from that.

 | 
 PT PMA | 
 Local PT | 

 Owners | any foreign shareholding — 1% or 100% | Indonesian citizens only, 100% of shares | 
Share capital | from IDR 10 billion | from IDR 50 million | 
Structure | at least 2 shareholders, a director and a commissioner | standard PT structure | 
Foreign share | set by KBLI codes: 100% in many sectors | not available | 
Registration time | 2 weeks to 2 months | 2 weeks to 2 months | 
Residence for the owner | investor KITAS based on the stake | work KITAS issued by the company | 

## When you need a PT PMA

 A company counts as foreign with any overseas shareholding. And a foreigner may carry on income-generating activity in Indonesia only through one.

 ✓You want to own the business lawfully and in your own name

 ✓You need an investor KITAS based on your stake

 ✓You plan to hire staff and operate locally on equal terms with Indonesian companies

 ✓You need a corporate account and contracts in the company's name

 The capital threshold is the price of that: from IDR 10 billion against 50 million for a Local PT. How registration runs is in a separate article.

## When a Local PT works

 The Local PT is the most common business form in Bali: a low capital threshold, a straightforward process and a lighter regulatory load. For a foreigner it is a workable format for a joint project with an Indonesian partner.

 ✓The partner holds ownership; you take part in legal roles

 ✓A foreigner can work in such a company on a work KITAS issued by the company itself

 ✓The standard route: KBLI → founding documents → NPWP → NIB → licences

## On nominee arrangements — plainly

 The 'register it to a local, but really it is yours' arrangement is widely sold and sounds cheap. The problem is that legally it belongs to whoever it is registered to.

 !You hold no owner's rights — neither to the shares nor to the company's assets

 !Private side agreements do not give the protection a register entry does

 !A dispute with the partner resolves against you by default

 !Claims can also come from the regulator — against both sides

 We say this plainly because the cost surfaces years later, at the worst possible moment. If the business is yours, the structure should say so.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How does a PT PMA differ from a Local PT?
By ownership. A PT PMA is a company with any foreign shareholding, capital from IDR 10 billion. A Local PT belongs to Indonesian citizens only, capital from IDR 50 million.

Вопрос: Can a foreigner own a Local PT?
No. A Local PT is 100% owned by Indonesian citizens. Any foreign shareholding automatically makes it a PT PMA.

Вопрос: How much capital is needed?
PT PMA from IDR 10 billion, Local PT from IDR 50 million. How it is evidenced depends on the structure and the line of business.

Вопрос: Can a foreigner work in a Local PT?
Yes, on a work KITAS issued by the company. That does not confer ownership, but it does give a lawful role in the project.

Вопрос: How risky are nominee arrangements?
Substantially. Legally the shares belong to whoever holds them, and side agreements do not replace the register. Disputes resolve against you.

## We will match the structure to your plan

 We work through your activity, KBLI codes and ownership structure — and tell you what is genuinely needed and what is being sold for nothing.

# The retirement KITAS: Bali after 55

 The retirement KITAS is a residence permit for foreigners aged 55 and over. It runs for a year and renews annually without leaving the country. You must evidence income of at least USD 3,000 a month and a bank statement. Insurance and a lease are not required, contrary to what is widely repeated. Selling directly inside the country is prohibited, and the route to KITAP opens at 60.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Who it suits

 The retirement KITAS is a residence permit for foreigners aged 55 and over who choose Indonesia to live in rather than holiday in: to stay through the season without border runs, rent a house long term, open an account and feel like a resident.

 ✓Age — 55 and over

 ✓Valid one year, renewed annually inside the country with no exit

 ✓Resident rights: a bank account, long-term rental, a driving licence, insurance

 ✓Unbroken status opens the route to KITAP

## What you must evidence

 The basis here is not work or business but steady income and a settled life. Hence the evidence required:

 ✓Regular income from USD 3,000 a month — a pension, rental income or another steady source, documented

 ✓A three-month bank statement showing at least USD 2,000

 ✓A passport valid for at least 6 months, a photo, a short CV and your itinerary

 ✓A sponsor guarantee letter — the annual status cannot be arranged without a sponsor, and a licensed agency acts as one

 Medical insurance and a housing lease are not needed. Some agencies still ask for them, but neither appears in the current requirements: both are left over from the old retirement regime under index C319, which has been abolished. One more detail that trips people up most often: savings do not count as income — immigration looks at regular inflows, not at your balance.

## The core restriction

 !Selling goods or services directly inside Indonesia is prohibited — that is the wording of the law, and it is narrower than the usual shorthand "no working". Other activity is formally possible through a separate notification to immigration about combining activities, though on the retirement track almost nobody goes through it

 !Income must come from outside: a pension, rent, investments abroad

 If you want to combine island life with remote work for foreign clients, that is a different status — the E33G. If a business in Indonesia is in the plan, the investor KITAS.

## Retirement or Second Home

 Two statuses solve a similar problem — living in Indonesia long term — but they are built differently.

 ✓Retirement, annual E33F — one year renewed annually, up to five years in total, an age floor of 55, sponsor required. There is also a five-year version, Silver Hair E33E: no sponsor, but a USD 50,000 deposit

 ✓Second Home — five or ten years at once, no age limit, but a different basis: proof of capital. Covered in its own article

 Put simply: with the age and a steady pension, the retirement route works. With capital but not yet 55, Second Home. With both, we price the two and compare on cost and on how often you renew.

## The route to permanent status

 The retirement KITAS is not a dead end: with unbroken status you may apply for KITAP — permanent residence on a five-year card that renews itself. One detail almost nobody publishes: on the retirement track, the move to KITAP opens at 60. So someone who takes the status at 55 is not waiting "a few years" in the abstract — they are waiting until sixty.

 ✓The operative word is unbroken: a gap resets the years accumulated

 ✓Bridging gaps on tourist visas is an expensive mistake

 ✓Conditions and timelines are in our KITAP article

## What changes day to day

 The difference between wintering on tourist visas and holding retirement status shows up not in paperwork but in everyday things.

 ✓Renting. With residence status a long lease at a sensible price is easier to agree — landlords prefer tenants who will not leave in two months

 ✓Banking. The account is an ordinary procedure: what it takes

 ✓Driving. An Indonesian licence becomes available instead of an IDP: explained

 ✓Peace of mind. No border runs, no counting days, no questions at immigration every two months

## Tax: what the market stays quiet about

 For a retiree this is the central question — it concerns their main income — and yet hardly any visa agency writes about it.

 The rule: a foreigner becomes an Indonesian tax resident by living here or by spending more than 183 days in any 12 months. The days need not be consecutive. A resident must register for tax, obtain an NPWP and file a return, and in the general case worldwide income is declared, not just Indonesian income. Rates are progressive, up to 35%.

 How strictly this is enforced is another matter, and people's experience differs. But cases where the tax office located foreign accounts through international data exchange are on record. Plan this with a tax adviser and with your country's double taxation treaty in mind. Worth knowing separately: anyone who has ever worked officially for an Indonesian company draws more attention, and for a long time.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: From what age is the retirement KITAS available?
From 55. That is a baseline condition with no way around it: for younger applicants with capital there is the Second Home programme, which has no age limit.

Вопрос: Can I work on a retirement KITAS?
No. Work in Indonesia is not permitted on this status. Income must come from outside — a pension, rent, or investments abroad.

Вопрос: Do I have to leave to renew?
No, the status is renewed annually inside the country.

Вопрос: What evidence is required?
Regular income, funds in an account, medical insurance and a long-term housing lease. The specific thresholds are updated periodically, so verify them before filing rather than from older publications.

Вопрос: Does it lead to permanent residence?
Yes — with unbroken status the route to KITAP opens after several years. A gap in status resets that count.

## We will verify the requirements for your case

 Income thresholds and evidence lists change. Tell us where your income comes from and we will say whether you qualify and what to prepare.

# Schengen from Bali: the Bulgaria route

 An Indonesian resident files for Schengen where they live, not where they hold citizenship — no trip home needed. For Russian citizens one route works in practice, the Bulgarian one: the country joined Schengen fully on 1 January 2025 and its visa is valid across the zone. Since November 2025, expect a single-entry visa tied to one trip.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 A Schengen application is filed where you legally live, not where you hold citizenship. For a KITAS holder that means Indonesia — no flight home required.

 ✓The right to file where you reside — proven by a KITAS or KITAP

 ✓For Russian citizens one route works in practice: Bulgaria. Other consulates in Jakarta either do not accept applications from Russian nationals or refuse nearly all of them

 ✓A Bulgarian visa is a full Schengen visa — the country joined the zone completely on 1 January 2025

 ✓Expect a single-entry visa tied to one trip rather than a multi-year multiple-entry one

 Practice shifts quickly and is decided by a particular consulate in a particular month. Everything below is worth re-checking before you file, especially if you are reading this six months later.

## What happened with Bulgaria, and why it matters

 Before 2025 a Bulgarian visa was national: it admitted you to Bulgaria but not to the Schengen area. That is now history.

 31 March 2024Checks were lifted at Bulgarian and Romanian air and sea borders.

 1 January 2025Land border checks went too. Both countries became full members of the Schengen area.

 What it changedA Bulgarian type C visa now works on the same terms as a French or Italian one: the whole zone is open with it.

That is the whole point of the route: you file where the application will actually be accepted and assessed, and you receive a document valid across Schengen.

## What changed on 7 November 2025

 On that date the European Commission adopted a decision recommending that EU states stop issuing multiple-entry Schengen visas to Russian citizens.

 ✓Formally it is a recommendation, not law: each country still decides for itself

 ✓In practice consulates moved en masse to single-entry visas tied to specific travel dates

 ✓Exceptions remain for narrow categories — close relatives of EU citizens, transport workers, independent journalists and human rights defenders

 !Planning around a five-year multiple-entry visa is no longer realistic

 !Each new trip most likely means a new application and a new document set

## Where to file in Indonesia

 The Bulgarian embassy is in Jakarta and its consular section receives in the morning.

 ✓Address: Jalan Imam Bonjol 34–36, Jakarta 10310

 ✓Phones: +62 21 390 40 48, +62 21 391 31 30

 ✓Consular email: consular.jakarta@mfa.bg

 ✓Hours: 09:00 to 13:00 on working days

 Schengen applications in Indonesia largely run through VFS Global visa centres — there are three, and Jakarta handles most embassies and the largest volume. Confirm the current filing route for Bulgaria before booking: it changes, and it determines where you give biometrics.
Every applicant must appear in person, children and infants included. From Bali that means a flight to Jakarta — budget for it in both time and money.

## Documents to prepare

 The base pack is standard Schengen, but two items are critical for an Indonesian resident.

 ✓KITAS or KITAP — proof of legal residence. Without it, filing where you live does not work

 ✓Passport — valid at least 3 months beyond your return, with two blank pages

 ✓Flight and accommodation bookings for the whole trip

 ✓Medical insurance covering EUR 30,000 across the Schengen area

 ✓Proof of funds — bank statements for recent months

 ✓Proof of income or employment — a contract, an employer letter or your own company documents

 An SKTT is sometimes requested as proof of address and an SKCK as a police certificate from your country of residence — check the requirements at the time you file.

## The main destination rule — where people come unstuck

 A Schengen visa is issued by the consulate of the country that is your main destination: where you will spend the most days, or, if equal, where you enter first.

 !Getting a Bulgarian visa and flying straight to Paris for two weeks breaks the rule rather than gaming it. Such itineraries are visible in your tickets and bookings

 !At your next application the travel history is reviewed: a mismatch between what you declared and what you did is a direct route to refusal

 The practical conclusion: if you travel on a Bulgarian visa, Bulgaria has to be a genuine destination rather than a formality. It is inconvenient, but that is what keeps the route working.

## Timing and money

 The Schengen consular fee is EUR 90 for adults and EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 12. Visa centres charge their own service fee on top.

 ✓File 4 to 8 weeks before travel — that is the visa centres' own guidance, and it is not arbitrary

 ✓Summer and holidays lengthen the queue for an appointment, not just for processing

 ✓Add the Bali–Jakarta flight and at least one night: reception closes at 13:00

## Where else you can file from Bali

 Residency in Indonesia opens applications elsewhere too — the procedures and the effort differ.

 ✓US visa — an interview in Jakarta or Surabaya, USD 185 with another 250 on the way

 ✓Australia visa — entirely online, no consulate visit, AUD 200

 ✓Japan visa — the visa centre is in Denpasar, no Jakarta trip needed

 ✓China, Korea and Singapore — where entry is free, where K-ETA applies and where a visa is not

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I apply for Schengen while living in Bali?
Yes. Schengen rules allow filing where you legally reside rather than where you hold citizenship. You need a valid KITAS or KITAP, which is what proves you live in Indonesia.

Вопрос: Why Bulgaria specifically?
It is the one realistic route for Russian citizens: other consulates in Jakarta either do not accept Russian applications or refuse almost all of them. Meanwhile Bulgaria became a full Schengen member on 1 January 2025, so its visa is valid across the zone.

Вопрос: Will I get a multiple-entry visa?
Most likely not. On 7 November 2025 the European Commission recommended that EU states stop issuing multiple-entry visas to Russian citizens, and consulates moved to single-entry visas tied to specific dates. Exceptions remain for narrow categories.

Вопрос: Can I travel to another Schengen country on a Bulgarian visa?
The visa is valid across the zone, but it is issued for your main destination. If your paperwork says Bulgaria while you actually spend the time in France, that breaks the main destination rule — and it surfaces at your next application.

Вопрос: Do I have to fly to Jakarta in person?
Yes. Personal appearance is required of every applicant, children included. The Bulgarian embassy's consular section receives from 09:00 to 13:00 on working days, so plan a flight and an overnight stay from Bali.

## We will assemble your Schengen file and prepare the filing

 Tell us your travel dates and your status in Indonesia — we will time it and check the documents.

# Second Home: five or ten years in Bali

 Second Home is the longest residence permit Indonesia offers a private individual without opening a company: five or ten years with multiple entry. The basis is proven capital — a benchmark of IDR 2 billion in an Indonesian bank account, or a qualifying property investment. No age limit and no employer. Employment with Indonesian companies is not permitted.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## How Second Home differs

 This is the longest residence permit Indonesia offers a private individual without opening a company. The basis is neither work nor business but proven capital.

 ✓Residence for five or ten years at once, multiple entry — no annual renewal treadmill

 ✓No age limit — unlike the retirement status

 ✓No employer required and no company of your own

 ✓Resident rights: a bank account, long-term rental, a driving licence

 ✓Dependent statuses are issued for your spouse and children

## What counts as the basis

 The core requirement is placing funds, or a qualifying property investment.

 ✓The benchmark is IDR 2 billion (around USD 125,000–130,000) in an Indonesian bank account

 ✓Or a qualifying investment in property

 That is a benchmark, not a final figure: thresholds and the manner of evidencing them are revised periodically. We verify the current requirements before filing — working from last year's publications is expensive here.

## What is not allowed

 !Employment with Indonesian companies is not permitted on Second Home

 !Nor is providing services to local clients or earning from Indonesian sources

 The status grants the right to live, not to work. For employment there is the work KITAS; for your own business the investor KITAS; for remote work with foreign clients the E33G.

## Second Home, golden visa or investor

 Three capital-based statuses, with thresholds an order of magnitude apart.

 ✓Second Home — five or ten years, benchmark IDR 2 billion in an account. The money stays yours and no company is needed

 ✓The golden visa — five or ten years, from USD 350,000 invested in the economy

 ✓The investor KITAS — one or two years, tied to your PT PMA, but carrying the right to run your own business

 The choice is simple: Second Home if you have the capital and no business planned in Indonesia. Investor if there is one. The golden visa if the sum allows and you want the most self-contained status available.

## Who it suits in practice

 ✓People tired of renewals who want the visa question closed for years

 ✓People under 55, for whom the retirement status is not available

 ✓Families: spouse and children take dependent statuses

 ✓People whose income and assets are abroad and for whom Indonesia is where they live, not where they earn

## The question that comes up most

 The second question after 'how much money' is what happens to that money afterwards.

 ✓The funds sit in an Indonesian bank account and remain yours — this is not a payment to the state

 ✓The alternative to placing funds is a qualifying property investment

 ✓The basis must be maintained for the whole term of the status

 Hence the practical read: Second Home makes sense if the sum is sitting idle anyway. If your capital is working in a business, the honest comparison is the investor KITAS — it gives status and keeps the money in play.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long is Second Home granted for?
Five or ten years, with multiple entry. It is the longest residence permit available to a private individual in Indonesia without opening a company.

Вопрос: How much money is required?
The benchmark is IDR 2 billion, roughly USD 125,000–130,000, in an Indonesian bank account, or a qualifying property investment. Thresholds are revised periodically, so verify them before filing.

Вопрос: Are there age requirements?
No. Unlike the retirement KITAS, Second Home requires no particular age, no employer and no business of your own.

Вопрос: Can I work on Second Home?
No, employment with Indonesian companies is not permitted on this status. It grants the right to live in the country, not to work in it.

Вопрос: Can I bring my family?
Yes, dependent statuses are issued for your spouse and children for the same term.

## We will price Second Home against your capital

 We verify the current thresholds, compare against the investor KITAS and the golden visa, and tell you which works out better.

# SKCK in Indonesia: the police certificate

 An SKCK is issued only to KITAS and KITAP holders — a visit visa gives no grounds. Filing is in person and only in Jakarta, as the police app is closed to foreigners. The government fee is IDR 60,000, and the six-month validity is the reason most people end up doing it twice.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Who can get an SKCK at all

 The limit people trip over most often: the certificate is issued only to holders of a KITAS or KITAP. Residency is a hard requirement, not a preference.

 !A tourist visa, e-VOA or business visa gives no grounds — the application will not be accepted

 !The C6 social visa does not qualify either: it grants no residency

 !The certificate covers the absence of a criminal record in Indonesia, not in your home country

 If you arrived on a visit visa and need a police certificate for local matters, you first need residency — for example through converting to a KITAS.

## What it is for

 An SKCK is rarely requested on its own — it usually surfaces on the way to something bigger.

 ✓Moving to a KITAP — permanent residency is not granted without it

 ✓Citizenship applications — a mandatory part of the file

 ✓Employment — some employers ask for it at hiring

 ✓Visas for other countries — some consulates want a certificate from your country of residence, not citizenship

 ✓Marriage to an Indonesian citizen — part of the document set

## Documents

 The list is short, but every item is formal: the wrong photo background is enough to be turned away.

 ✓A 4×6 cm photo on a yellow background, formal clothing — the yellow background is compulsory

 ✓A full copy of your passport, including every entry and exit stamp

 ✓A copy of your KITAS or KITAP

 ✓A fingerprint form, completed at the police station

 ✓A sponsor letter from your guarantor or employer in Indonesia

 Passport stamps are checked closely: if pages are missing or the passport was replaced, bring the old one too.

## How the procedure runs

 Here is the key difference from what Indonesians do: the POLRI SuperApp is not available to foreigners. Filing is in person and on paper.

 Recommendation from local policeYou start at the POLDA or city police covering your address, which issues a letter of recommendation.

 FingerprintsTaken at the same place. It takes a few minutes.

 Filing at Mabes PolriFor foreigners the SKCK is issued only by national police headquarters in Jakarta. A Bali office cannot close the case — the file goes to the capital.

 PaymentThe government fee is IDR 60,000 under regulation PP No. 60 of 2019. The fee is nominal; the real cost is travel and time.

 CollectionThe finished certificate is collected in person or by proxy.

## Validity, and the mistake it causes

 An SKCK is valid for six months from issue. That is shorter than it feels, and it produces the most common problem: people get the certificate early «to have it ready», and by the time the KITAP or citizenship file is submitted it has expired.

 ✓Order the certificate once the rest of the file is nearly complete, not first

 ✓If the process drags, budget for getting it a second time

 ✓For foreign consulates check their freshness rule — it is often three months, not six

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I get an SKCK on a tourist visa?
No. The certificate is issued only to KITAS or KITAP holders. Visit visas — e-VOA, C1, C2, the C6 social visa — give no grounds: an SKCK attests to a resident's clean record.

Вопрос: Where exactly do foreigners file?
At national police headquarters, Mabes Polri in Jakarta. You first obtain a recommendation letter from the POLDA or city police covering your address. The POLRI SuperApp is not available to foreigners.

Вопрос: What does an SKCK cost?
The government fee is IDR 60,000 under PP No. 60 of 2019. The real expense is not the fee but the trip to Jakarta and the time spent collecting recommendations.

Вопрос: How long is it valid?
Six months from the date of issue. If your KITAP or citizenship file takes longer to assemble, the certificate has to be obtained again.

Вопрос: Does an SKCK cover my home country record?
No. It concerns your stay in Indonesia only. If a consulate or authority asks for a certificate from your country of citizenship, that is obtained and legalised separately — see our apostille guide for how that works.

# SKTT and STM: registering as a foreigner

 Once your KITAS is issued you have 14 days to register your address. First the STM, the police notification, then the SKTT from the civil registry, which comes with an Indonesian NIK number. Without that pair you hit walls at extension, at the bank and at the licensing office.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 Getting a KITAS is not the finish line. After it you are required to register your address, and you have 14 days to do it.

 ✓STM — police registration. The first step; without it there is no second

 ✓SKTT — a certificate of residence from Dukcapil, the civil registry

 ✓NIK — the Indonesian personal number issued together with the SKTT

 ✓KTP-OA — the foreigner resident card, but that comes only after moving to a KITAP

 The clock starts from the date your KITAS is issued, or from your entry date if the status was arranged abroad. Two weeks pass faster than you think, especially while you are still looking for a place to live.

## Why it matters in practice

 Formally it is an obligation. Practically, without an SKTT and a NIK you hit walls where you least expect them.

 ✓Extending your KITAS — registration documents are part of the file

 ✓A bank account — some banks ask for the SKTT on top of the KITAS

 ✓A driving licence — an Indonesian licence cannot be issued without registration

 ✓Buying and registering a vehicle — a NIK is required

 ✓Moving to a KITAP — unbroken registration forms part of your residence history

## STM: registering with the police

 Surat Tanda Melapor certifies that a foreigner has notified the police of their address. It is issued by the local station covering where you actually live.

 ✓Filed first: an SKTT will not be issued without it

 ✓You need a passport copy, a KITAS copy and proof of address

 ✓Your sponsor is usually involved — the same guarantor as on the KITAS

 An STM is tied to a specific address. Move to another area and the registration must be redone, not left in place «until the next extension».

## SKTT: the Dukcapil certificate and your NIK

 Surat Keterangan Tempat Tinggal is issued by Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil, the civil registry office. This is where your NIK, the Indonesian identifier, comes from.

 FilingYou apply at the Dukcapil office covering your address, already holding the STM and the KITAS.

 DocumentsPassport copy, KITAS copy, a guarantee letter from your sponsor with a copy of their KTP, and two colour photos 3×4 cm.

 ProcessingBetween 3 and 10 working days depending on the office's workload.

 IssueYou receive the SKTT with a NIK assigned. That number stays with you and is used from then on.

## What happens if you skip it

 There is rarely a fixed on-the-spot fine for having no SKTT, but the trouble arrives from another direction.

 !At KITAS extension the missing registration surfaces and stalls the filing

 !A bank may decline an account, and a dealership may refuse to register a vehicle to you

 !Moving to a KITAP means explaining any gaps in your registration history

 !In a dispute over a rental or with the police, an unregistered address works against you

## How not to lose the two weeks

 Practical advice: handle registration while you are house-hunting, not after.

 ✓Prepare the rental agreement or proof of address early — neither STM nor SKTT works without it

 ✓Your sponsor is needed at both steps: stay in touch rather than calling on the last day

 ✓If the KITAS was issued abroad the clock runs from entry — plan your first week on the island around that

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How long do I have to register?
Fourteen days. The count starts from the date the KITAS is issued, or from your date of entry if the status was arranged outside Indonesia.

Вопрос: What is the difference between STM and SKTT?
The STM is the police notification of your address and comes first. The SKTT is the certificate from the Dukcapil civil registry, issued on the basis of the STM and the KITAS, and it carries your NIK personal number.

Вопрос: What does the NIK give me?
It is the Indonesian resident identifier. It is used for banking, vehicle registration and driving licences, and it forms part of your residence history when moving to a KITAP.

Вопрос: How long does an SKTT take?
Between 3 and 10 working days after filing, depending on the workload of the particular Dukcapil office.

Вопрос: Do I need to re-register when I move?
Yes. Registration is tied to the address: moving to another area means filing again rather than carrying the old registration through to the next KITAS extension.

## We will handle the STM and SKTT while you settle in

 Give us your address and the date your KITAS was issued — we will time it and gather the documents.

# Taxes in Indonesia: the 183-day rule

 A foreigner becomes an Indonesian tax resident by residing here, by spending more than 183 days in the country within 12 months, or by having documented intent to reside. Part of a day counts as a full day. Intent is evidenced by documents — among them a VITAS or KITAS valid beyond 183 days and a lease of the same length. This is reference material, not tax advice.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Three ways to become a tax resident

 The rules for determining tax residency are set out in Directorate General of Taxes regulations. A foreigner becomes an Indonesian tax resident if any one of three conditions is met:

 ✓They reside in Indonesia — meaning a home here that is not merely a stopover, or a centre of their main personal, social, economic or financial interests

 ✓They are in Indonesia more than 183 days within a 12-month period

 ✓They are in Indonesia during a tax year and intend to reside here

 How the 183 days are counted. The period runs across any 12 months, the days may be consecutive or broken, and part of a day counts as a full day. Your arrival and departure days each count in full.

## What counts as intent to reside

 This is the most underrated limb: you can become a resident without reaching 183 days if documents show intent. The rules list what proves it:

 ✓A VITAS — an entry visa valid for more than 183 days

 ✓An ITAS (KITAS) — a limited stay permit valid for more than 183 days

 ✓A contract for work, business or activity in Indonesia lasting more than 183 days

 ✓Other documents — for example a housing lease longer than 183 days, or papers showing your family has relocated

 The practical read: taking a one-year KITAS gives you a document that in itself signals intent to reside. That does not mean tax arises automatically, but your position is assessed under different rules from a tourist's.

## Who stays a non-resident

 A foreigner remains a foreign tax subject if they are in Indonesia no more than 183 days within 12 months and meet neither the residence nor the intent test.

 ✓A holiday, short trips, a stay of under six months — usually non-residence

 ✓A multiple-entry visa does not make you a resident by itself: actual days in the country are what count

 ✓Leaving interrupts your presence but does not reset the counter — days accumulate across 12 months

## What follows from the status

 Residents and non-residents are taxed differently, and the difference is fundamental.

 ✓A tax resident becomes a taxpayer where income has been received — from Indonesia or abroad — and exceeds the non-taxable threshold

 ✓A non-resident answers only for Indonesian-source income

 ✓Certain categories of foreigner fall under a regime taxing only Indonesian-source income — but it comes with conditions to be checked against your own case

 If your country has a double taxation agreement with Indonesia, your status is determined under that agreement rather than by the domestic rules alone.

## What we do not do

 We are a visa agency. We do not give tax advice or make calculations — that is a separate profession carrying separate liability.

 !We do not compute your tax base or file returns

 !We do not recommend 'structures' — they always cost more than they appear to

 !We are not a substitute for a tax adviser who knows both Indonesian rules and your home country's

 What we do: keep company books and match you to the right visa status. If your timeline is approaching 183 days we will say so plainly — so you can talk to a specialist before, not after.

 How many days each visa actually gives you is set out in our visa-free explainer and C1 versus e-VOA comparison.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: After how many days does a foreigner become an Indonesian tax resident?
More than 183 days within 12 months. The days may be consecutive or broken, and part of a day counts as a full day — so arrival and departure days each count in full.

Вопрос: Can I become a resident before 183 days?
Yes. Residency also arises from intent to reside, evidenced by documents: a VITAS or KITAS valid for more than 183 days, a contract longer than 183 days, a housing lease of the same length, or papers showing your family has moved.

Вопрос: Does a KITAS make me a tax resident automatically?
A KITAS valid for more than 183 days is named in the rules as a document evidencing intent to reside. The actual consequences depend on your circumstances and on any treaty between your country and Indonesia — a question for a tax adviser.

Вопрос: Does a non-resident pay tax in Indonesia?
A non-resident answers for Indonesian-source income. Income from abroad is not subject to Indonesian tax under that status.

Вопрос: Do trips out of the country count?
Presence is counted as actual days across any 12 months, and they accumulate even when broken up. Leaving interrupts your stay but does not reset the days already counted.

 We will tell you how many days each visa really gives you, and flag it if you are heading for the threshold.

# US visa from Bali: filing in Jakarta

 A US visa can be obtained without flying home: interviews run in Jakarta and Surabaya, and residents with a KITAS get priority when booking. The fee is USD 185 today, but a further USD 250 is expected before 30 September 2026 — taking the total to 435.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The short answer

 A US visa is filed not by citizenship but wherever you can attend the interview. Indonesia accepts applications, and you do not have to live here — though residency helps.

 ✓Two cities — the embassy in Jakarta and the consulate in Surabaya

 ✓Residents get priority in slot allocation, but booking without a KITAS is realistic too

 ✓Personal appearance is required: the interview is in person, with no remote option

 ✓The interview is in English; an interpreter is allowed, but their entry is agreed in advance

 Appointment booking opens only after the consular fee is paid. Until the payment clears you will not see any slots — the first thing that trips up anyone trying to «just check the dates».

## Fees: 185 dollars now, 435 soon

 The standard fee for a B1/B2 tourist or business visa is USD 185. A second part is about to take effect.

 4 July 2025Legislation was signed introducing a Visa Integrity Fee of USD 250 on top of the base fee.

 As of mid-2026The fee is not being collected yet. Collection is expected before the end of the fiscal year, that is by 30 September 2026.

 What followsThe total cost of a B1/B2 visa rises from 185 to USD 435.

 ✓The new fee is paid when the visa is issued, not on entry

 ✓Applicants who are refused do not pay it

 ✓The amount is indexed to inflation — USD 250 is a floor, not a fixed figure

 Formally the fee is refundable: a holder who complied with every visa condition may claim it back after expiry. No refund mechanism exists at the time of writing, so do not count on that money.

## How the process runs

 The DS-160 formCompleted online. The data must match your passport letter for letter — discrepancies surface at the interview, the worst possible place for a surprise.

 Paying the feeUSD 185. Only then does the appointment calendar open.

 Booking the interviewSlots in Jakarta and Surabaya. Indonesian residents get priority, so a KITAS usually means better dates.

 The interviewArrive no earlier than 15 minutes before your time. Bring a colour 5×5 cm photo, the interview appointment letter, the DS-160 confirmation and the payment receipt.

 The decisionAnnounced at the interview. If approved, your passport stays at the consulate for the visa foil.

## What strengthens a resident's application

 The interview always circles one question: will you come back. Residency in Indonesia works in your favour — it shows your life is built somewhere other than the US.

 ✓A valid KITAS or KITAP — proof of legal status and ties to your country of residence

 ✓Work or business — a contract, a company, PT PMA documents

 ✓Housing — a lease, and better still an SKTT registration

 ✓Family with you — a spouse and children on family KITAS count in your favour

 ✓Travel history — visas from other countries and a clean record of respecting their terms

 !A KITAS issued a week before filing answers few questions

 !An empty passport makes the conversation harder but does not make refusal inevitable

## Where else you can file from Bali

 Residency in Indonesia opens applications elsewhere too — the procedures and the effort differ.

 ✓Schengen via Bulgaria — the one working route for Russian citizens, filed in Jakarta

 ✓Australia visa — entirely online, no consulate visit, AUD 200

 ✓Japan visa — the visa centre is in Denpasar, no Jakarta trip needed

 ✓China, Korea and Singapore — where entry is free, where K-ETA applies and where a visa is not

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do I need a KITAS to apply for a US visa in Indonesia?
Formally no: being in the country lawfully is enough. But residents get priority for interview slots, and a valid KITAS strengthens the application by showing ties to where you live.

Вопрос: What does a B1/B2 visa cost?
USD 185 today. An additional Visa Integrity Fee of USD 250 was signed into law on 4 July 2025 but is not yet collected; it is expected by 30 September 2026, taking the total to USD 435.

Вопрос: Where does the interview take place?
At the US embassy in Jakarta or the consulate in Surabaya. Booking opens only after the consular fee is paid, so you cannot preview available dates.

Вопрос: What language is the interview in?
English. You may bring an interpreter, but their entry to the embassy is arranged in advance — turning up with one unannounced will not work.

Вопрос: Is the fee refunded if I am refused?
No. The USD 185 consular fee is non-refundable whatever the outcome. The new USD 250 fee works the other way: it is charged only when a visa is issued, so a refusal means you do not pay it.

# Converting a visa to a KITAS: without flying out

 A visit visa can be changed into a residence KITAS without leaving the country. One rule applies: you move upward, to residency, but never from one visit visa to another. The Bridging Visa covers the gap — 60 days of lawful waiting with no fines. From visa-free entry conversion is not possible at all.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## One rule: upward only

 Changing status inside the country is possible, but not in every direction. Moving from a visit visa to a residence status works; swapping one visit visa for another does not.

 ✓Visit visa → KITAS — the working scenario: from an e-VOA, C1, C2, D1/D2 or D12 to an investor, family, work or remote-worker status

 ✓D12 → investor KITAS — the classic: study the market, register a PT PMA, move to residence

 ✓C6 → KITAS — possible provided the sponsor stays the same

 !Visit to visit is not allowed. A C1 does not become a C2, nor an e-VOA a C1 — a different visit visa requires leaving

 !From visa-free entry, nothing at all. No extension, no change of status: visa-free explained

## The Bridging Visa: covering the gap

 The main fear when changing status is that the old visa expires before the new one is approved. That is what the bridging status is for.

 ✓It gives 60 days of lawful waiting inside the country

 ✓No overstay accrues during that time

 ✓It is issued only alongside an application for a new status — never on its own

 ✓It works only inside the country: fly out and it is gone

 The full explanation is in our Bridging Visa article. It is a bridge between two statuses, not a way to extend a holiday.

## What a conversion costs

 Moving from a visit visa to the E33G remote-worker KITAS costs IDR 16,000,000 turnkey. That covers the bridging permit, the filing and the status itself, with no exit from the country. Other KITAS categories depend on the grounds: a work contract, a company or a marriage are each processed differently and are priced separately.

## How a conversion runs

 Check the routeWe look at what you are moving from and to, and whether that move is allowed at all. Half the problems are solved here, before filing.

 Assemble the basisDifferent for each KITAS: PT PMA founding documents, an offer and employer permits, a marriage certificate, proof of income.

 File, with bridgingThe application for the new status, and with it the bridging status for the wait.

 KITAS issuedOnce approved, the limited stay permit is issued, with biometrics.

## Three mistakes that break a conversion

 !Starting in the final week. Conversion is not quick: assemble the basis, file, wait. Begin with room to spare, not with five days left

 !Entering visa-free. The most expensive mistake: status cannot change at all, so you must leave and re-enter on the right visa

 !Assuming the basis will appear along the way. No company yet, no offer yet, no registered marriage — nothing to convert into

 On timing specifically: the change-of-status function came under an anti-corruption investigation in 2026, and that affects processing speed. Allow more slack than usual.

## What to prepare in advance

 A conversion turns not on the filing but on the basis — the reason you would be granted residence at all. Assemble it before your current visa runs out.

 ✓Investor — a registered PT PMA and evidence of your share in its capital

 ✓Work — the employer's permits, RPTKA included, and your qualification documents

 ✓Family — a marriage or birth certificate with an English translation, plus the sponsor's documents

 ✓E33G — passport, selfie and address; the shortest pack of them all

 Check your passport separately: annual statuses have stricter validity requirements than visit visas. Explained in our passport rules article.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Which visas convert to a KITAS?
Visit visas: the e-VOA, C1, C2 and the D1/D2 and D12 multiple-entry visas. You can move to an investor, family, work or remote-worker status. From visa-free entry a change of status is prohibited.

Вопрос: Can I swap a C1 for a C2 inside the country?
No. One visit visa does not become another — that requires leaving and re-entering on the visa you want.

Вопрос: What is the Bridging Visa?
A transitional status of 60 days for people already in the country awaiting approval of a new permit. No overstay accrues meanwhile. It is issued only together with an application.

Вопрос: Does bridging expire if I fly out?
Yes. The status works only inside the country; leaving cancels it.

Вопрос: How long does a conversion take?
It depends on the KITAS type and how complete your basis is. In 2026 the change-of-status function is busier than usual, so start early rather than in your final weeks.

## We will check your conversion route before you file

 We tell you honestly whether the move is possible from your visa, what to assemble and how much time to allow.

# Bali Visa Extension in 2026: Every Type, Terms and Rules

 Almost every Indonesian visa can be extended without leaving: the eVOA once for 30 days, the C1 and C2 twice for 60 days each, the D12 once for a full 180. Since June 2025 every extension requires an in-person biometrics visit at an immigration office, so apply at least 7–10 working days ahead. Overstaying costs IDR 1,000,000 per day per person.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What can be extended, and for how long

 The rule is simple: an extension never changes your visa type — it only adds days within that visa's own limit. Once the limit is used up, the options are leaving the country or switching to a different status.

 ✓eVOA / VOA — 1 extension of 30 days, 60 days maximum. With us, turnkey — IDR 950,000, the IDR 500,000 government fee included. Step by step in our eVOA extension guide.

 ✓C1 tourist visa — 2 extensions of 60 days, 180 maximum. With us, turnkey: IDR 2,500,000 over 10 working days or IDR 3,500,000 over 5–6. Processed via a sponsor; details on the C1 page.

 ✓C2 business visa — 2 extensions of 60 days, 180 maximum, same scheme as the C1; with us — IDR 2,800,000 turnkey. More on the C2 page.

 ✓Multiple-entry D1/D2 — the stay within each entry is extendable. With us: IDR 2,600,000 when filed 6+ working days ahead, IDR 3,100,000 urgent. About the visa itself — D1/D2.

 ✓D12 Pre-Investment — 1 extension of 180 days, up to 360 per entry: IDR 5,000,000 turnkey. An existing company is not required to extend.

 ✓E33G remote-worker KITAS — extended for a further year without leaving, IDR 12,000,000 turnkey with us. Switching to it from an e-VOA or C1 in-country costs IDR 16,000,000 — a conversion through a Bridging Visa. How that works — in our E33G deep dive.

 ✓Annual KITAS — renewed via the sponsor for a fresh term: work IDR 15,000,000 per year, investor IDR 17,000,000 for two years, retirement IDR 12,000,000, family and student IDR 12,000,000 per year. Each status has its own guide in the blog.

## What each extension costs

 Prices are turnkey: government fees and our work are already inside, with nothing to top up at the office. Bali Levy is paid separately.

 Status | Extensions available | Our turnkey price | 
eVOA / VOA | once, 30 days | IDR 950,000 | 
C1 tourist | twice, 60 days each | IDR 2,500,000 · 3,500,000 rushed | 
C2 business | twice, 60 days each | IDR 2,800,000 | 
D1 / D2 multiple-entry | within each entry | IDR 2,600,000 · 3,100,000 rushed | 
D12 Pre-Investment | once, 180 days | IDR 5,000,000 | 
E33G KITAS | per year, in-country | IDR 12,000,000 | 
Work KITAS | per year | IDR 15,000,000 | 
Investor KITAS | two years | IDR 17,000,000 | 
Retirement KITAS | per year | IDR 12,000,000 | 
Family and student | per year | IDR 12,000,000 | 

 Price the stay, not the extension. One C1 extension costs less than a flight out and back for a fresh entry, and an annual KITAS often beats four extensions in a row. Not sure which route is cheaper in your case — run it through the visa finder.

## Biometrics: the visit you cannot skip

 Since June 2025 (circular IMI-417.GR.01.01) every extension of a visa or stay permit requires showing up in person: photo, fingerprints, a short interview. An agency can handle everything else — paperwork, filing, fees — but the biometrics trip is yours. Bali has five offices: Denpasar, Ngurah Rai (Jimbaran), Singaraja, Tabanan and Klungkung; which one is yours depends on where you live. Addresses and procedure — in our guide to Bali immigration offices.

## D12: use the visa for what it is meant for

 Extending a D12 does not require an existing company — it is granted to people whose PT PMA is still only a plan. But the purpose of the visa is specific: preparing an investment, researching the market and negotiating, rather than simply living on the island. Immigration has publicly reported deportations for using the D12 as a “lifestyle visa”. Full breakdown — in our D12 article; if a company is genuinely in your plans, look at setting up a PT PMA.

## When to apply, and what overstaying costs

 Apply at least 7–10 working days before your permit ends: processing takes 3 to 10 working days depending on the visa, and the biometrics slot adds waiting time of its own. Miss the deadline and the overstay clock starts: IDR 1,000,000 per day per person, children included; past 60 days it means detention, deportation and an entry ban. What to do if it has already happened — in our Bali overstay guide.

## FAQ

Вопрос: Can I extend my visa fully online, without visiting immigration?
No. The application is filed online, but since June 2025 biometrics (photo and fingerprints) are mandatory for every extension — at least one in-person visit is required.

Вопрос: How many times can the eVOA be extended?
Once, for 30 days — 60 days maximum in total. After that, the only options are leaving the country or a different visa arranged in advance.

Вопрос: Can the C1 be extended a third time?
No. The C1 grants 60 days plus two 60-day extensions — 180 days maximum. After that you must leave Indonesia.

Вопрос: Will a D12 be extended without a registered company?
Yes. A registered PT PMA is not required to extend a D12 that lists the applicant in the deed of establishment.

Вопрос: What happens if I overstay?
A fine of IDR 1,000,000 per day per person, children included. Overstaying beyond 60 days means detention, deportation and an entry ban.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

# Indonesia visa-free entry 2026: who qualifies

 Citizens of 19 countries and territories, plus Singapore permanent residents, enter Indonesia without a visa. On 9 July 2026 the list gained Turkey, Brazil, Peru, Kazakhstan, Macau and Belarus under ministerial regulation Permenimipas No. 10 of 2026. Visa-free entry gives you exactly 30 days, which cannot be extended and cannot be converted into a KITAS. Russia is not on the list — Russians still need an e-VOA or a C1 visa.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## The full visa-free list

 The list is maintained by Indonesia's Directorate General of Immigration. As of 25 August 2026 it holds 19 entries; the ones added in summer 2026 are highlighted in gold.

 ✓Brunei Darussalam

 ✓Malaysia

 ✓Thailand

 ✓Vietnam

 ✓Philippines

 ✓Cambodia

 ✓Singapore

 ✓Myanmar

 ✓Laos

 ✓Timor-Leste

 ✓Suriname

 ✓Colombia

 ✓Hong Kong

 ✓Turkey

 ✓Brazil

 ✓Peru

 ✓Kazakhstan

 ✓Macau

 ✓Belarus

 A twentieth entry covers foreigners holding Singapore permanent residence. For them visa-free entry works only through specific designated checkpoints, not every border post.

## What changed on 9 July 2026

 Minister of Immigration and Corrections Agus Andrianto signed regulation Permenimipas No. 10/2026 on 7 July; it was promulgated on 9 July. Six new subjects joined the list:

 ✓Turkey — the largest of the six by visitor numbers

 ✓Kazakhstan and Belarus — the first Russian-speaking countries on the list

 ✓Brazil and Peru — Latin America

 ✓Macau — special administrative region of China

 The basis is reciprocity: all six already admit Indonesians without a visa. The widely discussed visa waiver for Australia, China, Japan, South Korea and India did not make it into this regulation.

## Thirty days, full stop: three hard limits

 Visa-free entry looks like the easy option, yet it is the most limited entry status Indonesia offers. Three restrictions apply to everyone using it:

 !Exactly 30 days. Not working days, not roughly a month — 30 calendar days from the date of entry

 !No extension. Not once, not for any fee. The e-VOA can be extended; visa-free entry cannot

 !No change of status. Visa-free entry cannot become a KITAS — not a work, investor or family one

 Do the maths before you fly. Day 31 is an overstay: IDR 1,000,000 per day, per person. Hopping out and straight back in to reset the clock is a poor plan — immigration tracks these visa runs, and past 60 consecutive days the questions at the border start.

## What to take when 30 days is not enough

 The key point: you choose before departure. Once you have entered visa-free, you cannot change your mind inside the country — only leave and re-enter on the right visa.

 e-VOA · up to 60 days

 IDR 900,000

 all-in · 30 days + 30-day extension

 Arranged online before departure

 Opens the autogate, no payment queue

 Extends once without leaving the country

 In detail: the e-VOA guide

 C1 · up to 180 days

 from IDR 2,500,000

 60 days, extendable to 180

 The choice for a half-year stay

 Extends in 60-day steps, twice

 Compared: C1 or e-VOA

 D1 / D2 · multiple entry

 from IDR 5,000,000

 one year, up to 60 days per entry

 For several trips across the year

 No new visa before every flight

 Explained: D1 and D2 multiple-entry visas

 Planning to work, run a business or bring your family over? Neither visa-free entry nor a tourist visa covers that. Look at KITAS and KITAP: the permit is issued for your actual purpose, and you must enter on it.

## Russia and other countries off the list

 If your country is not on the list above, nothing has changed: you need a visa, and arranging it in advance is the sensible route. For Russians and most other Bali visitors that means the electronic visa on arrival — applied for online, delivered by email, with only your passport needed at the border.

 One planned change is worth knowing about. On 12 August 2026 immigration announced an intended fee increase: IDR 750,000 for an e-VOA arranged online before departure and IDR 1,000,000 for a visa obtained at the airport. Both currently cost IDR 500,000. No effective date had been set at the time of writing, but the direction is clear — arranging it in advance will cost noticeably less than queueing on arrival.

## What the border needs besides a visa

 These requirements are identical for visa-free entry and for every visa type:

 ✓A passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry

 ✓A return or onward ticket — checked by the airline at boarding and by immigration on arrival

 ✓Proof of accommodation: a hotel booking or your address in Indonesia

 ✓The All Indonesia declaration — filed online before landing, combining the immigration, customs and health forms

 ✓Bali's tourist levy of IDR 150,000 via the Love Bali portal: how and when to pay

 With a biometric passport and an approved electronic visa you can use the autogate — clearance takes roughly 15–25 seconds, and children aged 6 and over may use it too.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do Kazakhstan citizens need a visa for Bali in 2026?
No. Kazakhstan joined the visa-free list on 9 July 2026, so a tourist trip needs no visa. But visa-free entry gives you exactly 30 days and they cannot be extended. Planning to stay longer? Arrange an e-VOA or a C1 visa before you fly — you cannot switch to one after entering visa-free.

Вопрос: Can the 30 visa-free days be extended?
No. A visa-free stay permit cannot be extended at all — the rule is explicit. From day 31 you are overstaying, at IDR 1,000,000 per day per person. Only visa-based permits extend: the e-VOA once for 30 days, the C1 in 60-day steps up to six months.

Вопрос: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Indonesia?
Yes. Russia is not on the visa-free list. The standard holiday route is the electronic visa on arrival (e-VOA): 30 days, extendable once by another 30. For a longer stay people take the C1 visa — 60 days, extendable to 180.

Вопрос: Can I convert visa-free entry into a KITAS?
No. Switching from visa-free entry to a limited stay permit (KITAS) is not allowed. If your goal is a work, investor or family KITAS, you must enter on the matching visa arranged before departure.

Вопрос: What do I need to show at the border on visa-free entry?
A passport valid for at least 6 months, a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and a completed All Indonesia declaration. Bali's tourist levy of IDR 150,000 is paid separately through the Love Bali portal.

 Official sources: the Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia and the application portal evisa.imigrasi.go.id.
