# Visa runs from Bali: breaking the cycle

 A visa run is a flight out to obtain a fresh entry status. Over time the cycle gets expensive: flights, hotels, lost days and an officer's decision at every border. A year of visa runs approaches the cost of a residence status and loses to it outright on peace of mind. The way out is a four-step ladder: C1, a D multiple-entry, the E33G, and the matching KITAS.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What a visa run is and why it persists

 A visa run is a short flight out of the country in order to come back on a fresh entry status. It looks cheap for as long as you count only the visa and not the whole operation.

 ✓Return flights to the nearest country

 ✓A hotel night, transfers, food

 ✓A new visa on the way back

 ✓At least two days lost per cycle

## Doing the annual maths

 Take the e-VOA: 30 days plus one extension is 60 days per cycle, so roughly six cycles a year.

 ✓An e-VOA all-in — IDR 900,000, plus an extension with its IDR 500,000 fee

 ✓Six cycles means six visas, six extensions and six flights

 ✓A C1 — from IDR 2,500,000 gives 180 days; two cycles cover the year with one flight out

 ✓An E33G — IDR 12,000,000 for 12 months with no flights at all

 Even before airfares, a year of visa runs approaches the cost of a residence status. With airfares it overtakes it comfortably.

## The risk nobody prices in

 The main problem with visa runs is not financial. Entry is decided by an officer each time, and a history of frequent entries raises questions.

 !A long chain of short visits looks like living in the country without the matching status

 !Working on a visit visa is a leading cause of deportation from Bali: the figures

 !Visa-free entry cannot be extended at all — the cycle gets shorter and more conspicuous

## The ladder out

 Step 1 · C160 days with two 60-day extensions — up to 180 days without a single flight. From IDR 2,500,000.

 Step 2 · D1 or D2A one or two year visa with unlimited entries: you fly when it suits you, not when your status runs out. From IDR 5,000,000.

 Step 3 · E33GA year of residence for remote work with foreign clients. The visa question is closed.

 Step 4 · the matching KITASYour own business, family, or employment — investor, family or work.

## Picking your step

 The formula is simple and turns on two things: how many days a year you are here, and where your money comes from.

 ✓Up to six months a year, income from abroad — a C1 is enough

 ✓Flying in and out often — a D1 or D2

 ✓Living here and working remotely — the E33G

 ✓Running a business here or with family — the matching KITAS

 Work out your own case in the visa finder — four questions and a result with the price.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Are visa runs legal?
Leaving and re-entering on a fresh visa is not in itself a breach. But entry is decided by an officer, and a long history of short visits raises questions: it looks like living in the country without the matching status.

Вопрос: What does a year of visa runs cost?
On an e-VOA that is about six cycles: six visas at IDR 900,000, six extensions at the IDR 500,000 fee, plus flights and hotels. A year-long E33G at IDR 12,000,000 works out comparable, with no flights.

Вопрос: Can I do a visa run on visa-free entry?
Visa-free entry gives exactly 30 days and cannot be extended, so the cycle is half as long and twice as visible to immigration.

Вопрос: What should I choose if I live in Bali permanently?
A residence status matching your profile: E33G for remote work, investor for your own business, family if your spouse is Indonesian, work if employed.

Вопрос: How long can I stay without leaving?
60 days on an e-VOA, 180 on a C1. Visit visas do not go further — beyond that you need a KITAS.

## Get the status right and your next flight becomes a holiday

 Tell us how many days a year you spend here and where your income comes from — we will work out which status beats the runs on cost.

# Visa sponsors in Indonesia: who they are and why

 Most visas are filed not by the foreigner but through a sponsor — an Indonesian person or company that guarantees you before immigration. The sponsor files the application, issues the guarantee letter, handles every extension and answers for your breaches. Choosing a sponsor means choosing who every future extension depends on.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## Why a sponsor is needed at all

 Most Indonesian visas are filed not by the foreigner but through a penjamin — a sponsor, an Indonesian person or company that guarantees you before immigration. Sponsorship is governed by its own ministerial regulation on immigration guarantors.

 ✓They file your application in the immigration system — that route is closed to you

 ✓They issue the guarantee letter, formally vouching that you will comply with your visa terms

 ✓They file every extension — the C1, C2, D1/D2 and D12 cannot be extended without one

 ✓They answer to immigration for breaches: an overstay or unauthorised work is not only your problem

## Who can be a sponsor

 ✓Visit visas (C1, C2, D1/D2, D12) — an Indonesian company, usually a visa agency with a legal entity, sometimes a business host

 ✓Work KITAS — the employer, who obtains the RPTKA permits

 ✓Investor KITAS — your own PT PMA

 ✓Family KITAS — a spouse or parent who is an Indonesian citizen or holds a valid status

 ✓C6 — a sponsor with their own portal account, plus a letter from the host organisation

## Why choosing a sponsor matters

 A sponsor is not a one-off intermediary but the party every future extension depends on. If they stop responding, close down or simply drag their feet, your visa cannot be extended.

 !A vanished sponsor means no timely extension, which means an overstay

 !A sponsor with no legal entity and no track record is a risk that surfaces at renewal, not today

 !Cheap sponsorship 'through a friend' provides neither guarantees nor accountability

 We act as sponsor for our clients and track every visa in our system: deadlines are monitored, reminders come early, and extensions are filed with room to spare.

## How to change sponsor

 A change is possible but not a single click: immigration requires the previous guarantee to be closed in writing.

 ✓A statement from you that you no longer wish to be guaranteed by the previous sponsor

 ✓A release letter from the previous sponsor

 ✓A guarantee letter from the new one

 If the previous sponsor is unreachable the process drags — one more reason to choose a sponsor on reliability rather than price.

## How to vet a sponsor before you commit

 Sponsorship looks like a formality right up until the first extension. A few questions worth asking early:

 ✓Is there a legal entity? A registered Indonesian company, not a private individual with 'contacts'

 ✓Do they hold their own immigration portal account? Filing goes through it, and an intermediary in the chain is one more point of failure

 ✓How are deadlines tracked? Extensions are filed no later than the day the permit expires, and the reminder should come from them, not from you

 ✓What happens if plans change? Ask in advance how a release from the guarantee is handled

 The difference between a good and a bad sponsor shows up not at signing but months later — when your visa has a week left and nobody is answering emails.

 How sponsorship looks on specific visas is covered in our C1 and D12 guides.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do I need a sponsor for an e-VOA?
No, the electronic visa on arrival needs no sponsor. Sponsors are required for the C1, C2 and C6, the D1/D2 and D12 multiple-entry visas, and every type of KITAS.

Вопрос: Can an Indonesian friend be my sponsor?
For visit visas a company usually acts as sponsor. A private individual is possible in some scenarios, but the responsibility is identical — including answering to immigration for your breaches.

Вопрос: What happens if my sponsor disappears?
You cannot extend without them: the extension application is filed by the sponsor. A vanished sponsor turns quickly into an overstay.

Вопрос: Can I change sponsor?
Yes. You need a statement from you declining the previous guarantee, a release letter from the old sponsor, and a guarantee letter from the new one.

Вопрос: Is the sponsor liable for my breaches?
Yes, a guarantor answers to immigration for your compliance with the terms of your stay. An overstay or unauthorised work concerns both sides.

## Malina Visa — a sponsor with no surprises

 A legal entity, an account in the immigration system and deadline tracking. We file extensions early, not on the last day.

# Work KITAS 2026: employment, done lawfully

 The work KITAS bundles a work permit with a residence permit and is the only lawful way to take a job with an Indonesian company. Your employer sponsors it: first they obtain RPTKA approval, then a VITAS entry visa is issued, which converts into a KITAS with biometrics after you arrive. The term is usually 6–12 months.

 Updated: 25 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

## What the work KITAS is

 The work KITAS bundles a work permit with a residence permit. No other visa grants the right to work in Indonesia or earn income here: not a tourist visa, not a business visa, not a multiple-entry one.

 ✓The only lawful route into employment with an Indonesian company

 ✓Usually 6–12 months, set by the position, and renewable

 ✓Your employer is the sponsor, not you

 ✓Dependent family KITAS are issued for your spouse and children

## How the process runs

 It is a two-sided process: some steps are the employer's, some are yours. And it starts not with a visa but with permits on the company's side.

 Employer approvalThe company obtains approval to engage a foreign worker — the RPTKA and related permits. Nothing moves until that exists.

 VITAS entry visaOn the strength of those permits, a VITAS entry visa is issued.

 ArrivalYou enter Indonesia on the VITAS itself — not on a tourist visa and not visa-free.

 Conversion to KITASAfter arrival the VITAS is converted into a KITAS; biometrics are mandatory.

 RenewalThe status is renewed as needed for as long as the employment relationship holds.

## The core limitation: you are tied to the employer

 The KITAS entitles you to work only for the sponsoring company. That is not a technicality — the whole permit structure is built around one specific employer and one specific role.

 !Freelancing and side work for other companies are not permitted on a work KITAS

 !Changing employer means redoing the permits and the KITAS itself

 !Changing role within the company may also require the permits to be revisited

 Working remotely for foreign clients? That is the E33G, not this. Hold a stake in your own company? The investor KITAS lets you run your own business without a separate work permit.

## Documents from both sides

 From the employee:

 ✓A passport with plenty of validity left

 ✓A personal photo

 ✓A degree or proof of qualifications and a CV — matched to the role's requirements

 From the employer:

 ✓The company's corporate documents

 ✓The RPTKA approval and its accompanying pack

 We prepare both sides — the employee's file and, together with their team, the employer's permits. Pricing is individual: it depends on nationality, position and timing.

## Common mistakes and how much time to allow

 The work KITAS is the longest of the visa processes, because it starts not with you but with your employer's permits. Most mistakes are about the order of the steps.

 !Flying in on a tourist visa to 'sort it out here'. The standard route is entry on the VITAS itself, issued on the strength of permits already granted

 !Starting with yourself rather than the company. Until the employer holds the RPTKA and its accompanying pack, the employee's documents settle nothing

 !Overlooking qualifications. The degree and CV are filed against the requirements of the specific role — a mismatch stalls the process

 !Assuming a KITAS transfers. Change employer and the whole thing is done again

 The practical takeaway: allow generous time and start with the employer. If the company is hiring a foreign worker for the first time, it makes sense to run both sides through one provider — the employee's file and the company's permits then come together in parallel rather than one after the other.

 Entry during processing is covered by the C18 visa, and changing status without leaving by conversion to a KITAS.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I work in Indonesia on a tourist visa?
No. Tourist, business and multiple-entry visas grant no right to work or earn inside the country. Working on a visit visa is one of the leading causes of deportation from Bali.

Вопрос: How long is a work KITAS valid?
Usually 6–12 months, with the exact term set by the position. It is renewable for as long as the employment relationship with the sponsoring employer continues.

Вопрос: What happens if I change employer?
The permits and the KITAS have to be redone: the whole structure is tied to one company and one role. You cannot simply move to another company on an existing KITAS.

Вопрос: Can I take side projects at the same time?
No. A work KITAS entitles you to work only for the sponsoring company. Freelancing and side work for other companies are not permitted on this status.

Вопрос: Can my family move with me?
Yes, dependent family KITAS are issued for your spouse and children for the term of your status. They do not carry the right to work.

## We will walk both sides through it

 We assemble the employee's file and help the employer with the RPTKA and related permits. We will send a quote within the hour.

# Bridging visa without leaving

 01 · PriceIDR 4,000,000All-in. An interim status for moving onto another visa or a KITAS.
02 · What it gives+60 days on a VOABeyond the standard 30+30 — and without leaving Indonesia.
03 · How it runsRemotelyDocuments are filed online; no immigration visit for verification.

 Updated: 28 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 A bridging visa is an interim status that solves something the ordinary rules do not allow: changing your visa or extending your stay without leaving Indonesia. Normally switching visa type means flying out and coming back on a new document. A bridging visa removes that flight.
The price is IDR 4,000,000 all-in. Documents are filed remotely, no in-person verification at immigration is required, and the stay permit is issued straight away.

## What it is used for

 The two main uses of a bridging visa.
 Scenario | What happens | Who it suits | 

 Extending a stay on a VOA | Adds another 60 days beyond the standard 30 + 30, with no departure | People who have used the single eVOA extension but are not planning to leave | 

 Changing status | Moving from a visit visa to a KITAS, or from one KITAS to another | People already in Indonesia switching status — for example from an investor KITAS to an E33G | 

 Extending a VOA without leaving is by far the most common use. A standard eVOA gives 30 days plus one 30-day extension; after that the ordinary route requires departure. A bridging visa adds 60 more days inside the country.

## Why the route is convenient

 All documents are filed remotely — there is nowhere to travel to

 No in-person verification at the immigration office

 The stay permit is issued immediately

 No flight out and back just to reset your status

 Note: biometrics for a subsequent visa extension remain mandatory — that is a separate procedure. A bridging visa removes the need to leave the country, not the need to attend biometrics.

## Price and timing

 Bridging visa, all-in

 IDR 4,000,000

 Government fees included

 Documents filed remotely

 No immigration office visit

 Stay permit issued immediately

 If you are applying for a KITAS while already in Indonesia, the bridging visa is part of the route: the same IDR 4,000,000 is added to the price of an investor or work KITAS for the onshore switch.

 Message us on WhatsApp
 Message us on Telegram

## Moving to a KITAS E33G: when you need it and when you don't

 Here is the detail that costs people money. The route depends on which document you are currently in the country on.

 From a C1 visa, conversion to E33G is direct — no bridging visa needed

 From an eVOA, there is no direct conversion: the move only works through a bridging visa, as a separate procedure with its own cost

 Common condition: at least 30 days must remain on your current visa. Later than that is too late to file.

## How it works

 We review your caseWe look at the document you are in the country on, how long is left on it and the status you need at the end, and say straight away whether a bridging visa is needed at all.

 We collect documentsYou send scans — everything is remote, with no office visit.

 We fileWe prepare and submit the application, pay the government fees and follow it through to a decision.

 You get the statusThe stay permit arrives immediately. We then start the application for your target visa or KITAS.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much does a bridging visa cost?
IDR 4,000,000 all-in, with government fees included. When it is part of a move onto a KITAS, that amount is added to the price of the KITAS itself.

Вопрос: How many days does it add?
Sixty days on top of what you already have. On an eVOA that means 30 days of the initial stay, 30 days of the extension and a further 60 days on the bridging visa — without leaving Indonesia.

Вопрос: Do I have to visit the immigration office?
Not for the bridging visa itself: documents are filed remotely and no in-person verification is required. Biometrics for an ordinary visa extension are a separate procedure and remain mandatory.

Вопрос: Can I move straight from an eVOA to a KITAS E33G?
Not directly. From an eVOA the move only works through a bridging visa. A C1 visa converts directly. In both cases at least 30 days must remain on the current visa.

Вопрос: Can I switch from one KITAS to another without leaving?
Yes — that is the second main use of a bridging visa, for example moving from an investor KITAS to a remote worker KITAS E33G.

# Business Services in Indonesia

## Business in Indonesia: where it starts

A foreigner can legally own a business in Indonesia through a PT PMA — a foreign-capital company. It grants the right to operate, earn income and hire staff, and serves as the basis for the Investor KITAS — the owner’s residence permit. The key decisions happen at the start: KBLI activity codes (they drive licensing), the ownership structure and the charter capital — mistakes in these three cost far more to fix than to avoid.

We support the full cycle: PT PMA registration (or a Local PT for partner structures), licences, the NPWP tax number, a bank account, retainer accounting — and, when needed, a proper company closure with no loose ends. Still studying the market? For long scouting visits there is the D12 visa — up to 180 days per entry with no company required.

Not sure where to begin — message us on WhatsApp or Telegram: we will unpack your case, suggest the company form, and quote the budget and timeline. The consultation is free.

 Business Services · Liquidation

# Closing a Company in Indonesia

 01 · OutcomeLegally cleanThe company is removed from the registries, obligations settled, history clean.
02 · TaxesReconciliation & NPWP removalWe close the tax side — liquidation’s longest and most critical stage.
03 · TruthAbandoning ≠ closingA dumped company stacks penalties and hits the owners — closure must be done right.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 Projects end — for different reasons: the market didn’t click, a partnership dissolved, the focus moved. But an Indonesian company doesn’t evaporate: while it sits in the registries it must file and pay, and misses pile into penalties and problems for directors and shareholders.
Proper liquidation is a multi-stage process: corporate resolutions, appointing a liquidator, public notices, settling with creditors, tax reconciliation and removing the company from every registry. We run it end to end, for PT PMA and Local PT alike.

## Key terms
A shareholders’ liquidation resolution (RUPS) and appointment of a liquidator
Public notices and settlements with creditors and employees
Tax reconciliation: closing obligations and revoking the NPWP — usually the longest stage
Revoking the NIB and licences in the OSS system
Striking the company from the Ministry of Law registry
A realistic full-liquidation timeline — several months to a year or more
Why you can’t just walk away: a dormant company still owes nil filings and LKPM. An abandoned one stacks penalties, stains the owners’ tax history and can resurface at future visas, companies and deals in Indonesia.

## Required documents
Incorporation documents and the latest amendments
NPWP, NIB and active licences
Financial and tax filings for recent periods
Employee, account and liability details
If the filings are behind, we rebuild them first: liquidation is impossible without a closed tax history.

## Pricing and timing
Pricing is calculated individually — it depends on citizenship, timing and your situation. Message us on WhatsApp or Telegram and we’ll send an exact quote within the hour.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I just stop using the company?
Technically yes, legally it’s the worst option: obligations don’t vanish, penalties grow, and the tail follows the directors and shareholders. Proper closure costs money and time — and ends it for good.

Вопрос: How long does liquidation take?
Several months to a year or more — the tax stage drives the timeline: reconciliation, a possible audit and NPWP revocation. We’ll give an exact forecast after an express audit of the company.

Вопрос: The company is behind on filings — now what?
Restoration first: we back-file the returns, settle the penalties and clean the history — only then does liquidation start. We do both parts.

Вопрос: Are there alternatives to closing?
Two: selling the company (if it holds value — licences, history, assets) or dormant mode with continued nil reporting. We’ll calculate which is cheaper in your case.

TITLE: EPO: Closing a KITAS in Indonesia, IDR 1,500,000

Home/Visas to Indonesia/EPO

 Status Closure · EPO

# Closing a KITAS with an EPO

 01 · Who it is forYou are in IndonesiaThe procedure for people still inside the country.
02 · PriceIDR 1,500,000All-in. An ERP for those who left costs the same.
03 · Afterwards7 days to flyYou must leave within that window.

 Updated: 28 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 EPO (Exit Permit Only) is the procedure for closing a KITAS while you are still in Indonesia. Immigration annuls the status and gives you a window to fly out.
Our all-in price is IDR 1,500,000. If you have already left and the KITAS is still open, you need the other procedure — ERP.

## How it works

 Closing a KITAS: EPO and ERP, August 2026.
 Procedure | Where you are | What happens | All-in price | 

 EPO | in Indonesia | the KITAS is annulled, seven days to fly out | IDR 1,500,000 | 

 ERP | outside the country | the KITAS is closed remotely | IDR 1,500,000 | 

 The only difference is where you physically are when filing. The price is the same.

 Close a KITAS via WhatsAppMessage us on Telegram

## What to know before filing

 Seven days to fly out after it is issued — after that, overstay starts

 The passport is submitted physically — you cannot travel while the procedure runs

 The KITAS is annulled immediately — you cannot return on it; entry requires a new visa

 It works on an expired KITAS too — an expired status still has to be closed, it does not lapse on its own

 Do not buy the ticket in advance. Procedure first, ticket second. While the passport sits with immigration, flying is physically impossible, and public holidays shift timelines easily. A ticket for the day after tomorrow is the single most common source of stress in closing a KITAS.

## When closing a KITAS is mandatory

 There are more situations than "leaving for good". Closing is required whenever the old status has to make way for a new one.

 Leaving Indonesia permanently — even with six months still left on the KITAS

 Changing KITAS type — say from an E33G to an investor KITAS once the company exists. The new status will not be issued while the old one sits in the system

 Changing employer — a work KITAS is not transferable between companies

 Closing the sponsoring company — liquidating the PT and closing the linked KITAS go together

## Why a KITAS cannot simply be abandoned

 The logic of "the term will run out and the status will fall away" does not hold. A stay permit lives in the immigration database independently of where you are, and a person has to close it, not the calendar.

 An unclosed KITAS stays active in the system even if you left a year ago

 While it is active, no new visa can be issued — including the eVOA many people count on as a fallback

 The sponsor remains formally tied to your status, and the questions reach them as well

## What to sort out before closing

 A KITAS drags a tail of linked things behind it, and they are easier to close while the status is still valid: a bank account, rental agreements, a driving licence, residence registration. Tell us what is open and we will put the steps in order.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much does an EPO cost?
IDR 1,500,000 all-in. An ERP — the procedure for people who have already left the country — costs the same.

Вопрос: How long do I have to leave after an EPO?
Seven days. You must fly within that window; after it, overstay begins at IDR 1,000,000 per day.

Вопрос: Will my passport be held?
Yes, the passport is physically submitted to immigration for the duration. While it is there you cannot fly — which is why the ticket is bought after the procedure, not before.

Вопрос: Do I need to close a KITAS that has already expired?
Yes. This is the most common misconception: an expired status still sits in the immigration database and blocks a new visa. An EPO works on an expired KITAS too.

Вопрос: Can I come back to Indonesia after an EPO?
Not on the closed KITAS — it is annulled. Entering again requires a new visa: an eVOA, a C1 tourist visa or a new KITAS.

Вопрос: What if I just fly out and leave the status open?
The KITAS stays active in the system. When you decide to return and apply for a new visa — including an ordinary eVOA — it turns out the old status was never closed. Unpicking that after the fact costs more time and money.

Home/Visas to Indonesia/ERP

 Status Closure · ERP

# Closing a KITAS with an ERP

 01 · Who it is forYou have leftFor people who departed with the status still open.
02 · PriceIDR 1,500,000All-in. An EPO for those still here costs the same.
03 · Your partNoneHandled in Indonesia under your power of attorney.

 Updated: 28 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 ERP (Exit Re-entry Permit) is the procedure for closing a KITAS when you have already left Indonesia and the status stayed open. It is handled remotely: you are abroad, we file here.
Our all-in price is IDR 1,500,000. If you are still in the country, you need the other procedure — EPO.

## How it works

 Closing a KITAS: ERP and EPO, August 2026.
 Procedure | Where you are | What happens | All-in price | 

 ERP | outside the country | the KITAS is closed remotely, without you | IDR 1,500,000 | 

 EPO | in Indonesia | the KITAS is annulled, seven days to fly out | IDR 1,500,000 | 

 The price is identical; what differs is where it is filed and how much you have to do.

 Close a KITAS via WhatsAppMessage us on Telegram

## What to know

 Your presence is not required — everything is done in Indonesia under a power of attorney

 The KITAS is closed — the status is annulled exactly as with an EPO

 You cannot return on it — despite "re-entry" in the name

 A ticket and exit stamp are needed — proof that you actually left

 About the name. The abbreviation misleads: historically "exit re-entry permit" meant permission to leave and come back. In KITAS-closing practice it refers to the offshore annulment procedure. If you plan to return, what you need is a new visa, not an ERP.

## When closing a KITAS is mandatory

 There are more situations than "leaving for good". Closing is required whenever the old status has to make way for a new one.

 Leaving Indonesia permanently — even with six months still left on the KITAS

 Changing KITAS type — say from an E33G to an investor KITAS once the company exists. The new status will not be issued while the old one sits in the system

 Changing employer — a work KITAS is not transferable between companies

 Closing the sponsoring company — liquidating the PT and closing the linked KITAS go together

## Why it surfaces later

 An unclosed KITAS does not stop you living abroad — it stops you coming back. While the status is active in the immigration database, no new visa can be issued, including an ordinary eVOA.

 It comes to light at the worst moment: once the tickets are booked and the visa application is in. Unpicking the history after the fact costs more than closing the status calmly and early.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much does an ERP cost?
IDR 1,500,000 all-in — the same as an EPO. The only difference between the two is where you are.

Вопрос: Do I need to be in Indonesia?
No. That is the whole point of an ERP: you are abroad while an agent or sponsor files here under your power of attorney.

Вопрос: Can I return on an ERP?
No. Despite the word "re-entry" in the name, this is a closing procedure, not a return one. A closed KITAS cannot be re-entered on — you need a new visa.

Вопрос: What is needed?
A ticket and an exit stamp, proving you actually left the country, plus a power of attorney and your KITAS documents.

Вопрос: I left a year ago and closed nothing. What now?
We arrange the ERP remotely. The sooner the better: while the status sits active, no new Indonesian visa can be issued, and that usually surfaces at the worst possible moment.

Вопрос: How is an ERP different from an EPO?
Only by where you are. An EPO is for people still in Indonesia, and it gives seven days to fly out. An ERP is for people who have already left, and it is done without them.

# Family KITAS

 01 · StatusA full residence permitLegal residence for spouses and children — renewed yearly without leaving the country.
02 · SponsorSpouse or parentSponsored by an Indonesian spouse or a family member holding a valid KITAS/KITAP.
03 · Daily lifeBank, licence, schoolA local bank account, a driving licence, school for the kids — resident-level life.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 The Family KITAS is a residence permit for families tied to Indonesia: foreign spouses of Indonesian citizens, and spouses and children of foreigners who already hold a KITAS or KITAP. The whole family lives in the country legally, under one clear status.
The process has two stages: first an entry visa (VITAS) is issued, then after arrival it is converted into a KITAS with photos and fingerprints at the immigration office. We manage both stages.

## Key terms
For spouses of Indonesian citizens and their minor children
For spouses and children of KITAS/KITAP holders — valid as long as the sponsor’s document
Renewed annually, with no need to leave the country
Children can be registered on a KITAS up to age 17
After 2 years of registered marriage to an Indonesian citizen you may qualify for a KITAP (permanent residence)
Note: a Family KITAS does not permit employment in Indonesia. Children, however, can attend school.

## Required documents
A passport with generous remaining validity
Marriage certificate with an English translation
Children’s birth certificates with English translations
Sponsor documents: passport/KTP, KITAS or KITAP, proof of funds
The exact list depends on who acts as sponsor — we’ll send yours after a short consultation.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Who can sponsor a Family KITAS?
An Indonesian spouse — for a foreign husband/wife and their children, or a foreigner holding a valid KITAS or KITAP — for their own spouse and children. The sponsor type determines the permit’s duration.

Вопрос: Can I work on a Family KITAS?
No — it does not permit employment. Working requires a Work KITAS through an employer. You can, however, live, open a bank account, get a driving licence and send children to school.

Вопрос: Do I have to leave the country to renew?
No — the annual renewal happens inside Indonesia. Start the process roughly 30 days before the current term expires.

Вопрос: What happens in case of divorce or the sponsor’s death?
The status is tied to the sponsor, so a sponsor change or a switch to another visa type is needed. It is solvable but takes time — reach out early and we’ll plan the transition.

Вопрос: When can I get a KITAP (permanent residence)?
Spouses of Indonesian citizens — typically after 2 years of registered marriage; holders of other KITAS types — usually after 5 years. We’ll map your scenario in a consultation.

## How Bali visas work: the short version

 Indonesia splits visas into three tiers. The first is short trips: eVOA gives you 30 days plus one 30-day extension. The second is long visits without residency: the C1 tourist visa and C2 business visa stretch to 180 days through extensions, while multiple-entry D1/D2 let you come and go for one to two years. The third is residency: KITAS E33G for people employed by companies abroad, investor and family KITAS, and after several years KITAP, permanent residence.

 Three rules that save money: a visa cannot be swapped for another without leaving the country (a few KITAS routes are the exception, and they run through a bridging visa), every extension since June 2025 requires biometrics in person at an immigration office, and overstaying costs IDR 1,000,000 per day per person. How each type is extended is covered on our visa extension page; what to do if you have already overstayed is in the overstay guide.

 Planning to work for yourself rather than just live here — that is what PT PMA is for, a company with 100% foreign ownership. It also opens the way to an investor KITAS and a local bank account. We publish breakdowns of every status, prices and rule changes in the blog, each article stamped with the date its facts were checked.

 The Investor KITAS is the residence permit for business owners in Indonesia: shareholders, directors and commissioners of PT PMA companies. It combines residency with the right to run your own company — no separate work permit required.
The basis is a registered PT PMA and your share in its capital (thresholds depend on your role and the company’s investment plan — typically a personal stake from ~IDR 1 billion with company capital from IDR 10 billion). No company yet? We’ll register one end to end.

Work in your own company — without a separate work permit

A path to KITAP with continuous status
The from-zero route: D12 for scouting → PT PMA registration → Investor KITAS. We support every step, licences and accounting included.

 Visa Service · Permanent

# KITAP — Permanent Residence

 01 · StatusIndonesian PRA 5-year card with automatic renewal — the visa routine ends here.
02 · PathYears of KITASFamily is the fastest route; work and investor lines take several years.
03 · RightsA foreigner’s maximumLong-term status stability, banking, property, peace of mind.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 KITAP is permanent residence — the top rung of Indonesia’s immigration ladder. The card is issued for 5 years and renews automatically: annual extensions, document runs and immigration-office visits become history.
There is no direct route to a KITAP — it comes after years of continuous KITAS. Fastest for spouses of Indonesian citizens (typically after 2 years of registered marriage); holders of work, investor and retirement KITAS qualify after several years of continuous status.

## Key terms
A 5-year card with automatic renewal
Basis — continuous KITAS: family (typically from 2 years of marriage), work/investor/retirement (after several years)
A multiple re-entry permit (MERP) covers trips abroad
The status lapses after prolonged absence without a valid permit
Maximum stability: no more annual visa routine
Strategy: the road to a KITAP is laid when you choose your first KITAS. Tell us your plans and we’ll map the route from day one.

## Required documents
A passport with generous remaining validity
A valid KITAS and your status history
Basis documents: marriage / company / employment / pension
Sponsor documents — per your route

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How many years until I can get a KITAP?
Spouses of Indonesian citizens — typically after 2 years of registered marriage. Work, investor and retirement lines — after several years of continuous KITAS; exact timing depends on your line and status history.

Вопрос: Can a KITAP be lost?
Yes — for instance after prolonged absence from Indonesia without a valid re-entry permit (MERP), or if the underlying basis ends. We’ll show you how to maintain it safely.

Вопрос: Does a KITAP grant the right to work?
Rights follow your line: work and investor routes — yes, within their basis; a family KITAP by itself grants no employment rights. We’ll assess your case individually.

Вопрос: Is this citizenship?
No — a KITAP is permanent residence, not a passport. But it is the most stable status a foreigner can hold in Indonesia.

Home/Visas to Indonesia/KITAS & KITAP

 Visa Service · Residency

# KITAS & KITAP

 01 · KITASTemporary residenceA limited-stay permit — resident status for 1–10 years depending on type.
02 · KITAPPermanent residenceA 5-year auto-renewing card — the reward for years of continuous KITAS.
03 · Choice8 routesWork, investment, family, retirement, remote work, the stage — a status for every life.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 A KITAS (ITAS) is Indonesia’s temporary residence permit: proper resident status with a bank account, a driving licence and life without visa runs. A KITAP is the next rung — permanent residence, reached through years of continuous KITAS.
There are several KITAS types, and choosing the right first status shapes the whole journey — all the way to permanence. All eight options are below; if you’re unsure which is yours, a short consultation saves months.

## Key terms
A KITAS is temporary residence; the basis depends on type: employer, company stake, family, age, income or capital
All KITAS grant resident rights: banking, rentals, a licence; work rights belong only to the work, investor and artist types within their basis
Renewals happen in-country, no exits required
A KITAP is permanent: a 5-year card with automatic renewal
The fastest KITAP route is the family line; others take several years of continuous status

## Pick your KITAS
1 year · E33GRemote Worker KITASResidence for employees of foreign companies — work from Indonesia legally.5–10 yearsSecond Home KITASThe longest residence — via proof of capital, no employment strings.1–2 yearsInvestor KITASFor PT PMA shareholders and directors — run your own company.ResidenceFamily KITASFor spouses and children of Indonesian citizens and KITAS holders.Residence + workWork KITASThe only route to legal employment — through an employer.55+Retirement KITASAnnual residency for retirement living — with a path to permanence.PerformingArtist KITASLegal fees for musicians, DJs and performers.PermanentKITAPPermanent residence: a 5-year card without the annual routine.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How is a KITAS different from a KITAP?
A KITAS is temporary, with its own term and renewals. A KITAP is permanent: a 5-year card renewing automatically, ending the annual routine. You convert to a KITAP after years of continuous KITAS.

Вопрос: Which KITAS should I start with?
It depends on your basis: employed by a foreign company — E33G; building a business — D12 then investor; joining a spouse — family; 55+ — retirement. Tell us a little about yourself and we’ll orient you in one conversation.

Вопрос: Do KITAS grant the right to work?
Only the purpose-built ones: work (with the sponsoring company), investor (in your own company) and artist (within the contract). The rest are residence without Indonesian work rights.

Вопрос: Can I switch from one KITAS to another?
Yes — statuses convert when your basis changes, e.g. from remote worker to investor after founding a company. We’ll carry you through without gaps.

Home/Business Services/Local PT (PMDN)

 Business Services · Local PT

# Local Company Local PT

 01 · ThresholdCapital from IDR 50MHundreds of times below the PT PMA bar — a fast, affordable start.
02 · OwnersIndonesian citizens100% of shares belong to Indonesian founders.
03 · Timing2 weeks — 2 monthsA clear, well-trodden registration and launch process.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 A Local PT (PT PMDN — Perseroan Terbatas Penanaman Modal Dalam Negeri) is a company fully owned by Indonesian citizens. It is Bali’s most common business format: a low capital threshold, a clear registration path and lighter regulatory load than a PMA.
For a foreign entrepreneur it is the working format for a joint project with an Indonesian partner you trust: the partner holds the ownership, you participate in legal roles. We are upfront about the risks of “nominee” schemes — see the questions below.

## Key terms
Owners — Indonesian citizens only (100% of shares)
Charter capital — from IDR 50 million; the capital class sets the company category
The standard route: KBLI → incorporation documents → NPWP → NIB → licences
Registration — 2 weeks to 2 months
A foreigner can work in the company on a Work KITAS arranged by it
Be clear-eyed: a Local PT is for projects with a genuine Indonesian partner. If ownership must stay with you — it’s a PT PMA, full stop.

## Required documents
A company name (2–3 options)
ID copies of the director and commissioner
A company address — or we arrange a legal address
An activity description for KBLI matching

## Pricing and timing
Pricing is calculated individually — it depends on citizenship, timing and your situation. Message us on WhatsApp or Telegram and we’ll send an exact quote within the hour.

## How it works

Data and documentsSend a passport-spread photo, a personal photo and a WhatsApp or Telegram contact.

Agreement and paymentWe prepare the agreement, you sign — and receive an invoice for the chosen package.

ProcessingAfter payment we file the documents and manage the application at every stage.

DeliveryThe finished document arrives with a notification and stays in your personal account.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can a foreigner own a Local PT?
No — only Indonesian citizens can hold PT PMDN shares. Any foreign share automatically makes the company a PT PMA.

Вопрос: What about putting shares in a nominee’s name?
We have to say it straight: nominee schemes give a foreigner no legal protection — on paper the company and its assets belong to the nominee, and in a dispute the court sides with the registered owner. If control matters, choose a PT PMA; if you have a real partner, a Local PT with properly drafted agreements.

Вопрос: Why pick a Local PT over a PMA for a joint project?
Entry bar and speed: capital from IDR 50 million versus 10 billion, lighter reporting (no LKPM), a faster launch. For a local business with a local partner it is the optimal format.

Вопрос: Can a Local PT become a PMA later?
Yes — when foreign capital enters, the company converts to a PT PMA, aligning capital and documents with foreign-investment requirements. We manage such transitions.

# Multiple-entry Visa D1 / D2

 01 · Validity1 or 2 yearsThe visa runs for one or two years — fly as often as you like.
02 · Per visit60 → 180 daysEach entry grants 60 days with two 60-day extensions.
03 · FreedomEnter anytimeA fresh 60 days starts on every arrival — no re-applying.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 D1 and D2 are multiple-entry visas for people living between two homes: valid for 1 or 2 years with unlimited entries and exits. Every arrival opens a fresh 60-day stay, extendable up to 180 per visit.
D1 covers tourist purposes, D2 covers business: meetings, negotiations, conferences. Processing is online, from any country.

## Key terms
Visa validity — 1 or 2 years, unlimited entries
Each visit — 60 days with two 60-day extensions (up to 180 per visit)
A fresh 60 days starts on each arrival date
D1 — tourist purposes, D2 — business purposes
Online processing, sponsor required
Note: like other visit visas, D1/D2 do not permit working or earning income in Indonesia.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How is D1 different from D2?
Only the purpose: D1 is tourism and personal trips, D2 is business activity (meetings, negotiations, conferences). The timing mechanics are identical.

Вопрос: What happens to my days when I exit?
The counter resets: the next arrival opens a fresh 60 days. Extensions apply within a single visit.

Вопрос: Can I stay the entire visa validity without leaving?
No — a single visit maxes out at 180 days (60 + two extensions). Then you exit; you can return even the next day while the visa is valid.

Вопрос: Who should pick D1/D2 over C1?
If you fly to Indonesia several times a year, the multiple-entry visa saves you re-applying for every trip. If the plan is one long uninterrupted stay, a C1 is enough.

 Tool · Overstay

# Overstay fine calculator

 An overstay in Bali costs IDR 1,000,000 for every day, per person. Enter the days and the number of people — the calculator works out the total and shows what changes past the 60-day threshold.

 How many days overdue?Days past the permit
People

The fine is IDR 1,000,000 per day of overstay, per person. Children count the same as adults.

## How the fine is calculated
There is one rate and it does not depend on your visa type or the reason for the delay: IDR 1,000,000 for every day past your permit, per person. Children count the same as adults, so a family of four multiplies the total by four.
Calendar days count, not working days. The clock starts the day after your stay permit expires.

## The 60-day threshold
Up to 60 days overdue — it is settled with a fine, paid on departure
Beyond 60 days — it stops being a financial question: immigration measures apply, up to deportation and a re-entry ban
Do not let it run. The longer the overstay, the fewer options remain. If your permit has expired or is about to, write to us today and we will look at your situation.

## How to avoid an overstay
An extension is filed no later than the day your current permit ends, and no earlier than 14 days before
If payment clears before expiry, no overstay accrues — even if the office visit comes later
Processing takes up to 3 working days after payment, so file with time to spare
The new period starts the day after the old one — no days are lost
With our support the dates are our problem: every visa is tracked, reminders come early, and extensions are filed with headroom.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How much does a day of overstay cost in Bali?
IDR 1,000,000 for each day, per person. The rate does not depend on your visa type, and children count the same as adults.

Вопрос: When is the fine paid?
For an overstay of up to 60 days it is paid when you leave the country. Beyond 60 days a payment no longer settles it — immigration measures apply.

Вопрос: Do children count?
Yes, exactly as adults do. For a family the total is multiplied by the number of people, infants included.

Вопрос: What should I do if my permit has already expired?
Do not wait. The sooner you get in touch the more options remain, particularly while the overstay is still under 60 days. Write to us and we will assess your situation.

Вопрос: Can a visa be extended retroactively?
No. The application must be filed no later than the day your current permit ends. After that date an extension is no longer possible and the overstay begins.

 Business Services · PT PMA

# Foreign-Investment Company PT PMA

 01 · ControlUp to 100% ownershipA foreigner legally owns the company — the share depends on the sector.
02 · StatusInvestor KITASThe company gives owners a route to residence, banking and insurance.
03 · Timing2 weeks — 2 monthsThe typical registration window with documents in hand.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 PT PMA (Perseroan Terbatas Penanaman Modal Asing) is the core, most reliable format for a foreign investor in Indonesia. Any foreign share — 1% or 100 — makes a company foreign, and revenue-generating activity is open to foreigners only through it.
A PT PMA unlocks the full set: legal business and contracts, a corporate bank account, Investor KITAS for the owners, hiring, and market participation on par with Indonesian companies.

## Key terms
Charter capital — from IDR 10 billion (how it is declared and evidenced depends on the structure — we’ll unpack it in consultation)
A minimum of two shareholders (individuals or entities), a director and a commissioner
The permitted foreign share depends on the activity (KBLI): many sectors allow 100%, some carry investment-list caps
A legal address is mandatory; a virtual office is acceptable in many cases
Registration — 2 weeks to 2 months
The key step is the right KBLI: the classification defines both the ownership ceiling and the licence set. Getting it wrong means re-registration — we match the codes to the goal from day one.

## Required documents
Passports of shareholders and officers
A company name (several options) and an activity description
A registration address — or we arrange a legal/virtual office
The ownership structure: shares, director, commissioner

## Pricing and timing
Pricing is calculated individually — it depends on citizenship, timing and your situation. Message us on WhatsApp or Telegram and we’ll send an exact quote within the hour.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can a foreigner own 100% of the company?
In many activities — yes. Certain sectors carry a foreign-share cap under the investment list. We’ll check your KBLI and give the exact figure before you start.

Вопрос: Do I have to deposit IDR 10 billion right away?
10 billion is the PT PMA charter-capital requirement; how it is declared and evidenced depends on structure and sector. It’s a central planning question — we’ll lay out the options honestly in consultation.

A route to the Investor KITAS (residence with the right to run your own company), corporate and personal bank accounts, local insurance — and a legal foundation for life and business in Indonesia.

Monthly taxes, the quarterly LKPM investment report, the annual return — even a dormant company must file. We pick this up with the accounting retainer.

Вопрос: I only need a presence, no revenue
Then a PT PMA isn’t required — a representative-office format exists for presence without commercial activity. We’ll tell you which fits your case.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Do I qualify as a freelancer?
The core E33G scenario is a contract with a foreign company. Freelance cases are assessed individually — much depends on income structure and paperwork. Message us and we’ll give you an honest read.

Вопрос: Can I take projects from Indonesian clients?
No — income from Indonesian sources is prohibited under this status. Foreign employers and clients only.

Вопрос: What about my family?
A spouse is covered by code E31B and children under 18 by code E31E — dependent permits attached to yours, so they live with you legally and the kids attend school. IDR 11,000,000. They are filed once your own E33G has been issued and run until your status expires.

Вопрос: Why E33G over a C1 tourist visa?
It is resident status: no exits every six months, with a bank account, a licence and in-country renewal. Crucially, remote work from Indonesia is legal on it — on a tourist visa it sits in a grey zone.

Вопрос: What income is required for the E33G?
The threshold is USD 60,000 a year from foreign sources: salary, contracts or freelance payments from outside Indonesia.

Вопрос: Can I apply while already in Bali?
Yes, via the onshore route — switching from your current visa without flying out. From a C1 the conversion is direct; from an e-VOA it runs through an intermediate Bridging Visa; from visa-free entry it is not possible. At least 30 days must remain on your current visa.

Вопрос: What if I start working with Indonesian clients?
That breaches the status terms: risk of KITAS revocation and deportation. For local income you need a work KITAS or your own PT PMA with an investor KITAS.

## How the process works: four steps

 ✓Message us — send three files: passport photo page, a selfie, and your Bali address as plain text. We will then tell you what your employment contract and income proof must show

 ✓We check eligibility — employer or clients abroad, income from USD 60,000 a year, passport valid 6+ months

 ✓We file the application — the offshore route takes 7–9 working days; onshore (you are already in Bali) means switching from your current visa without flying out

 ✓You receive the e-KITAS — and live for a year with no 60-day extensions and no visa runs

## E33G or another status: how to choose

 Every residence status solves the same problem — living in Indonesia legally. What differs is the basis: where your money comes from.

 Indonesian residence statuses, August 2026. Prices are ours, turnkey, in IDR.
 Status | Basis | Term | Threshold | Turnkey price | Sponsor | 

 E33G remote worker | foreign employer | 1 year | USD 60,000 / year | 12,000,000 | not needed | 

 E28A investor | stake in your company | 1–2 years | IDR 10bn | on request | required | 

 E23 work | hired by a local company | up to 2 years | job offer | on request | employer | 

 E33 Second Home | capital | 5 years | USD 130,000 | on request | not needed | 

 E33E Silver Hair | age 55+ and income | 5 years | USD 50,000 | on request | not needed | 

 E33F retirement | age 55+ and income | 1 year | USD 3,000 / month | on request | required | 

 What sets the E33G apart: the money arrives from abroad and no sponsor is needed. Income from Indonesian sources is prohibited on it — earning locally requires the E23 work permit or the E28A investor route.

## Who it fits — and who it does not

 The E33G is built for two scenarios: you are employed by a foreign company, or you freelance for clients whose payments come from outside Indonesia. The key threshold is income from USD 60,000 a year. The status does not fit if your money comes from Indonesia: working for a local company, trading, services or renting out property inside the country are prohibited — immigration reads this broadly, down to Instagram promotions (see our legal remote-work guide). For local income there are other routes: a work KITAS from an employer or an investor KITAS via your own company. Not sure which status is yours — start with the visa selection guide.

## What happens after 12 months

 The E33G is extended for a further year, and you do not leave the country to do it. With us the extension costs IDR 12,000,000 turnkey — the same as issuing it in the first place. Spouses and children stay on their family KITAS tied to your status.

 How the timing works: you apply while you are in Indonesia, and the filing window is the last 30 days of your permit: no earlier than 30 days before it expires and no later than the day it does. In our experience the procedure takes 3–4 weeks, and you should not plan a trip out during that time. While the application is under review you remain in the country legally on the strength of it. If your KITAS expires while you are abroad, it stops working — you cannot return on it and will have to apply for a new visa from outside the country. It will still need closing through the ERP procedure: in the immigration database it stays open and blocks new applications. That is exactly why we track every deadline in our CRM.

 If you no longer need the status — you are leaving for good or moving to a different KITAS — it has to be closed officially: simply flying out is not enough. We covered how in our guide to EPO and ERP; closing costs IDR 1,500,000 with us.

 Switching to the E33G from a visit visa is a separate route. You do not need to leave Bali, but the path depends on the document you currently hold. From a C1 visa the conversion is direct. From an e-VOA there is no direct conversion: it goes through an intermediate Bridging Visa, which is a separate procedure. From visa-free entry you cannot switch at all. In both available cases at least 30 days must remain on your current visa. Conversion costs IDR 16,000,000 turnkey.

Income — from USD 3,000 per month: a pension, annuity or other regular source
A three-month bank statement showing at least USD 2,000
A sponsor is required — a licensed agency acts as one; this status cannot be arranged alone
Selling goods or services directly inside Indonesia is not allowed; the path to KITAP opens at 60
The age is 55, not 60. Half the market still writes 60 — that figure applies not to the visa but to converting into permanent KITAP. The 55 threshold is set in the 2025 ministerial decree on visa classification.

## Required documents
A passport valid for at least 6 months
A personal photo
Proof of income from USD 3,000 per month
A three-month bank statement showing at least USD 2,000
A short CV and your travel itinerary
A sponsor guarantee letter — we prepare this
Health insurance and a housing lease are not required. Some agencies still ask for them out of habit: those items are left over from the old retirement regime under index C319, which has been abolished.

## There is a five-year version — with no sponsor

 Retirement status comes in two forms, and almost everyone on the market shows only the first.

 E33FAnnualOne year with renewals, up to five years in total. A sponsor is required — that is us. No deposit. This is what the page above describes.

 E33ESilver Hair, 5 yearsFive years upfront instead of annual renewals, and no sponsor at all. In exchange: a USD 50,000 deposit in an Indonesian state bank.

 Age and income requirements are identical: 55 and over, from USD 3,000 a month. The difference is the term, the sponsor and the deposit. Full breakdown of the five-year route on the Silver Hair KITAS E33E page.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: Can I do a little work on a Retirement KITAS?
Selling goods or services directly inside Indonesia is prohibited under this status — that is the core restriction. The law does formally allow other activity, but only through a separate notification to immigration about combining activities (rangkap kegiatan), and on the retirement track almost nobody goes through it. If you plan to earn, it is more honest to look at the E33G for remote work with a foreign company, or the investor KITAS E28A.

Вопрос: My spouse is 52 — what then?
The law lets a retirement status holder bring family, and the spouse is issued a separate dependent KITAS under its own code, not the retirement one. The spouse’s age does not matter. One important detail: the income requirement is counted per person, not per couple. It is a non-standard case, so we will work through it in a consultation before you pay for anything.

Вопрос: How painful are the annual renewals?
Routine we take off your hands: we remind you in advance, gather the papers and run the process without you standing in queues.

Вопрос: When can I apply for a KITAP?
After several years of continuous retirement status — permanent residence removes the annual renewals. We’ll get you there.

TITLE: Silver Hair KITAS E33E: 5 Years in Bali | Malina Visa

Home/Visas to Indonesia/Silver Hair KITAS

 Visa Service · 55+ · E33E

# Silver Hair KITAS E33E

 01 · TermFive years upfrontNo annual renewals and no yearly trips to immigration.
02 · SponsorNot requiredThe only retirement status that does not tie you to an agency.
03 · ConditionUSD 50,000 depositIn your own account at an Indonesian state bank.

 Updated: 27 August 2026 · Verified by the Malina Visa team

 Silver Hair is the five-year version of Indonesia's retirement residence permit, officially part of the Golden Visa programme. In the immigration classification it carries the code E33E; its full name is Visa Rumah Kedua Lansia Untuk 5 Tahun — the "second home visa for seniors, five years".
Two things set it apart from the ordinary retirement KITAS: the term is granted for five years at once, and no sponsor is required at all. In exchange, you place a deposit in an Indonesian state bank.

## How it differs from the annual route

 Age and income requirements are the same across both retirement statuses. The difference is the term, the sponsor and the money.

 Age — 55 and over in both cases

 Income — from USD 3,000 a month in both cases

 Term — 5 years on the E33E against 1 year on the E33F

 Sponsor — not needed on the E33E, mandatory on the E33F

 Deposit — USD 50,000 on the E33E, none on the annual route

 Maximum total — up to 10 years on the E33E, up to 5 on the annual one

 The real difference is independence, not the term. An annual retirement KITAS cannot be arranged without a sponsoring agency, and changing agency means losing the years you have accrued. Silver Hair removes that dependency entirely: the status is yours, not held "through someone".

## How the deposit actually works

 This is the part almost everyone describes wrongly, promising you simply "put down fifty thousand dollars". The real sequence is different:

 At applicationThe money is not needed yet. You sign a written commitment to place the deposit — surat pernyataan komitmen.

 After entryWithin 90 days you open an account at an Indonesian state bank in your own name, deposit the sum and report it to immigration.

 ThereafterThe deposit must stay in place for the whole term of the status. The balance can be checked.

 The account must be personal — a joint account with a spouse will not do. And it is a deposit, not an investment: the money sits, it does not work.

## What you need to prove

 Age 55 or over — by passport

 Income from USD 3,000 per month

 A three-month bank statement showing at least USD 2,000, in your own name

 A passport valid for at least 6 months

 A photo, a short CV and your travel itinerary

 A commitment to place the USD 50,000 deposit

 Health insurance and a housing lease are not required — they are asked for out of habit, left over from the old retirement regime under index C319, long since abolished.

## Worth knowing in advance

 The programme is new and small. The Golden Visa launched in July 2024, and just over a thousand visas have been issued across all its categories since. Silver Hair within that is a handful of people, so airports and smaller immigration offices may simply not know it.

 Savings are not income. Immigration looks at regular inflows, not at your balance. A large lump sum does not satisfy the income requirement.

 Joint accounts with a spouse are not accepted. Both the statement and the deposit must be in your name.

 Tax residency. Living here more than 183 days in any 12 months makes you an Indonesian tax resident, with everything that follows. More below.

## Tax: the part nobody mentions

 Almost no visa agency writes about this, and for a retiree it is the central question — it concerns their main income.

 The rule is simple: a foreigner becomes an Indonesian tax resident by living here or by spending more than 183 days in any 12 months. The days need not be consecutive. A tax resident must register, obtain an NPWP and file a return, and in the general case worldwide income is declared, not just Indonesian income. Rates are progressive, up to 35%.

 How strictly this is enforced is a separate matter and people's experience varies. But cases where the tax office found foreign accounts through international data exchange are on record. Plan this part with a tax adviser, taking your country's double taxation treaty into account.

## Who it fits, and who it does not

 A good fitYou are 55 or over, have regular income from USD 3,000, and can comfortably park USD 50,000 for five years without touching it. You want to live here long-term and not depend on an agency.

 Not a fitThe money needs to stay working, or that sum is your entire reserve. Then the annual E33F is more practical: no deposit, and we act as your sponsor.

 Worth comparingIf you are not yet 55, there is Second Home E33 — also five years and with no age limit, but the deposit there is USD 130,000.

Pricing is quoted individually — it depends on your nationality, timing and circumstances. Message us on WhatsApp or Telegram and we will send an exact quote within the hour.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: From what age is Silver Hair available?
From 55. That is written directly into the 2025 ministerial decree on visa classification. Many sites say 60 — that is wrong: the 60 threshold applies not to the visa but to converting into permanent KITAP on the retirement track.

Вопрос: Can property replace the deposit?
Not for Silver Hair — this route specifies a bank deposit. The property option exists on Second Home E33, but the threshold there is different.

Вопрос: Can I work on this status?
Selling goods or services directly inside Indonesia is prohibited. The law does formally allow other activity through a separate notification to immigration about combining activities, but on the retirement track practically nobody goes through it. If you plan to earn, look at the E33G or the investor E28A.

Вопрос: What about my spouse?
The law allows a status holder to bring family — the spouse is issued under a separate dependent code, not the retirement one. The spouse's age does not matter. One important detail: the income requirement is counted per person, not per couple. It is a non-standard case, so we work through it in a consultation.

Вопрос: What happens after five years?
The status is extended for another five, up to ten years in total. After that a move to KITAP — permanent residence — becomes possible; on the retirement track that opens at 60.

## Extending the visa

 A C1 visa can be extended twice, 60 days each — up to 180 days in the country without leaving, after which you must exit. Extensions are paid separately; start the process no later than 14 business days before your current visa expires.

Вопрос: What documents does an extension need?

 If you arranged the visa yourself, we'll need:

 A full passport-spread photo

 A personal photo

 Your ITK or the entry sticker in your passport

 Marital status

 E-mail and a WhatsApp or Telegram contact

 If we issued your visa, your data is already in our system — just message us a photo of the passport sticker, or your entry date if you used the e-gates, and we'll pull up the record and start the extension.

 Note: if the passport or entry stamp is damaged (torn, water-damaged, etc.), immigration may refuse the extension — success can't be guaranteed in such cases.

Вопрос: How do I start an extension?

 Just write to us. Send a photo of your passport sticker — or your entry date if you passed through the automatic gates — and we'll locate your entry record, load it into your account and create the extension.

Вопрос: How much does an extension cost?

 2,500,000 IDR — Minimal package, 10 business days

Вопрос: Can the extension be expedited?

 Yes. The standard process takes about two weeks; expedited — 5 to 7 business days. It's a paid service, and the final timing depends on the stage at which you request it and the specifics of the extension.

Вопрос: Is biometrics required?

 Yes — biometric submission is currently mandatory per Immigration Office requirements.

## Frequently asked questions

Вопрос: How is a business visa different from a tourist one?

 The difference is the purpose of the trip and what you may do. A tourist visa covers holidays, travel and personal visits; a business visa covers meetings and negotiations.

 Note: neither visa grants the right to work or earn income in Indonesia.

Вопрос: Can I get a tourist visa after a business visa?

 Yes. Switching visa types is straightforward and usually raises no questions at entry.

Вопрос: Which cities does the visa cover?

 The C1 e-Visa isn't tied to a city — you can enter through any international airport in Indonesia that accepts foreign nationals.

Вопрос: Can minors travel on their own?

 Yes, with a notarized parental or guardian consent translated into English. Also check the airline's rules in advance — many won't board an unaccompanied minor.

Вопрос: Why does the choice of agency matter?

 When you apply through an agency, a sponsor is assigned to you — all matters of your stay run through them. Changing sponsors is possible but slow and laborious.

 The agency's quality determines correct paperwork, met deadlines and support at every stage, extensions included. Mistakes turn into delays, extra costs and immigration complications — so pick a reliable partner from the start.

Вопрос: Why shouldn't I buy tickets before the visa is issued?

 Visas are issued by Indonesian Immigration, and timing depends on their internal processes — delays happen and can't be influenced. It's safer to book flights after the visa is in hand.

Вопрос: Tickets are bought but the visa isn't ready — what now?

 You can enter on a Visa on Arrival (VOA). Once the C1 is ready, you'll need to fly out and re-enter on the long-stay visa.

Вопрос: What is overstay and what does it cost?

 Overstay means remaining in the country past your visa's limit. Indonesia enforces this strictly: the fine is 1,000,000 IDR per day. Up to 60 days it's paid at the airport on departure; beyond that, additional immigration measures are possible — seek advice early.
